templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish habitual routine (present simple) from action-in-progress-now (present continuous)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner applies the habitual present simple to an action visibly in progress at the moment of speaking
templates.reasoningOperation: identify time-frame marker -> select aspect
templates.stem: Look! The chef ___ a new dish right now — you can smell it.

distractors.misconception: habitual-aspect overgeneralization
distractors.whyFails: 'Prepares' states a routine or general habit, which clashes with a dish being made at this very moment.
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang rutinitas, padahal masakannya lagi dibikin saat itu.
distractors.misconceptionId: kebiasaan dipakai buat kejadian yang lagi jalan.

distractors.misconception: confusing in-progress with completed result
distractors.whyFails: 'Has prepared' announces a finished dish, but 'right now — you can smell it' shows the cooking is still in progress.
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang masakannya udah jadi, padahal masih dibikin.
distractors.misconceptionId: yang lagi jalan ketuker sama yang udah selesai.

distractors.misconception: missing subject-verb agreement / bare form
distractors.whyFails: Third-person singular subject requires an -s or auxiliary form, not the bare infinitive.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar nggak cocok sama subjek orang ketiga tunggal.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar nggak disesuaikan sama subjeknya.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Look!' plus 'right now — you can smell it' points at an activity visibly unfolding this moment, so present continuous 'is preparing' is required.
explanation.rule: Present continuous = am/is/are + verb-ing, used for actions happening at the moment of speaking.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Present simple would describe a routine; present perfect would describe a finished action; the bare form is ungrammatical here.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is this a repeated habit, or something happening right in front of me?
explanation.memoryCue: 'Look!' = look at the -ing.
explanation.ruleId: Kejadian yang lagi jalan pakai am, is, atau are + kata kerja -ing. Kebiasaan yang berulang pakai bentuk sekarang biasa.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Look!” dan “right now — you can smell it” nunjuk kejadian yang lagi jalan. Jadi “is preparing” yang pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Present simple bilang kebiasaan, present perfect bilang udah selesai. Bentuk dasar “prepare” nggak cocok sama subjeknya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: ini kebiasaan yang berulang, atau kejadian di depan mata?
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada “Look!”, berarti lihat bentuk -ing-nya.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bedain kebiasaan yang berulang dari kejadian yang lagi jalan sekarang. Pilih present simple atau present continuous.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai present simple yang buat kebiasaan, padahal kejadiannya lagi jalan di depan mata.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari kata kunci waktunya → tentuin bentuk kata kerjanya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Choose past simple for a finished action with a specific past time reference vs present perfect for unspecified/relevant-to-now past
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner assumes present perfect always means 'ongoing' rather than 'unspecified time with present relevance'
templates.reasoningOperation: detect explicit time anchor -> select tense
templates.stem: She ___ to Lisbon exactly once, in 2019, before the pandemic changed everything.

distractors.misconception: present-perfect-for-any-past-event
distractors.whyFails: The specific year '2019' anchors the action to a finished point in the past, which blocks present perfect in standard usage.
distractors.whyFailsId: tahun “2019” maku kejadiannya di titik lampau yang udah kelar.
distractors.misconceptionId: present perfect dipakai buat sembarang kejadian lampau.

distractors.misconception: aspect confusion (progressive for a single completed trip)
distractors.whyFails: Past continuous frames an ongoing background action, not a completed single event.
distractors.whyFailsId: past continuous bikin latar yang lagi jalan, padahal perjalanannya udah kelar.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk yang lagi jalan dipakai buat perjalanan yang udah kelar.

distractors.misconception: tense-timeline mismatch
distractors.whyFails: Present simple cannot refer to a dated past event.
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple nggak bisa nyebut kejadian lampau yang tanggalnya jelas.
distractors.misconceptionId: garis waktu kalimatnya nggak cocok sama bentuk kata kerjanya.

explanation.whyCorrect: A specific past date ('2019') requires past simple, not present perfect.
explanation.rule: Present perfect is blocked by definite past time expressions (yesterday, in 2019, last week).
explanation.whyOthersFail: Present perfect ties the event to the present without a fixed date; past continuous suggests interruption or duration, not fact statement; present simple is timeless/habitual.
explanation.howToAvoid: If you can attach a specific calendar date to it, use past simple.
explanation.memoryCue: A dated past = past simple, not perfect.
explanation.ruleId: Present perfect nggak bisa jalan bareng keterangan waktu lampau yang pasti. Contohnya “yesterday”, “in 2019”, atau “last week”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “in 2019” itu rentang yang udah tutup, jadi past simple yang dipakai, bukan present perfect.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Present perfect ngiket kejadian ke sekarang tanpa tanggal pasti. Past continuous bunyinya kayak latar yang lagi jalan. Present simple bilang hal yang nggak keiket waktu.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau kejadiannya bisa ditempelin tanggal di kalender, pakai past simple.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada tanggal pasti, berarti past simple.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pilih past simple buat kejadian yang waktunya disebut jelas. Pakai present perfect kalau waktunya nggak disebut tapi efeknya masih kebawa sekarang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira present perfect selalu berarti masih jalan sekarang. Padahal maknanya lampau tanpa waktu pasti yang masih nyambung ke sekarang.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temukan tanggal atau tahun yang pasti di kalimatnya → pilih past simple, bukan present perfect

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Differentiate a pre-arranged plan (present continuous / going to) from a spontaneous decision (will)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats a spontaneous offer made at the moment of speaking as a pre-arranged plan, reaching for present continuous instead of 'will'
templates.reasoningOperation: detect prior arrangement vs on-the-spot decision -> select future form
templates.stem: Which completion shows a decision made only at the moment of speaking? A: 'The phone's ringing.' B: 'Don't worry, I ___ it.'

distractors.misconception: treats spontaneous offers as pre-arranged plans
distractors.whyFails: Present continuous frames the response as an arrangement already in place or an action already under way, not a decision made only at the moment of speaking, which is what the question asks to show.
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang rencananya udah diatur atau udah jalan, bukan keputusan pas ngomong.
distractors.misconceptionId: tawaran mendadak dianggap rencana yang udah diatur.

distractors.misconception: present simple used for a one-off future act
distractors.whyFails: Present simple is for routines/schedules, not spontaneous offers.
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple buat kebiasaan dan jadwal, bukan tawaran mendadak.
distractors.misconceptionId: present simple dipakai buat satu tindakan mendadak nanti.

distractors.misconception: structural error: double -ing after 'going to'
distractors.whyFails: 'Going to' takes the base verb, not another -ing form.
distractors.whyFailsId: setelah “going to” wajib nyusul kata kerja bentuk dasar.
distractors.misconceptionId: dua kali bentuk -ing setelah “going to”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Will' expresses a decision made at the moment of speaking, such as an offer.
explanation.rule: Use 'will' for spontaneous decisions/offers; use present continuous or 'going to' for pre-arranged plans or intentions formed earlier.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Present continuous requires the plan to already exist; present simple is for facts/schedules; the last option is ungrammatical.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: was this decided before this exact moment, or right now?
explanation.memoryCue: Instant decision = instant 'will'.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai “will” buat keputusan mendadak dan tawaran bantuan. Pakai present continuous atau “going to” buat rencana yang udah disusun lebih dulu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Will” dipakai buat keputusan yang baru diambil pas ngomong, misalnya nawarin bantuan.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Present continuous nuntut rencananya udah ada dari sebelumnya. Present simple buat fakta dan jadwal. Pilihan terakhir bentuknya nggak sah.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: ini diputusin sebelum percakapan, atau baru kepikiran pas ngomong?
explanation.memoryCueId: Keputusan yang seketika, pakai “will” seketika.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bedain rencana yang udah diatur dari keputusan yang baru muncul pas kamu ngomong.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nganggep tawaran yang baru muncul pas ngomong sebagai rencana yang udah diatur, jadi milih present continuous, bukan “will”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek udah direncanain dari tadi atau baru diputusin pas ngomong → pilih bentuk masa depannya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish external obligation (have to/must) from granted permission (can/may)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats all modals as interchangeable politeness markers
templates.reasoningOperation: identify whose authority is being expressed -> select modal
templates.stem: Visitors ___ leave their bags at the front desk; it's a museum rule, not a choice.

distractors.misconception: obligation read as ability/permission
distractors.whyFails: 'Can' expresses that something is allowed, not that it is required by a rule.
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang sesuatu diperbolehkan, bukan diwajibkan aturan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kewajiban dibaca sebagai kemampuan atau izin.

distractors.misconception: obligation read as formal permission
distractors.whyFails: 'May' grants permission; it does not impose a requirement.
distractors.whyFailsId: ngasih izin, nggak nuntut keharusan apa pun.
distractors.misconceptionId: kewajiban dibaca sebagai izin dalam bahasa formal.

distractors.misconception: obligation read as a polite hypothetical
distractors.whyFails: 'Could' softens a request or suggests possibility, not a firm rule.
distractors.whyFailsId: memperhalus permintaan atau nyebut kemungkinan saja.
distractors.misconceptionId: kewajiban dibaca sebagai pengandaian yang sopan.

explanation.whyCorrect: The stem explicitly states 'it's a rule, not a choice,' which signals obligation.
explanation.rule: 'Must'/'have to' express obligation; 'can'/'may'/'could' express permission or possibility.
explanation.whyOthersFail: None of the alternatives carry the sense of a mandatory rule enforced by an outside authority.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look for context clues like 'rule,' 'required,' or 'not optional' to identify obligation.
explanation.memoryCue: Rule = must.
explanation.ruleId: “Must” dan “have to” bilang wajib. “Can”, “may”, dan “could” bilang boleh atau mungkin.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kalimatnya bilang sendiri ini aturan museum, bukan pilihan. Itu ciri kewajiban.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Pilihan lain cuma bilang boleh atau mungkin. Nggak ada yang bilang ini wajib.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cari kata kunci kayak “rule”, “required”, atau “not optional” buat nemuin kewajiban.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kalau ini aturan, pakai “must”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bedain kewajiban yang datang dari aturan sama izin yang dikasih orang. Kata kayak must, can, dan may punya tugas beda.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira must, can, dan may cuma soal sopan, jadi bisa gantian.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek siapa yang punya wewenang di kalimat → pilih kata kayak must atau can

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'must' for confident logical deduction vs 'might/could' for uncertain speculation
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'must' for any guess, not reserving it for strong evidence-based conclusions
templates.reasoningOperation: spot a present-time deduction -> weigh how strong the visible evidence is -> pick must for near-certainty or can't for impossibility
templates.stem: Which option expresses the strongest negative deduction supported by the evidence? The lights are off and the car isn't in the driveway, so they ___ be home.

distractors.misconception: negative obligation confused with negative deduction
distractors.whyFails: 'Mustn't' expresses prohibition ('not allowed to'), not a deduction that something is impossible.
distractors.whyFailsId: artinya nggak boleh dilakuin, bukan kesimpulan kalau sesuatu mustahil.
distractors.misconceptionId: larangan ketuker sama kesimpulan yang negatif.

distractors.misconception: underestimates the strength of the evidence
distractors.whyFails: The evidence (dark house, no car) is strong enough for confident deduction, not weak possibility.
distractors.whyFailsId: buktinya kelewat kuat buat dugaan yang selemah ini.
distractors.misconceptionId: kekuatan bukti yang keliatan dinilai kelewat rendah.

distractors.misconception: deduction confused with expectation/advice
distractors.whyFails: 'Shouldn't' expresses what is expected or advisable, not a logical conclusion from evidence.
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang apa yang sebaiknya, bukan kesimpulan dari bukti.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesimpulan ketuker sama harapan atau saran.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Can't' expresses a confident negative deduction from strong evidence.
explanation.rule: For confident negative deduction, use 'can't' (not 'mustn't', which means prohibition).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Mustn't' = forbidden; 'might not' = weak possibility; 'shouldn't' = advice/expectation, none matching confident deduction.
explanation.howToAvoid: For deduction, positive certainty = 'must', negative certainty = 'can't' (never 'mustn't').
explanation.memoryCue: Certain it's NOT true = can't, never mustn't.
explanation.ruleId: Buat kesimpulan negatif yang kamu yakin, pakai “can’t”, bukan “mustn’t” yang artinya larangan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Can’t” bilang kesimpulan negatif yang kamu yakin banget dari bukti yang ada.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Mustn’t” artinya dilarang, “might not” cuma kemungkinan lemah, “shouldn’t” itu saran. Nggak ada yang pas buat kesimpulan yang yakin.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Yakin itu bener, pakai “must”. Yakin nggak mungkin, pakai “can’t”, jangan “mustn’t”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Yakin nggak mungkin: pakai “can’t”, bukan “mustn’t”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “must” buat kesimpulan yang kamu yakin banget. Pakai “might” atau “could” buat dugaan yang masih ragu.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “must” buat sembarang tebakan. Padahal kata itu buat kesimpulan yang buktinya kuat.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali ini simpulan soal keadaan sekarang → timbang kekuatan buktinya → pilih kata bantu yang kekuatannya pas

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish general/scientific truth (zero conditional) from a specific likely future result (first conditional)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'will' in the if-clause for general truths
templates.reasoningOperation: identify generality vs specific-future prediction -> select conditional type
templates.stem: Which completion states this as a general fact that is always true, not a prediction about one occasion? If you heat ice, it ___.

distractors.misconception: general truth treated as a one-time prediction
distractors.whyFails: This is correct English, but 'will' frames it as a prediction about a particular occasion; the question asks for the always-true general fact.
distractors.whyFailsId: bahasanya bener, tapi ini ramalan satu kejadian.
distractors.misconceptionId: fakta yang selalu bener diperlakukan kayak ramalan sekali kejadian.

distractors.misconception: real condition treated as hypothetical
distractors.whyFails: 'Would' signals an unreal/hypothetical condition, but heating ice always causes melting — it's real and general.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” buat keadaan yang nggak nyata, padahal es memang mencair.
distractors.misconceptionId: syarat nyata diperlakukan kayak pengandaian.

distractors.misconception: past tense used for a timeless fact
distractors.whyFails: Zero conditional describes a general truth in present tense, not a completed past event.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk lampau bikin fakta itu kayak udah lewat.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lampau dipakai buat fakta yang nggak terikat waktu.

explanation.whyCorrect: Zero conditional (if + present, present) states a general, always-true cause-effect relationship.
explanation.rule: Zero conditional: If + present simple, present simple — for facts and general truths.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Will' fits a specific future scenario (first conditional); 'would' fits an unreal scenario (second conditional); past tense misrepresents a timeless fact.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is this true every single time, or just predicted for one situation?
explanation.memoryCue: Always true = present + present.
explanation.ruleId: Zero conditional: if + present simple, terus present simple lagi. Rumus ini buat fakta yang selalu bener.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Es dipanasin memang selalu mencair, bukan cuma sekali. Fakta kayak gini pakai present simple dua-duanya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Will” buat satu kejadian nanti, “would” buat keadaan yang nggak nyata. Bentuk lampau bikin fakta itu kayak udah lewat.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: ini bener setiap kali, atau cuma ramalan satu keadaan?
explanation.memoryCueId: Selalu bener? Present ketemu present.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bedain fakta yang selalu bener dari ramalan buat satu kejadian. Pilih zero conditional atau first conditional.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “will” di bagian if buat nyatain fakta yang selalu bener.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek ini berlaku selalu atau cuma satu kejadian → pilih rumus if-nya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use second conditional to express a hypothetical/unreal present situation, not a likely future one
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner picks first conditional for any 'if' sentence about winning money, ignoring the unreal/imaginary framing
templates.reasoningOperation: detect improbability/hypothetical framing -> select second conditional
templates.stem: If I ___ the lottery, I would travel the world — but let's be honest, it's not going to happen.

distractors.misconception: if-clause verb form mismatched with 'would' in the main clause
distractors.whyFails: First-conditional 'if + present' should not pair with 'would' in the result clause.
distractors.whyFailsId: pola “if + present” itu nggak dipasangin sama “would” di hasilnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk anak kalimat if nggak sejalan sama “would” di induk kalimat.

distractors.misconception: duplicating 'would' in both clauses
distractors.whyFails: Standard conditionals put 'would' only in the result clause, not the if-clause.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” cuma berdiri di anak kalimat hasil, bukan di bagian if.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would” dipakai di dua anak kalimat sekaligus.

distractors.misconception: real/likely framing applied to an admittedly unlikely event
distractors.whyFails: The speaker explicitly signals this is not going to happen, which calls for the unreal second conditional, not 'will'.
distractors.whyFailsId: pembicaranya sendiri bilang hal itu nggak akan kejadian.
distractors.misconceptionId: kejadian yang diakui mustahil diperlakukan kayak kemungkinan nyata.

explanation.whyCorrect: Second conditional (if + past simple, would + base verb) expresses a hypothetical, unlikely present/future situation.
explanation.rule: Second conditional: If + past simple, ... would + base verb — for imaginary or improbable situations.
explanation.whyOthersFail: First-conditional forms mismatch the 'would' result clause; doubling 'would' is a structural error.
explanation.howToAvoid: If the speaker signals the situation is unreal or unlikely, use past simple in the if-clause even though the meaning is present/future.
explanation.memoryCue: Unreal now = past form, but not past meaning.
explanation.ruleId: Second conditional: if + past simple, terus would + kata kerja dasar. Bentuk ini buat keadaan yang cuma dibayangin atau kecil banget kemungkinannya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kalimatnya sendiri bilang menang lotre itu nggak akan kejadian. Keadaan kayak gini pakai past simple di anak kalimat if.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Bentuk first conditional nggak sejalan sama “would” di anak kalimat hasil. Pakai “would” dua kali bikin susunannya salah.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau pembicaranya nandain keadaannya nggak nyata, pakai past simple di anak kalimat if.
explanation.memoryCueId: Nggak nyata sekarang: bentuknya lampau, maknanya bukan lampau.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai second conditional buat keadaan sekarang yang nggak nyata. Bukan buat masa depan yang wajar kejadian.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pilih first conditional buat semua kalimat if. Padahal kalimatnya sendiri bilang hal itu nggak akan kejadian.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari tanda kalau keadaannya nggak nyata → pilih second conditional

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Recognize when passive voice is preferred because the agent is unknown or unimportant
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner keeps 'by + agent' even when the actor is irrelevant, producing an unnatural sentence
templates.reasoningOperation: assess relevance of the agent to the message -> choose passive with or without 'by'
templates.stem: Which completion most explicitly leaves the unknown builder out of the sentence? The bridge ___ in 1932; nobody today remembers who built it.

distractors.misconception: active voice used despite an unknown/irrelevant agent
distractors.whyFails: Using active voice would require naming a subject/agent, but the context states the builder is unknown.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimat aktif nuntut pelaku yang disebut, padahal pembangunnya nggak diketahui.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimat aktif dipakai padahal pelakunya nggak diketahui.

distractors.misconception: malformed passive/perfect blend
distractors.whyFails: This is not a valid English verb form.
distractors.whyFailsId: susunan ini bukan bentuk kata kerja yang sah.
distractors.misconceptionId: campuran pasif dan perfect yang bentuknya rusak.

distractors.misconception: adds a vague, uninformative agent instead of omitting it
distractors.whyFails: This is grammatically correct, but naming a generic agent ('workers') adds nothing; the question asks for the version that leaves the unknown builder out.
distractors.whyFailsId: bener tata bahasanya, tapi pelaku samar yang gini nggak nambah info.
distractors.misconceptionId: pelaku samar malah ditambahin, padahal mestinya dihilangin.

explanation.whyCorrect: Passive voice without a 'by' phrase is preferred when the agent is unknown or unimportant to the message.
explanation.rule: Passive = be + past participle; drop 'by + agent' when the doer is unknown, obvious, or irrelevant.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Active voice needs a known agent; the perfect-passive blend is ungrammatical; adding a vague agent contradicts the context.
explanation.howToAvoid: If the sentence explicitly says the agent is unknown, don't add one back in with 'by'.
explanation.memoryCue: Don't know who did it? Drop the 'by'.
explanation.ruleId: Kalimat pasif dibentuk dari be + bentuk ketiga kata kerja (past participle). Bagian “by + pelaku” dibuang kalau pelakunya nggak diketahui, udah jelas, atau nggak penting.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Pasif tanpa bagian “by” lebih pas kalau pelakunya nggak diketahui atau nggak penting.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Kalimat aktif nuntut pelaku yang jelas. Campuran perfect dan pasif bentuknya nggak sah. Nambah pelaku samar malah bentrok sama konteksnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau kalimatnya sendiri bilang pelakunya nggak diketahui, jangan masukin pelaku lagi lewat “by”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kalau nggak tahu siapa pelakunya, buang “by”-nya.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kenali kapan kalimat pasif lebih pas karena pelakunya nggak diketahui atau nggak penting.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu tetep nambahin “by + pelaku” walau pelakunya nggak penting. Kalimatnya jadi kedengeran janggal.
templates.reasoningOperationId: nilai pelakunya penting buat pesan kalimatnya atau nggak → pilih pasif pakai “by” atau tanpa “by”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Apply tense backshift when reporting a statement made in the past
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner copies the original tense verbatim into reported speech
templates.reasoningOperation: check the reporting verb's tense -> shift the reported statement's main verb one step back, e.g. present simple 'am' to past simple 'was'
templates.stem: Apply conventional backshift to report the earlier state: Yesterday she said, ‘I am tired.’ Today we report that she ___ tired.

distractors.misconception: no backshift applied
distractors.whyFails: Since the reporting verb 'said' is past, the reported present tense must shift back to past.
distractors.whyFailsId: laporannya netral dan keadaannya udah lewat, jadi bentuk presentnya mundur.
distractors.misconceptionId: pergeseran bentuk waktunya nggak dilakuin sama sekali.

distractors.misconception: backshift target confused with present perfect
distractors.whyFails: Present simple in direct speech backshifts to past simple, not present perfect.
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple mundurnya ke past simple, bukan ke present perfect.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sasaran gesernya ketuker sama present perfect.

distractors.misconception: tense category changed instead of shifted one step back
distractors.whyFails: This changes present into future rather than shifting it one step back into the past.
distractors.whyFailsId: ini malah maju ke masa depan, bukan mundur satu langkah.
distractors.misconceptionId: jenis bentuk waktunya ganti, bukan mundur satu langkah.

explanation.whyCorrect: Present simple ('am') backshifts to past simple ('was') when the reporting verb is past.
explanation.rule: Backshift is the conventional choice when the report is neutral or the situation no longer holds: present simple -> past simple; present continuous -> past continuous; present perfect -> past perfect.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Keeping the present tense ignores backshift; the other options shift to the wrong tense category.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check whether the reported content still holds; if it does not, move the original tense one step back on the timeline.
explanation.memoryCue: Neutral report? Step it back.
explanation.ruleId: Kalau laporannya netral atau isinya udah nggak berlaku, tense-nya biasanya mundur satu langkah: present simple jadi past simple, present continuous jadi past continuous, present perfect jadi past perfect.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kata pelapornya “said” dan keterangan “Yesterday” naruh laporannya di lampau, dan keadaannya udah lewat. Jadi “am” mundur jadi “was”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Di kalimat ini keadaannya udah lewat, jadi bentuk present berarti gesernya dilewatin. Pilihan lain geser ke jenis bentuk waktu yang keliru.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dulu isi laporannya masih berlaku atau nggak, terus geser bentuk waktunya satu langkah mundur.
explanation.memoryCueId: Laporan yang netral biasanya mundur satu langkah.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Geser bentuk waktu (tense) kata kerjanya waktu kamu ngelaporin ucapan yang diucapin di masa lalu.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nyalin bentuk waktu aslinya apa adanya ke kalimat pelaporan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat bentuk waktu kata kerja pelapornya → mundurin kata kerja utamanya satu langkah, misalnya “am” jadi “was”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use indefinite article for first mention and definite article for subsequent, already-identified mention
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reuses the indefinite article for a noun that has already been identified, treating every mention as a first mention
templates.reasoningOperation: track discourse identifiability -> select article
templates.stem: I saw a dog in the park. ___ dog was chasing a ball.

distractors.misconception: indefinite article reused for an already-identified noun
distractors.whyFails: 'A' introduces the dog as if it were brand-new information, even though the first sentence already made it identifiable.
distractors.whyFailsId: anjingnya udah disebut, jadi bukan info baru lagi.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata buat penyebutan pertama diulang di benda yang udah dikenal.

distractors.misconception: wrong article form regardless of identifiability (vowel-sound rule misapplied)
distractors.whyFails: 'Dog' starts with a consonant sound, so 'an' would be wrong even if an indefinite article were needed.
distractors.whyFailsId: bunyi awal “dog” itu konsonan, bukan vokal.
distractors.misconceptionId: aturan bunyi vokal dipakai di tempat yang salah.

distractors.misconception: quantifier substituted for a singular countable reference
distractors.whyFails: 'Some' is used with plurals/uncountables, not a specific singular dog already mentioned.
distractors.whyFailsId: “some” buat benda jamak, bukan satu anjing tertentu.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata jumlah dipakai buat satu benda tertentu.

explanation.whyCorrect: Once a noun has been mentioned, subsequent references use 'the' because both speaker and listener can identify it.
explanation.rule: Indefinite article (a/an) for first mention of a countable noun; definite article (the) once it is identifiable.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'A' and 'an' reintroduce the dog as if new; 'some' doesn't fit a specific singular noun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: has this exact noun already been introduced in the conversation?
explanation.memoryCue: New = a/an. Known = the.
explanation.ruleId: Kata a atau an dipakai waktu benda baru pertama kali muncul. “The” dipakai setelah pembaca udah tahu benda mana.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Anjingnya udah disebut di kalimat pertama. Jadi kamu dan pembaca sama-sama tahu anjing mana.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “A” dan “an” bikin anjingnya kayak baru muncul. “Some” nggak cocok buat satu benda tertentu.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: benda ini udah pernah diperkenalkan sebelumnya atau belum?
explanation.memoryCueId: Baru muncul pakai a atau an, udah dikenal pakai the.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai a atau an waktu benda baru disebut. Pakai the waktu bendanya udah dikenal.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngulang “a” buat benda yang udah disebut, seolah tiap penyebutan itu penyebutan pertama.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek bendanya udah dikenal pembaca atau belum → pilih a, an, atau the

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select the correct time preposition based on the specificity level (month/year vs day vs clock time)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner picks 'at' for any time expression regardless of specificity level
templates.reasoningOperation: classify time expression granularity -> select preposition
templates.stem: The meeting is ___ Monday morning.

distractors.misconception: day-level expression treated as a broad time period
distractors.whyFails: 'In' is used for months, years, and seasons, not specific days.
distractors.whyFailsId: dipakai buat bulan, tahun, dan musim, bukan hari.
distractors.misconceptionId: keterangan hari dianggap rentang waktu yang luas.

distractors.misconception: day-level expression treated as clock time
distractors.whyFails: 'At' is reserved for precise clock times (at 9am), not a day like Monday.
distractors.whyFailsId: cuma buat jam yang persis kayak at 9am.
distractors.misconceptionId: keterangan hari dianggap jam.

distractors.misconception: time preposition confused with deadline preposition
distractors.whyFails: 'By' means 'no later than', which changes the meaning rather than simply locating the event on a day.
distractors.whyFailsId: artinya paling lambat, jadi maknanya berubah.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan waktu tertukar sama kata depan batas akhir.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'On' is used with specific days, including parts of a specific day (Monday morning).
explanation.rule: in = months/years/seasons; on = days/dates; at = clock times/specific points.
explanation.whyOthersFail: The other prepositions belong to different specificity levels or change the meaning entirely.
explanation.howToAvoid: Match the noun's specificity level (year > day > clock time) to in/on/at respectively.
explanation.memoryCue: Days live ON a calendar page.
explanation.ruleId: in buat bulan, tahun, dan musim. on buat hari dan tanggal. at buat jam.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Monday morning itu hari tertentu. Hari pakai “on”, termasuk bagian harinya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Pilihan lain buat waktu yang lebih luas atau lebih sempit. Ada juga yang bikin maknanya berubah.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: ini bulan, hari, atau jam? Baru pilih kata depannya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Hari nempel di halaman kalender: on Monday.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Milih kata depan waktu sesuai luas waktunya: bulan, hari, atau jam
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang kepeleset pakai “at” buat semua keterangan waktu.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat dulu waktunya seluas apa → baru pilih kata depannya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Recognize that 'stop + gerund' (ending an activity) and 'stop + infinitive' (pausing to do something else) carry different meanings
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats gerund/infinitive after 'stop' as free variation rather than meaning-changing
templates.reasoningOperation: identify intended meaning -> select the pattern that encodes it
templates.stem: On the way home, she stopped ___ some bread because the bakery was still open.

distractors.misconception: gerund used where a purpose-infinitive is needed
distractors.whyFails: 'Stop buying' would mean she quit the habit of buying bread, which contradicts the context of a single errand.
distractors.whyFailsId: “stop buying” berarti dia berhenti dari kebiasaan beli roti, bukan satu kali mampir.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai padahal yang diminta bentuk to buat tujuan.

distractors.misconception: bare infinitive used instead of the required to-infinitive
distractors.whyFails: The purpose sense of 'stop' requires a to-infinitive, not a bare form.
distractors.whyFailsId: makna tujuan di “stop” minta bentuk pakai to, bukan bentuk dasar.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar dipakai padahal yang diminta bentuk to.

distractors.misconception: perfect gerund used where a simple purpose clause is needed
distractors.whyFails: This form implies a completed prior action rather than the purpose of stopping.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini bilang tindakannya udah kelar lebih dulu, bukan tujuan berhentinya.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing perfect dipakai padahal yang diminta anak kalimat tujuan biasa.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Stop to buy' means she paused her journey in order to buy bread — a purpose infinitive.
explanation.rule: stop + gerund = discontinue an activity; stop + to-infinitive = pause in order to do something else.
explanation.whyOthersFail: The gerund form reverses the intended meaning; the other options are structurally or semantically wrong.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is the activity itself being ended, or is it a new purpose interrupting something else?
explanation.memoryCue: Stop TO DO = pause for a purpose.
explanation.ruleId: “Stop” + bentuk -ing berarti kamu berhenti dari kegiatan itu. “Stop” + to + kata kerja berarti berhenti sebentar buat ngerjain hal lain.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Stop to buy” berarti dia berhenti sebentar buat beli roti, jadi bentuk to-nya nyatain tujuan.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Bentuk -ing malah bikin maknanya kebalik. Pilihan lain salah susunan atau salah makna.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: kegiatannya yang diberhentiin, atau ada tujuan baru yang nyela?
explanation.memoryCueId: “Stop to do” berarti berhenti demi satu tujuan.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu bedain “stop” + gerund (bentuk -ing) dari “stop” + bentuk to. Maknanya beda jauh.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nganggep bentuk -ing dan bentuk to sesudah “stop” bisa gantian, padahal maknanya beda.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin makna yang kamu maksud → pilih pola yang bawa makna itu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish a defining relative clause (essential, no commas) from a non-defining one (extra info, commas)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner adds commas around identifying information, obscuring which noun is meant
templates.reasoningOperation: assess whether the clause is essential for identifying the noun -> punctuate/select accordingly
templates.stem: Choose the sentence where the relative clause is ESSENTIAL to know which brother is meant:
options: My brother, who lives in Rome, called me yesterday.
The brother who lives in Rome called me yesterday (I have three brothers).
My only brother, who is a doctor, called me.
My brother, who I love dearly, called me.

distractors.option: My brother, who lives in Rome, called me yesterday.
distractors.misconception: assumes any relative clause about a sibling is essential
distractors.whyFails: Commas here mark it as extra, non-identifying detail, implying the speaker has only one brother already clear from context.
distractors.whyFailsId: koma di sini nandain keterangan tambahan buat penutur yang saudaranya cuma satu.
distractors.misconceptionId: setiap anak kalimat soal saudara dianggap wajib.

distractors.option: My only brother, who is a doctor, called me.
distractors.misconception: ignores that 'only' already uniquely identifies the noun
distractors.whyFails: 'Only brother' is already unique, so the clause adds extra info, not identification — hence commas are correct there, not essential.
distractors.whyFailsId: “only brother” udah nunjuk satu orang, jadi komanya di situ malah bener.
distractors.misconceptionId: lupa kalau kata “only” udah nunjuk satu orang aja.

distractors.option: My brother, who I love dearly, called me.
distractors.misconception: confuses emotional/extra detail with identifying detail
distractors.whyFails: This clause adds feeling, not identification, so it is non-defining.
distractors.whyFailsId: anak kalimat ini nambah perasaan, bukan nunjuk saudara yang mana.
distractors.misconceptionId: keterangan perasaan ketuker sama keterangan yang ngenalin bendanya.

explanation.whyCorrect: With three brothers, only the relative clause tells us which one — it is essential and takes no commas.
explanation.rule: Defining relative clauses (essential, no commas) identify which noun is meant; non-defining clauses (commas) add extra, non-essential information.
explanation.whyOthersFail: In the other sentences, the noun is already uniquely identified by context or possessive, so the relative clause is extra detail rather than identification.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: if I delete the clause, is it still clear which specific person/thing is meant?
explanation.memoryCue: Can't identify without it? No commas.
explanation.ruleId: Anak kalimat yang wajib nunjuk benda mana yang dimaksud ditulis tanpa koma. Anak kalimat yang cuma nambah keterangan ditulis di antara koma.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Saudara laki-lakinya ada tiga, jadi cuma anak kalimat itu yang nunjuk saudara yang mana. Keterangan itu wajib, jadi tanpa koma.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Di kalimat lain orangnya udah tertunjuk jelas sama kata milik atau konteksnya. Anak kalimatnya jadi cuma nambah keterangan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya, ya: kalau anak kalimat itu dihapus, masih jelas benda mana yang dimaksud?
explanation.memoryCueId: Nggak bisa dikenali tanpa keterangan itu? Berarti tanpa koma.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu bedain relative clause (anak kalimat penjelas) yang wajib dari yang cuma nambah keterangan. Yang wajib ditulis tanpa koma.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh koma di sekitar keterangan yang justru dipakai buat ngenalin bendanya. Jadi nggak jelas benda mana yang dimaksud.
templates.reasoningOperationId: nilai apakah anak kalimatnya wajib buat ngenalin bendanya → tentuin pakai koma atau nggak

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use comparative for a two-item comparison and superlative for a three-or-more group comparison
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses superlative forms even when comparing only two items
templates.reasoningOperation: count items being compared -> select comparative or superlative form
templates.stem: Between these two routes, the coastal road is ___ than the mountain pass.

distractors.misconception: superlative used for a two-item comparison
distractors.whyFails: Superlatives compare three or more items; here only two routes are being compared.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk “paling” nunjuk juara kelompok, di sini cuma dua jalur.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk “paling” dipakai buat perbandingan dua hal.

distractors.misconception: base adjective used without comparative marking
distractors.whyFails: 'Scenic' leaves the adjective unmarked, so the 'than' comparison has nothing to hang on.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata sifatnya polos, “than” jadi nggak punya pijakan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata sifat dasar dipakai tanpa kata kunci perbandingan.

distractors.misconception: superlative used without 'the', still wrong scope
distractors.whyFails: Besides missing 'the', a superlative is still the wrong category for a two-item comparison.
distractors.whyFailsId: “the” hilang, dan bentuk “paling” tetap salah cakupan.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk “paling” tanpa “the”, cakupannya juga tetap keliru.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'More scenic ... than' correctly compares exactly two things.
explanation.rule: Comparative (+ than) for two items; superlative (the + -est/most) for three or more.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Superlative forms misrepresent a two-item comparison as a group comparison; the base adjective lacks any comparison marker.
explanation.howToAvoid: Count what's being compared: exactly two = comparative; a group = superlative.
explanation.memoryCue: Two = -ER/more. Group = -EST/most.
explanation.ruleId: Bentuk “lebih” (comparative) jalan bareng “than” buat mbandingin dua hal. Bentuk “paling” (superlative) pakai the plus -est atau most buat nunjuk juara satu kelompok.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Susunan “more scenic ... than” mbandingin tepat dua jalur. Itu memang tugas bentuk “lebih” (comparative).
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Bentuk “paling” bikin dua jalur ini kayak satu kelompok besar. Kata sifat polos malah nggak bawa arti mbandingin.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hitung dulu, ya: tepat dua hal, atau satu kelompok yang dicari juaranya?
explanation.memoryCueId: Dua hal pakai -er atau more. Satu kelompok pakai -est atau most.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai bentuk “lebih” (comparative) buat mbandingin dua hal. Pakai bentuk “paling” (superlative) buat nunjuk juara satu kelompok.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai bentuk “paling” padahal yang dibandingin cuma dua hal.
templates.reasoningOperationId: hitung ada berapa hal yang dibandingin → pilih bentuk “lebih” atau bentuk “paling”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Form a question tag with reversed polarity matching the main clause's auxiliary
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner matches tag polarity to the main clause instead of reversing it
templates.reasoningOperation: identify main clause polarity and auxiliary -> generate reversed tag
templates.stem: You haven't finished the report yet, ___?

distractors.misconception: tag polarity copied instead of reversed
distractors.whyFails: The main clause is already negative, so the tag must be positive, not also negative.
distractors.whyFailsId: di kalimat ini induknya udah negatif, jadi ekor negatif lagi nggak pas.
distractors.misconceptionId: positif-negatif ekornya disalin, bukan dibalik.

distractors.misconception: wrong auxiliary borrowed from a different tense
distractors.whyFails: The main clause uses present perfect ('haven't'), so the tag must use 'have', not 'did'.
distractors.whyFailsId: induk kalimatnya pakai present perfect, jadi kata bantunya nggak nyambung.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantunya diambil dari bentuk waktu yang beda.

distractors.misconception: wrong auxiliary substituted (present simple instead of present perfect)
distractors.whyFails: The auxiliary in the tag must match the auxiliary in the statement, which is 'have', not 'do'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata bantu di ekornya wajib sama kayak yang di pernyataannya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantunya diganti punya present simple.

explanation.whyCorrect: A negative statement takes a positive tag using the same auxiliary as the main clause.
explanation.rule: A question tag normally reverses the polarity of the main clause and repeats its auxiliary; a same-polarity tag is a separate agreement or surprise pattern.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Same-polarity and mismatched-auxiliary tags both break the tag-question rule.
explanation.howToAvoid: Copy the auxiliary from the main clause, then flip positive/negative.
explanation.memoryCue: Negative statement, positive tag.
explanation.ruleId: Ekor pertanyaan biasanya ngebalik positif-negatif induk kalimatnya dan ngulang kata bantu yang sama. Ekor yang positif-negatifnya sama kepakai buat nunjukin kesetujuan atau kaget, kayak “So you are coming, are you?”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “haven’t” di induk kalimatnya negatif dan kata bantunya “have”. Jadi ekornya positif dan tetep pakai “have”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Ekor yang positif-negatifnya sama nggak pas di kalimat ini karena induknya udah negatif. Ekor yang kata bantunya beda juga nggak nyambung.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Salin kata bantu dari induk kalimatnya, terus balik positif-negatifnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Kalimat negatif biasanya dapet ekor positif.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Susun ekor pertanyaan (question tag) dengan positif-negatif yang dibalik dan kata bantu yang sama.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nyamain positif-negatif ekornya sama induk kalimatnya. Padahal bagian itu harus dibalik.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kata bantu dan positif-negatif induk kalimatnya → balik positif-negatifnya di ekornya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Identify that the verb must agree with the true grammatical subject, not a nearby noun in an intervening phrase
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner makes the verb agree with the closest noun rather than the actual subject
templates.reasoningOperation: locate true subject past the intervening prepositional phrase -> check agreement
templates.stem: Find and correct the error: 'The list of requirements are posted on the noticeboard.'
options: The list of requirements is posted on the noticeboard.
The list of requirements were posted on the noticeboard.
The lists of requirements are posted on the noticeboard.
The list of requirements are post on the noticeboard.

distractors.option: The list of requirements were posted on the noticeboard.
distractors.misconception: keeps plural agreement, just changes tense, missing the real error
distractors.whyFails: This still agrees with 'requirements' (plural) instead of 'list' (the true singular subject).
distractors.whyFailsId: masih nyocok sama “requirements” yang jamak, bukan sama subjek tunggalnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kecocokan jamak dipertahanin, yang diubah cuma bentuk waktunya.

distractors.option: The lists of requirements are posted on the noticeboard.
distractors.misconception: changes the subject to match the verb instead of fixing the verb
distractors.whyFails: This alters the original meaning (multiple lists) rather than correcting the agreement error.
distractors.whyFailsId: makna aslinya jadi banyak daftar, kesalahan kecocokannya nggak dibenerin.
distractors.misconceptionId: subjeknya yang diubah biar cocok, bukan kata kerjanya yang dibenerin.

distractors.option: The list of requirements are post on the noticeboard.
distractors.misconception: introduces a new verb-form error while keeping the agreement error
distractors.whyFails: This still has the agreement problem and adds an incorrect bare verb form.
distractors.whyFailsId: kecocokannya masih salah dan bentuk kata kerjanya malah ngaco.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambah kesalahan bentuk kata kerja sambil ninggalin kesalahan kecocokannya.

explanation.whyCorrect: The grammatical subject is 'list' (singular), so the verb must be 'is', regardless of the plural noun 'requirements' inside the prepositional phrase.
explanation.rule: The verb agrees with the head noun of the subject, not with a noun inside a modifying prepositional phrase.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Each alternative either preserves the agreement error or fixes it by distorting the original meaning.
explanation.howToAvoid: Mentally delete the prepositional phrase ('of requirements') and check agreement with what remains.
explanation.memoryCue: Cross out 'of ___' to find the real subject.
explanation.ruleId: Kata kerja nyocokin diri sama kata benda inti di subjeknya. Frasa kata depan yang nyempil nggak ikut dihitung.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Subjeknya “list” yang tunggal, jadi kata kerjanya “is”. Kata jamak “requirements” cuma nempel di frasa kata depan.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Pilihan lain masih ninggalin kesalahan kecocokannya. Ada juga yang benerin dengan cara ngubah makna aslinya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Coret dulu, ya, frasa “of ___” dalam hati, terus cek kecocokan sama sisanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Coret bagian “of ___” buat nemuin subjek aslinya.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kata kerjanya harus cocok sama subjek aslinya, bukan sama kata benda terdekat di sisipan.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nyocokin kata kerjanya sama kata benda paling deket, bukan sama subjek kalimatnya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin subjek aslinya di balik frasa sisipan → cek kecocokan kata kerjanya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select past continuous for a longer background action interrupted by a shorter past-simple event
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner picks past simple for both clauses because both events are 'in the past', ignoring which action was already in progress
templates.reasoningOperation: identify background/interrupting relationship -> assign aspect to each clause
templates.stem: I ___ dinner when the power suddenly went out.

distractors.misconception: treats both clauses as sequential completed events
distractors.whyFails: This would suggest the cooking finished before the power went out, losing the interruption meaning.
distractors.whyFailsId: kesannya masakannya udah selesai sebelum listrik padam.
distractors.misconceptionId: dua kejadiannya dianggap berurutan dan sama-sama selesai.

distractors.misconception: confuses interrupted past action with present perfect result
distractors.whyFails: Present perfect has no fixed past time frame like 'when the power went out' requires.
distractors.whyFailsId: present perfect nggak bisa bareng waktu lampau yang pasti.
distractors.misconceptionId: kejadian lampau yang tersela ketuker sama hasil present perfect.

distractors.misconception: bare present form used for a past narrative
distractors.whyFails: The sentence is anchored in the past by 'went out', so a present bare form is ungrammatical.
distractors.whyFailsId: “went out” naruh kalimatnya di masa lalu.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar present dipakai di dalam cerita lampau.

explanation.whyCorrect: The cooking was already in progress (background) when the shorter past-simple event interrupted it.
explanation.rule: Past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) sets the scene; past simple reports the interrupting event.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Past simple for both loses the sense of one action being 'in progress'; present perfect has no place in a fixed-past narrative.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask which action was already happening when the other one suddenly occurred.
explanation.memoryCue: Background = -ing, interruption = simple past.
explanation.ruleId: Past continuous pakai was atau were + kata kerja -ing buat bangun latarnya. Past simple ngelaporin kejadian yang nyela.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Masak udah jalan sebagai latar waktu listrik tiba-tiba padam.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Past simple di dua-duanya bikin arti “lagi jalan” hilang. Present perfect nggak bisa masuk cerita berwaktu lampau pasti.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: kegiatan mana yang udah jalan waktu kejadian lain muncul?
explanation.memoryCueId: Latar pakai -ing, penyela pakai past simple.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai past continuous buat kejadian latar yang lebih panjang. Pakai past simple buat kejadian pendek yang nyela.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai past simple buat dua kejadiannya karena sama-sama lampau.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin mana kejadian latar dan mana yang nyela → pilih bentuk tiap kata kerjanya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Choose present perfect continuous to emphasize the duration/ongoing nature of an activity vs present perfect simple for result/completion
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner assumes any 'for/since' time phrase automatically requires the continuous form, even when the focus is on a completed result count
templates.reasoningOperation: check whether sentence emphasizes ongoing duration or a countable/completed result -> select form
templates.stem: She ___ three novels this year, and she's already working on a fourth.

distractors.misconception: over-applies continuous aspect whenever a time span like 'this year' appears
distractors.whyFails: The sentence counts a completed result ('three novels'), which needs the simple form, not the continuous.
distractors.whyFailsId: “has been writing” nyorot prosesnya jalan serentak, bukan tiga novel yang udah tuntas.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk continuous dipakai berlebihan tiap muncul rentang waktu kayak “this year”.

distractors.misconception: shifts to a fixed past narrative tense
distractors.whyFails: 'Was writing' frames the writing inside a closed past moment, but 'this year' is still open and no finished reference point appears in the sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: “was writing” ngunci kegiatannya di momen lampau yang tutup, padahal “this year” masih kebuka.
distractors.misconceptionId: pindah ke bentuk cerita lampau yang waktunya udah dipatok.

distractors.misconception: treats the sentence as a habitual routine
distractors.whyFails: The sentence reports a specific cumulative achievement so far, not a general habit.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya nglaporin capaian yang kekumpul sejauh ini, bukan kebiasaan berulang.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimatnya dibaca kayak kebiasaan sehari-hari.

explanation.whyCorrect: A countable, completed result ('three novels') within an unfinished time period calls for present perfect simple.
explanation.rule: Use present perfect simple for completed actions/results with present relevance; use present perfect continuous when duration or repetition of the activity itself is the focus.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Has been writing' is grammatical but says the three novels are still in progress together; past simple needs a finished time frame; present simple describes habits, not a tally.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is the sentence counting/finishing something, or describing the activity as it unfolds?
explanation.memoryCue: Countable result -> simple; ongoing process -> continuous.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai present perfect simple buat tindakan yang udah kelar dan hasilnya masih kerasa sekarang. Pakai present perfect continuous kalau yang ditonjolin lamanya atau berulangnya kegiatan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “three novels” ngitung hasil yang udah kelar, dan “already working on a fourth” nunjukin novel keempatnya baru mulai. Jadi present perfect simple yang pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Has been writing” sah secara bahasa, tapi maknanya tiga novel itu masih dikerjain bareng, bukan tuntas. Past simple minta rentang waktu yang udah tutup, dan present simple nggambarin kebiasaan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: kalimat ini ngitung hasil yang kelar, atau nggambarin kegiatan yang masih jalan?
explanation.memoryCueId: Hasil kehitung pakai simple; proses yang masih jalan pakai continuous.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai present perfect continuous buat nekenin lamanya kegiatan. Present perfect simple buat hasil yang udah kehitung.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira setiap keterangan rentang waktu otomatis minta bentuk continuous. Padahal kalimatnya justru ngitung hasil.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kalimatnya nekenin lamanya kegiatan atau hasil yang kehitung → pilih bentuknya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use past perfect to mark the earlier of two past events when sequence must be made explicit
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses past simple for both events and relies on 'before/after' alone to signal order, even when clarity requires past perfect
templates.reasoningOperation: find the 'by the time' marker that sets the past reference point -> mark the event already completed before that point with had + past participle
templates.stem: By the time the ambulance arrived, the neighbors ___ first aid, so the paramedics only had to check the bandages.

distractors.misconception: uses past simple for the earlier event, flattening the sequence
distractors.whyFails: Without past perfect, 'by the time' loses its meaning of 'before this later point'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “by the time” jadi kehilangan maknanya “sebelum titik itu”.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple dipakai buat kejadian yang lebih dulu, jadi urutannya rata.

distractors.misconception: confuses completed prior action with an action still in progress at the reference point
distractors.whyFails: The continuous form says the first aid was still in progress when the ambulance arrived, but 'so the paramedics only had to check the bandages' shows it had already been completed.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk continuous bilang pertolongannya masih jalan pas ambulans dateng, padahal “only had to check the bandages” nunjukin udah kelar.
distractors.misconceptionId: kejadian yang udah kelar ketuker sama yang masih jalan di titik acuan.

distractors.misconception: bare present form in a past narrative
distractors.whyFails: The whole sentence is anchored in the past by 'arrived', making the bare present ungrammatical.
distractors.whyFailsId: seluruh kalimatnya udah dipatok ke masa lalu sama “arrived”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar present dipakai di dalam cerita lampau.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'By the time' + a past-simple event signals a reference point, and 'the paramedics only had to check the bandages' shows the first aid was already finished before that point — the earlier, completed action needs past perfect.
explanation.rule: Past perfect (had + past participle) marks the earlier of two past actions when the order needs to be unambiguous.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Past simple for both actions leaves the order ambiguous or wrong; the continuous form implies the first aid was still unfinished, which 'only had to check the bandages' rules out; the bare present clashes with the past narrative.
explanation.howToAvoid: When you see 'by the time X happened', make X the reference point, then ask what had already finished before X — that verb takes the past perfect.
explanation.memoryCue: 'By the time X happened' -> the other action needs 'had' first.
explanation.ruleId: Past perfect pakai had + bentuk ketiga kata kerja (past participle). Bentuk ini nandain kejadian yang lebih dulu di antara dua kejadian lampau.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “By the time” plus kejadian past simple bikin titik acuan. “Only had to check the bandages” nunjukin pertolongannya udah kelar sebelum titik itu, jadi pakai past perfect.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Past simple buat dua-duanya bikin urutannya rancu. Bentuk continuous bilang pertolongannya belum kelar, padahal petugasnya tinggal meriksa perbannya. Bentuk dasar present nabrak cerita lampaunya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Begitu lihat “by the time X happened”, jadiin X titik acuannya. Terus tanya apa yang udah kelar sebelum X.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada “by the time X happened”, kejadian satunya butuh “had” di depan.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai past perfect buat nandain kejadian yang lebih dulu di antara dua kejadian lampau.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai past simple buat dua kejadiannya dan cuma nyandar ke “before” atau “after”. Padahal urutannya perlu ditegasin.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin “by the time” yang naruh titik acuannya → tandain kejadian yang udah kelar sebelum titik itu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish future continuous (action in progress at a future point) from future perfect (action completed before a future point)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats any future time expression as requiring 'will + base verb' and cannot separate 'in progress then' from 'finished by then'
templates.reasoningOperation: locate the future reference point -> decide if the action is ongoing or already finished at that point
templates.stem: Which completion shows the action already in progress at that exact moment? Don't call at 8pm — I ___ dinner with my in-laws then.

distractors.misconception: uses a bare future form without marking the ongoing nature of the action
distractors.whyFails: This is correct English ('have dinner' = eat), but it only announces the plan; it does not present the meal as already under way at 8pm.
distractors.whyFailsId: “will have” bener tapi cuma nyebut rencananya, bukan makan malam yang udah jalan.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk masa depan biasa dipakai tanpa nandain tindakannya masih jalan.

distractors.misconception: wrongly applies future perfect, implying the dinner is finished by 8pm
distractors.whyFails: The context says dinner is happening AT 8pm, so it isn't finished yet at that point.
distractors.whyFailsId: konteksnya bilang makan malamnya jalan PADA jam delapan, jadi belum kelar.
distractors.misconceptionId: future perfect dipakai keliru, makan malamnya jadi seolah kelar sebelum jam delapan.

distractors.misconception: drops the future marker entirely, defaulting to present simple
distractors.whyFails: The sentence explicitly refers to a specific future time ('at 8pm'), which requires a future form.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya nyebut waktu nanti yang jelas jadi minta bentuk masa depan.
distractors.misconceptionId: tanda masa depannya ilang sama sekali dan jatuh ke present simple.

explanation.whyCorrect: The dinner will be in progress at the specific future moment (8pm), which is exactly what future continuous expresses.
explanation.rule: Future continuous (will be + verb-ing) describes an action in progress at a stated future time; future perfect (will have + past participle) describes an action completed before that time.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Future perfect wrongly implies the dinner is already over by 8pm; the other options ignore aspect entirely.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: at that future moment, is the action still happening, or already finished?
explanation.memoryCue: Still happening then = will be + -ing; finished by then = will have + past participle.
explanation.ruleId: Future continuous “will be” + kata kerja -ing nggambarin tindakan yang masih jalan di waktu tertentu nanti. Future perfect “will have” + past participle (bentuk ke-3 kata kerja) nggambarin tindakan yang udah kelar sebelum waktu itu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Makan malamnya masih jalan tepat jam delapan, dan itu yang dinyatain future continuous.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Future perfect malah bilang makan malamnya udah kelar sebelum jam delapan. Pilihan lain nggak nandain bentuk waktunya sama sekali.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: pas titik waktu itu nanti, tindakannya masih jalan atau udah kelar?
explanation.memoryCueId: Masih jalan nanti pakai “will be” + -ing; udah kelar pakai “will have” + bentuk ke-3.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu bedain future continuous buat tindakan yang masih jalan di satu titik nanti. Future perfect buat yang udah kelar sebelum titik itu.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira semua keterangan waktu nanti minta “will” + kata kerja dasar. Kamu juga belum misahin “masih jalan saat itu” dari “udah kelar sebelum itu”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin titik acuan waktunya di masa depan → tentuin tindakannya masih jalan atau udah kelar di titik itu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish general past ability (could) from a single successful achievement in a specific past situation (was able to / managed to)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses 'could' for one-time specific past successes, which in standard usage requires 'was/were able to' or 'managed to'
templates.reasoningOperation: check if ability is general/repeated or a single specific achievement -> select modal form
templates.stem: The fire was spreading fast, but the firefighters ___ everyone out of the building.

distractors.misconception: extends general-ability 'could' to a single specific achievement
distractors.whyFails: 'Could' normally reports general past ability, not one specific successful event under pressure.
distractors.whyFailsId: “could” biasanya bilang kemampuan umum, bukan satu keberhasilan yang mendesak.
distractors.misconceptionId: “could” buat kemampuan umum yang ditarik ke satu keberhasilan tertentu.

distractors.misconception: uses present-tense modal for a clearly past narrative
distractors.whyFails: The context ('was spreading') anchors the sentence firmly in the past.
distractors.whyFailsId: “was spreading” udah maku kalimat ini di masa lalu.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu bentuk present dipakai di cerita yang jelas lampau.

distractors.misconception: drops the modal/auxiliary entirely
distractors.whyFails: The sentence needs a modal or auxiliary to express ability, not a bare verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimat ini butuh kata bantu buat nyatain kemampuan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantunya ilang sama sekali.

explanation.whyCorrect: This describes one specific, successful past achievement under difficult conditions, which requires 'was/were able to' rather than 'could'.
explanation.rule: Use 'could' for general past ability; use 'was/were able to' (or 'managed to') for a single specific successful past event, especially against difficulty.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Could get' misapplies general ability to a one-off achievement; the present forms ignore the past time frame.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is this a skill someone generally had, or one specific thing they actually managed to do?
explanation.memoryCue: One-time success under pressure = 'was able to', not 'could'.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai “could” buat kemampuan umum di masa lalu. Pakai “was/were able to” atau “managed to” buat satu keberhasilan tertentu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ini satu keberhasilan tertentu di keadaan sulit, jadi yang pas “was/were able to”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Could get” naruh kemampuan umum di keberhasilan sekali kejadian. Bentuk present ngabaikan ceritanya yang udah lampau.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: ini kemampuan yang biasa dia punya, atau satu hal yang berhasil dia lakuin?
explanation.memoryCueId: Berhasil sekali di keadaan mendesak: “was able to”, bukan “could”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bedain kemampuan umum di masa lalu dari satu keberhasilan di situasi tertentu.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “could” buat keberhasilan sekali kejadian. Padahal pemakaian bakunya minta “was/were able to” atau “managed to”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kemampuannya umum dan berulang atau satu keberhasilan tertentu → pilih bentuknya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Select the correct past modal of deduction based on whether the evidence supports a confident positive or negative conclusion about a past event
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reverses the polarity of a past deduction, reaching for 'can't have' even though the evidence confidently supports that the event did happen
templates.reasoningOperation: evaluate evidence polarity -> match to must have (positive certainty) or can't have (negative certainty)
templates.stem: Which option expresses the strongest positive past deduction supported by the evidence? The lights are still off and his car isn't here — he ___ left for work already.

distractors.misconception: confuses the polarity of the deduction
distractors.whyFails: The evidence (dark house, missing car) supports the conclusion that he DID leave, not that he couldn't have.
distractors.whyFailsId: bukti lampu mati dan mobil yang nggak ada justru dukung dia MEMANG udah pergi.
distractors.misconceptionId: arah kesimpulannya kebalik.

distractors.misconception: confuses deduction with obligation/expectation not met
distractors.whyFails: 'Should have' criticizes a missed obligation; it doesn't express a logical deduction from evidence.
distractors.whyFailsId: “should have” negur kewajiban yang terlewat, bukan nyimpulin dari bukti.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesimpulan ketuker sama kewajiban yang nggak kepenuhan.

distractors.misconception: weakens certainty when the evidence actually supports a confident conclusion
distractors.whyFails: The stem gives strong supporting evidence, which calls for the confident 'must have', not a tentative 'might have'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “might have” masih ragu, padahal buktinya kuat dan searah.
distractors.misconceptionId: tingkat keyakinannya diturunin padahal buktinya kuat.

explanation.whyCorrect: The dark house and absent car are strong evidence for a confident positive conclusion, matching 'must have + past participle'.
explanation.rule: 'Must have' = confident deduction that something happened; 'can't have' = confident deduction that something did NOT happen; both differ from 'should have' (missed obligation) and 'might have' (uncertain possibility).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Can't have' reverses the logic; 'should have' shifts to obligation; 'might have' understates the certainty the evidence supports.
explanation.howToAvoid: First decide if the evidence points confidently 'yes' or confidently 'no', then pick must have / can't have accordingly.
explanation.memoryCue: Strong evidence FOR = must have; strong evidence AGAINST = can't have.
explanation.ruleId: “Must have” berarti yakin sesuatu kejadian; “can’t have” berarti yakin sesuatu nggak kejadian. Beda dari “should have” yang nyoal kewajiban terlewat, dan “might have” yang cuma kemungkinan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Lampu mati dan mobilnya nggak ada itu bukti kuat, jadi pas sama “must have” + past participle.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Can’t have” mbalik arah kesimpulannya, “should have” pindah ke soal kewajiban, dan “might have” ngeremehin kekuatan buktinya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Putusin dulu, ya: buktinya ngarah yakin iya atau yakin nggak? Baru pilih modalnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Bukti kuat mendukung: “must have”. Bukti kuat nyangkal: “can’t have”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pilih modal (kata kayak must, might) buat nyimpulin kejadian lampau sesuai arah buktinya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu mbalik arah kesimpulan lampaunya: milih “can’t have” padahal buktinya yakin kejadiannya memang terjadi.
templates.reasoningOperationId: nilai arah buktinya → pasangin sama “must have” buat yakin iya, atau “can’t have” buat yakin nggak

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish absence of necessity (needn't / don't have to) from prohibition (mustn't)
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats 'mustn't' as simply the negative of 'must', assuming it means 'not necessary' rather than 'forbidden'
templates.reasoningOperation: identify whether the sentence expresses 'not required' or 'forbidden' -> select correct negative modal
templates.stem: You ___ bring your passport to the local gym — a membership card is enough.

distractors.misconception: treats 'mustn't' as the negation of obligation rather than prohibition
distractors.whyFails: 'Mustn't' means it is forbidden to bring a passport, which contradicts the neutral context of simply not being required.
distractors.whyFailsId: artinya bawa paspor itu dilarang, padahal konteksnya cuma bilang nggak perlu.
distractors.misconceptionId: “mustn’t” dikira kebalikan dari kewajiban, padahal maknanya larangan.

distractors.misconception: confuses absence of necessity with negative advice
distractors.whyFails: The sentence isn't warning against bringing a passport, only saying it isn't required.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimat ini nggak nyaranin jangan bawa paspor, cuma bilang nggak wajib.
distractors.misconceptionId: keharusan yang nggak ada ketuker sama saran biar nggak dilakuin.

distractors.misconception: confuses lack of requirement with lack of permission/ability
distractors.whyFails: Nothing in the context suggests bringing a passport is not allowed, only that it's unnecessary.
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak ada bagian konteksnya yang bilang bawa paspor nggak boleh.
distractors.misconceptionId: hal yang nggak diwajibin ketuker sama yang nggak diizinin.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Needn't' expresses that something is not necessary, matching the context where a membership card alone is sufficient.
explanation.rule: 'Needn't' / 'don't have to' = not necessary (but allowed); 'mustn't' = forbidden (not allowed at all).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Mustn't' wrongly forbids the action; 'shouldn't' wrongly advises against it; 'can't' wrongly denies permission.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask: is the action forbidden, or just optional/unnecessary?
explanation.memoryCue: Mustn't = don't do it. Needn't = you may skip it.
explanation.ruleId: “Needn’t” dan “don’t have to” berarti nggak diwajibin tapi tetep boleh. “Mustn’t” berarti dilarang sama sekali.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Needn’t” bilang sesuatu nggak diperluin, dan itu cocok sama kartu anggota yang udah cukup.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Mustn’t” itu ngelarang, “shouldn’t” nyaranin jangan, dan “can’t” nutup izinnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dulu: perbuatannya dilarang, atau cuma nggak wajib?
explanation.memoryCueId: “Mustn’t” berarti jangan dilakuin. “Needn’t” berarti boleh dilewatin.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bedain hal yang nggak diwajibin dari hal yang dilarang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira “mustn’t” cuma bentuk negatif dari “must”, jadi dibaca nggak perlu. Artinya yang bener malah dilarang.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kalimatnya bilang nggak diwajibin atau dilarang → pilih bentuk negatifnya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Form the third conditional to express an unreal hypothetical about a past situation that did not happen
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner mixes a past-simple if-clause with 'would have', instead of using past perfect in the if-clause
templates.reasoningOperation: identify that both clauses refer to an unreal past -> apply if + past perfect / would have + past participle
templates.stem: If she ___ earlier, she wouldn't have missed the flight.

distractors.misconception: uses second-conditional past simple in an if-clause that needs third-conditional past perfect
distractors.whyFails: The main clause 'wouldn't have missed' signals a third conditional, which requires 'had left' in the if-clause, not simple past.
distractors.whyFailsId: induk kalimat “wouldn’t have missed” nandain third conditional, bukan past simple.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple punya second conditional dipakai di bagian yang minta past perfect.

distractors.misconception: duplicates 'would' in both clauses
distractors.whyFails: The if-clause of a conditional never takes 'would'; that belongs only in the main clause.
distractors.whyFailsId: anak kalimat if dalam susunan conditional nggak pernah pakai “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would” dipakai di dua-dua bagian kalimatnya.

distractors.misconception: uses a zero/first-conditional present form for a past unreal situation
distractors.whyFails: The sentence discusses a hypothetical about the past, not a general truth or future possibility.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimatnya ngomongin pengandaian masa lalu, bukan kebenaran umum.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk present punya zero atau first conditional dipakai buat masa lalu yang nggak nyata.

explanation.whyCorrect: The main clause ('wouldn't have missed') marks this as a third conditional describing an unreal past, so the if-clause needs past perfect.
explanation.rule: Third conditional: If + past perfect, ... would have + past participle — used for hypothetical situations in the past that didn't happen.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Simple past belongs to the second conditional (unreal present/future); 'would leave' incorrectly puts 'would' in the if-clause; present simple belongs to real/general conditionals.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check the main clause first — 'would have + past participle' confirms you need 'had + past participle' in the if-clause.
explanation.memoryCue: Both halves look back: had... would have...
explanation.ruleId: Third conditional: if + past perfect, terus would have + past participle (bentuk ke-3 kata kerja). Dipakai buat ngebayangin keadaan lampau yang nggak kejadian.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Induk kalimatnya “wouldn’t have missed” nandain third conditional soal masa lalu yang nggak nyata. Jadi anak kalimat if-nya minta past perfect.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Past simple itu punya second conditional buat keadaan sekarang yang nggak nyata. “Would leave” salah naruh “would” di anak kalimat if, dan present simple punya syarat yang nyata.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dulu induk kalimatnya: kalau bunyinya “would have” + bentuk ke-3, anak kalimat if-nya minta “had” + bentuk ke-3.
explanation.memoryCueId: Dua-duanya nengok ke belakang: had ... would have ...

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun third conditional buat ngebayangin keadaan lampau yang sebenernya nggak kejadian.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nyampur bagian if bentuk past simple sama “would have”, padahal bagian if-nya minta past perfect.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali dua bagiannya sama-sama ngomongin masa lalu yang nggak nyata → pakai if + past perfect dan would have + bentuk ke-3

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Construct a mixed conditional linking an unreal past cause to a present-time hypothetical result
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner forces a 'pure' third conditional (would have) even when the result clause clearly refers to the present, not the past
templates.reasoningOperation: separate the time of the cause from the time of the result -> apply past perfect in if-clause, would + base verb in main clause
templates.stem: If I hadn't taken that job in Berlin, I ___ fluent in German now.

distractors.misconception: places the result in the unreal past instead of the present
distractors.whyFails: 'Would not have been' is a past hypothetical result, but 'now' requires a present hypothetical state.
