templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira kalimat yang kedengeran lancar udah bener, tanpa ngecek pelaku tersirat di frasa pembukanya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin siapa yang masuk akal ngelakuin tindakan di frasa pembukanya → cek subjek induk kalimatnya memang itu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects 'despite' (+ noun/gerund) rather than 'although' (+ clause) when the following element is a noun phrase, not a full clause.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners use 'although' before a noun phrase, ignoring that 'although' requires a full subject-verb clause while 'despite' takes a noun/gerund.
templates.reasoningOperation: Check the grammatical form of what follows the connector (clause vs noun phrase) and match it to the connector that accepts that form.
templates.stem: ____ the heavy rain, the outdoor concert went ahead as planned.

distractors.misconception: Assumes 'although' can be followed directly by a noun phrase like 'despite' can.
distractors.whyFails: 'Although' must be followed by a full clause (subject + verb), such as 'although it rained heavily', not a bare noun phrase like 'the heavy rain'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “although” harus diikuti anak kalimat utuh, bukan frasa benda telanjang.
distractors.misconceptionId: “although” dikira bisa langsung diikuti frasa benda.

distractors.misconception: Treats 'however' as a subordinating connector that can start a sentence and directly attach to a noun.
distractors.whyFails: 'However' is a sentence adverb that needs its own independent clause and typically a comma-separated structure, not a direct noun-phrase attachment.
distractors.whyFailsId: “however” itu kata keterangan kalimat yang butuh anak kalimat sendiri.
distractors.misconceptionId: “however” dianggap penghubung yang bisa langsung nempel ke kata benda.

distractors.misconception: Confuses 'even though' (also clause-requiring, like 'although') with prepositional 'despite'.
distractors.whyFails: Like 'although', 'even though' requires a full clause, not a bare noun phrase such as 'the heavy rain'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “even though” juga minta anak kalimat utuh, bukan frasa benda telanjang.
distractors.misconceptionId: “even though” yang minta anak kalimat ketuker sama kata depan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Despite' is a preposition that can be directly followed by a noun phrase such as 'the heavy rain'.
explanation.rule: Despite/in spite of + noun/gerund; although/even though/though + subject + verb clause.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Although', 'even though', and 'however' all require a clause structure, not a bare noun phrase, in this position.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check what follows: a noun alone needs despite/in spite of; a full clause needs although/even though.
explanation.memoryCue: Despite + noun; although + clause.
explanation.ruleId: Despite dan in spite of diikuti kata benda atau bentuk -ing. Although, even though, dan though diikuti anak kalimat berisi subjek dan kata kerja.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Despite” itu preposition (kata depan) yang bisa langsung diikuti frasa benda kayak “the heavy rain”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Although”, “even though”, dan “however” sama-sama minta susunan anak kalimat, bukan frasa benda telanjang di posisi ini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek yang nyusul: kata benda aja minta despite atau in spite of; anak kalimat utuh minta although atau even though.
explanation.memoryCueId: Despite + kata benda; although + anak kalimat.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pilih “despite” yang diikuti kata benda, bukan “although” yang diikuti anak kalimat. Itu pas yang nyusul berupa frasa benda.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “although” di depan frasa benda. Kamu nggak lihat “although” minta anak kalimat berisi subjek dan kata kerja.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek bentuk yang nyusul kata penghubungnya, anak kalimat atau frasa benda → pasangin sama penghubung yang nerima bentuk itu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects the 'so + adjective + that' result pattern rather than 'such' when directly modifying an adjective (not a noun).
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners use 'such' before a bare adjective, forgetting that 'such' requires a following noun while 'so' modifies adjectives/adverbs directly.
templates.reasoningOperation: Identify whether the intensified word is an adjective alone (so) or a noun phrase (such a/an + adjective + noun).
templates.stem: The lecture was ____ boring that half the audience fell asleep.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'such' directly before an adjective without a following noun.
distractors.whyFails: 'Such' needs a noun phrase (such a boring lecture); here 'boring' stands alone as a predicate adjective, which takes 'so', not 'such'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “such” minta frasa benda kayak “such a boring lecture”, bukan kata sifat telanjang.
distractors.misconceptionId: “such” dipakai langsung di depan kata sifat tanpa kata benda.

distractors.misconception: Inserts an article as if a noun were about to follow.
distractors.whyFails: There is no noun after 'boring' in this sentence structure (it's 'the lecture was boring', not 'a boring lecture'), so 'such a' doesn't fit grammatically.
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak ada kata benda sesudah “boring” di susunan ini.
distractors.misconceptionId: artikel disisipkan seolah akan ada kata benda yang menyusul.

distractors.misconception: Confuses a result adverb linking two independent clauses with an intensifier inside a so...that structure.
distractors.whyFails: 'Therefore' connects two full sentences and cannot sit inside a 'that'-result clause modifying an adjective this way.
distractors.whyFailsId: “therefore” nyambungin dua kalimat utuh, bukan nguatin kata sifat di anak kalimat “that”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata keterangan akibat ketuker sama penguat di dalam pola so ... that.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'So + adjective + that' is the correct pattern when intensifying a predicate adjective, as in 'so boring that...'.
explanation.rule: So + adjective/adverb + that; such (+ a/an) + adjective + noun + that.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Such' and 'such a' both require a noun that isn't present; 'therefore' is a separate-sentence connector, not part of this clause pattern.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check if a noun follows the adjective: if not, use 'so'; if a noun is present, use 'such (a/an)'.
explanation.memoryCue: So + adjective (so boring); such + a + adjective + noun (such a boring lecture).
explanation.ruleId: So + kata sifat atau kata keterangan + that; such (+ a atau an) + kata sifat + kata benda + that.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Pola so + kata sifat + that itu bentuk yang tepat buat nguatin kata sifat di predikat. Contohnya “so boring that ...”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Such” dan “such a” sama-sama minta kata benda yang di sini nggak ada. “Therefore” itu penghubung antarkalimat, bukan bagian pola ini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek ada kata benda sesudah kata sifatnya atau nggak: kalau nggak ada, pakai “so”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “So” + kata sifat kayak so boring; “such” + a + kata sifat + kata benda kayak such a boring lecture.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pilih pola so + kata sifat + that, bukan “such”, pas yang diterangin langsung sebuah kata sifat.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “such” di depan kata sifat telanjang. Kamu lupa “such” minta kata benda, sedangkan “so” langsung nerangin kata sifat.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin yang dikuatin sebuah kata sifat sendirian atau frasa benda → pilih so, atau such a dan such an + kata sifat + kata benda

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner constructs an it-cleft sentence to place emphatic focus on a specific element of the original sentence.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners misplace the emphasized element or use 'who/which' inconsistently instead of the standard cleft pattern with 'that'.
templates.reasoningOperation: Identify the element needing emphasis, then front it correctly inside the 'It was/is ... that ...' frame.
templates.stem: Original: Sarah broke the vase, not her brother. Cleft emphasis: ____ broke the vase, not her brother.

distractors.misconception: Misorders the fixed cleft frame, inserting the emphasized element before 'was'.
distractors.whyFails: The cleft frame requires 'It was' to stay together immediately before the emphasized element: 'It was Sarah', not 'It Sarah was'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kerangka cleft minta “It was” tetap nyatu persis sebelum bagian yang ditonjolin.
distractors.misconceptionId: kerangka cleft yang baku diacak dengan naruh bagian yang ditonjolin sebelum “was”.

distractors.misconception: Fronts the emphasized noun before the cleft frame entirely.
distractors.whyFails: 'Sarah it was that' pushes the emphasized noun in front of even the pronoun 'it', so the sentence no longer opens with the obligatory 'It was' frame at all.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata benda yang ditonjolin naik bahkan sebelum kata “it”, jadi kerangka wajibnya nggak kepakai.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata benda yang ditonjolin dimajuin bahkan sebelum kata “it” pembuka kerangka cleft.

distractors.misconception: Places 'that' before the emphasized noun instead of after it.
distractors.whyFails: 'That' must come after the emphasized element (It was Sarah that...), introducing the rest of the clause, not before it.
distractors.whyFailsId: “that” wajib berdiri sesudah bagian yang ditonjolin buat mbuka sisa anak kalimatnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: “that” ditaruh sebelum kata benda yang ditonjolin, bukan sesudahnya.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'It was Sarah that broke the vase' follows the fixed it-cleft frame: It + be + emphasized element + that + rest of clause.
explanation.rule: It-cleft: It + was/is + [emphasized element] + that + [remainder of the original sentence].
explanation.whyOthersFail: The distractors all scramble the fixed word order of the cleft frame, none of which are grammatical.
explanation.howToAvoid: Keep 'It was' fixed at the start, insert the emphasized noun right after it, then 'that' before the rest of the clause.
explanation.memoryCue: It was [emphasis] that [rest] — never break up 'It was'.
explanation.ruleId: It-cleft: It + was atau is + bagian yang ditonjolin + that + sisa kalimat aslinya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “It was Sarah that broke the vase” ngikutin kerangka it-cleft yang baku. Urutannya: It, bentuk be, bagian yang ditonjolin, that, sisa anak kalimatnya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Pilihan lainnya ngacak urutan kerangka cleft yang udah baku, dan nggak ada satu pun yang sah.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Biarin “It was” tetap di awal, sisipin kata benda yang ditonjolin persis sesudahnya, terus “that” sebelum sisanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: It was [yang ditonjolin] that [sisanya] — jangan pernah misahin “It was”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun kalimat penekanan bentuk it-cleft buat nonjolin satu bagian tertentu dari kalimat aslinya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu salah naruh bagian yang ditonjolin, atau pakai who dan which nggak konsisten, bukan pola baku pakai “that”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin bagian yang perlu ditonjolin → majuin dengan bener ke kerangka “It was/is ... that ...”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner recognizes that 'would' cannot express past habitual states (only repeated actions), unlike 'used to'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners treat 'used to' and 'would' as fully interchangeable for all past habits, including states.
templates.reasoningOperation: Classify whether the sentence describes a past state (only used to/past simple) or a repeated action (used to or would).
templates.stem: When I was a child, I ____ a small village near the mountains.

distractors.misconception: Applies 'would' to a stative verb (live = residing state) as if it were a repeated dynamic action.
distractors.whyFails: 'Would' is reserved for repeated dynamic actions (would visit, would play), not extended past states like living somewhere.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” disediain buat tindakan berulang kayak “would visit”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would” diterapin ke kata kerja keadaan seolah itu tindakan berulang.

distractors.misconception: Adds a past-tense ending to the verb after the modal 'would'.
distractors.whyFails: Modals are always followed by the bare infinitive; 'would lived' incorrectly double-marks the past tense.
distractors.whyFailsId: modal selalu diikutin kata kerja bentuk dasar.
distractors.misconceptionId: akhiran lampau ditambahin pada kata kerja sesudah modal.

distractors.misconception: Uses a bare gerund with no finite verb to carry the sentence's tense.
distractors.whyFails: The sentence needs a finite past-tense verb form to function as the main verb; 'living in' alone cannot do that.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk -ing sendirian nggak bisa jadi kata kerja utama.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing telanjang dipakai tanpa kata kerja bertense yang nopang kalimatnya.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Used to live' correctly expresses a past state that no longer holds, which 'would' cannot express.
explanation.rule: Used to covers past states and repeated actions; would only covers repeated actions, never states.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Would live' misapplies the action-only modal to a state verb; the other options are simply not valid finite verb forms.
explanation.howToAvoid: For state verbs (live, have, know, believe) describing the past, use 'used to' or plain past simple, never 'would'.
explanation.memoryCue: States: used to only. Actions: used to OR would.
explanation.ruleId: “Used to” nyakup keadaan lampau dan tindakan berulang. “Would” cuma nyakup tindakan berulang, nggak pernah keadaan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Live” itu kata kerja keadaan. “Used to live” nyatain keadaan lampau yang sekarang udah nggak berlaku.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Would live” maksa modal khusus tindakan ke kata kerja keadaan. Dua pilihan lain sama sekali bukan bentuk kata kerja bertense yang sah.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Buat kata kerja keadaan kayak “live” dan “know”, pakai “used to” atau past simple.
explanation.memoryCueId: Keadaan lampau cuma “used to”; tindakan berulang boleh dua-duanya.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu ngenali “would” nggak bisa nyatain keadaan lampau. Kata itu cuma buat tindakan yang berulang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nganggep “used to” dan “would” bisa saling gantiin buat semua kebiasaan lampau, termasuk keadaan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kalimatnya nyebut keadaan lampau atau tindakan berulang → pilih bentuk yang boleh dipakai

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner uses present perfect with an unfinished time period ('this week') to connect a past action to the still-ongoing present frame.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners default to past simple whenever a specific event is named, ignoring that the time period itself is still in progress.
templates.reasoningOperation: confirm the tested contrast is present perfect versus past simple -> check the named period (this week) is still running -> reject the past form that would close it
templates.stem: So far this week I ___ three important emails, and there are two more to write before Friday.

distractors.misconception: Uses past simple because a specific number of emails is mentioned.
distractors.whyFails: 'Sent' closes the time frame as finished, but 'so far this week' shows the week is still in progress — two emails are still to be written before Friday — so the finished frame it needs does not exist here.
distractors.whyFailsId: “so far” nandain rentang yang masih jalan, jadi bentuk lampau nggak pas.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple dipakai padahal rentang waktunya belum tutup.

distractors.misconception: Uses past continuous to describe a series of completed actions.
distractors.whyFails: Past continuous suits an action in progress at a specific past moment, not three completed, countable actions within an ongoing period.
distractors.whyFailsId: past continuous cocok buat tindakan yang lagi jalan di satu saat lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: past continuous dipakai buat nggambarin serangkaian tindakan yang udah tuntas.

distractors.misconception: Uses present simple, ignoring that the sentence reports completed past actions within the current period.
distractors.whyFails: Present simple describes habits/facts, not specific completed actions that already happened earlier in the still-ongoing week.
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple nggambarin kebiasaan atau fakta.
distractors.misconceptionId: present simple dipakai padahal kalimatnya nyebut tindakan lampau tertentu.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'So far this week' keeps the period open and two emails are still unwritten, so present perfect is required; past simple would close a period that is still running.
explanation.rule: Choose present perfect over past simple when reporting actions inside a period that has not ended yet, as in 'I have sent three reports this week'; the past form would close a period that is still running.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Past simple needs a finished time frame; past continuous misrepresents completed actions as in-progress; present simple isn't for specific past actions.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check if the named time period has ended yet — if not, present perfect is usually required.
explanation.memoryCue: Time period not over yet = present perfect, not past simple.
explanation.ruleId: Pilih present perfect daripada past simple buat tindakan di dalam rentang yang belum berakhir. Bentuk lampau justru nutup rentang yang masih jalan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “So far this week” nyebut rentang yang belum tutup, dan dua surel lagi belum kekirim. Jadi present perfect yang pas di sini.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Past simple nutup rentang yang masih jalan, dan “so far” ngunci pilihan itu. Past continuous nampilin tindakan tuntas kayak masih jalan. Present simple bukan buat tindakan lampau tertentu. Tanpa “so far”, ragam Amerika kadang masih nerima bentuk lampau.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dulu rentang waktu yang disebut udah berakhir atau belum.
explanation.memoryCueId: Rentang waktunya belum tutup, berarti pakai present perfect.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai present perfect bareng rentang waktu yang belum berakhir, kayak “this week”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu langsung pakai past simple tiap ada kejadian tertentu yang disebut. Rentang waktunya yang masih jalan jadi kelewat.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek rentang yang disebut masih jalan atau udah tutup → pilih present perfect atau past simple

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner distinguishes 'should have' (criticizing a wrong decision) from 'could have' (noting an unused possibility) in a context calling for criticism.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners select 'could have' when the sentence context clearly implies blame/regret rather than a neutral missed option.
templates.reasoningOperation: Find the blaming tone — a bad outcome now regretted — then mark that criticism of the past choice with should have + past participle.
templates.stem: Which completion explicitly criticizes the past decision rather than merely noting a possibility? You ____ more carefully before signing the contract — now we're stuck with these terms.

distractors.misconception: Treats a clearly critical statement as a neutral, non-judgmental missed opportunity.
distractors.whyFails: The context ('now we're stuck with these terms') expresses blame/regret, which calls for 'should have', not the neutral 'could have'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “now we’re stuck with these terms” nyatain penyesalan, bukan peluang netral.
distractors.misconceptionId: pernyataan yang jelas negur diperlakuin sebagai peluang terlewat yang netral.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'would have' as if this were a hypothetical conditional result rather than direct criticism.
distractors.whyFails: 'Would have' typically pairs with an if-clause to state a hypothetical result, not to directly criticize someone's past action like this.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would have” biasanya pasangan anak kalimat if buat hasil pengandaian.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would have” dipakai seolah ini hasil pengandaian, bukan teguran langsung.

distractors.misconception: Confuses past deduction ('must have') with retrospective criticism.
distractors.whyFails: 'Must have read' would mean the speaker is deducing that the person probably did read it, which contradicts the sentence's implication that they did not.
distractors.whyFailsId: “must have read” nyimpulin dia kemungkinan besar udah baca, bentrok sama maksud kalimatnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesimpulan soal masa lalu ketuker sama teguran sesudah kejadian.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Should have read' criticizes the past failure to read carefully, matching the regretful consequence described.
explanation.rule: Should have + past participle = criticism/regret about a past action that didn't happen or was done wrong.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Could have' is neutral, 'would have' needs a conditional pairing, and 'must have' expresses deduction, not blame.
explanation.howToAvoid: If the sentence blames someone for a past failure, use should have, not could have.
explanation.memoryCue: Should have = 'you were wrong not to'; could have = 'it was possible, no judgment'.
explanation.ruleId: Should have + bentuk ke-3 berarti teguran atau penyesalan atas tindakan lampau yang nggak dilakuin atau keliru dilakuin.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Should have read” negur kelalaian baca yang teliti, dan itu sejalan sama akibat yang disesalin di kalimatnya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Could have” netral, “would have” minta pasangan anak kalimat pengandaian, dan “must have” nyatain kesimpulan, bukan teguran.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau kalimatnya nyalahin seseorang atas kelalaian di masa lalu, pakai should have.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada penyesalan atas kelalaian di masa lalu? Pakai should have.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu bedain “should have” + past participle (bentuk ke-3 kata kerja) yang negur, dari “could have” yang netral.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu milih “could have” padahal konteksnya jelas nyiratin penyesalan dan teguran, bukan pilihan yang netral.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin nada nyalahin di kalimatnya, akibat buruk yang sekarang disesalin → tandain teguran atas pilihan lampau itu dengan should have + bentuk ke-3

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'be able to' where the grammar requires a non-finite ability expression after another infinitive.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats 'can' like a normal infinitive and writes impossible combinations such as 'to can'.
templates.reasoningOperation: detect the preceding infinitive marker -> recognize that can has no infinitive -> substitute be able to
templates.stem: After months of treatment, she hopes to ___ walk without assistance again.

distractors.misconception: places the finite modal 'can' after infinitive 'to'
distractors.whyFails: English has no infinitive 'to can'; after 'hopes to', ability must be expressed as 'be able to'.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk “to can” nggak dikenal dalam Bahasa Inggris.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal bertense ditaruh sesudah “to”.

distractors.misconception: uses a finite past/conditional modal in a non-finite slot
distractors.whyFails: 'Could' cannot follow 'hopes to' and would also introduce the wrong time or conditional meaning.
distractors.whyFailsId: “could” modal bertense yang nggak bisa nyusul “hopes to”.
distractors.misconceptionId: modal bertense lampau dipakai di posisi yang minta bentuk tanpa tense.

distractors.misconception: uses a gerund-participle where a bare infinitive is required
distractors.whyFails: The first 'to' belongs to 'hopes to' and must be followed by the base form 'be', not 'being'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to” yang pertama minta bentuk dasar bukan bentuk -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai di posisi yang minta bentuk dasar.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Hopes to be able to walk' uses the infinitive form of the ability expression that 'can' itself does not possess.
explanation.rule: When grammar requires an infinitive, perfect, or other non-finite form of ability, use a form of 'be able to' instead of 'can'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Can' and 'could' are finite modals and cannot occupy the infinitive slot; 'being' is the wrong non-finite form after 'hopes to'.
explanation.howToAvoid: If you are about to write 'to can', stop and replace the whole ability phrase with 'to be able to'.
explanation.memoryCue: No 'to can'; say 'to be able to'.
explanation.ruleId: “Can” nggak punya bentuk “to” dan bentuk perfect. Kalau susunannya minta bentuk kayak itu, pakai “be able to”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Hopes to” minta bentuk dasar sesudahnya. “Be able to” nyediain bentuk kemampuan yang nggak dimiliki “can”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Can” dan “could” modal bertense, jadi nggak bisa ngisi posisi ini. “Being” bentuk tanpa tense yang keliru sesudah “hopes to”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau mau nulis “to can”, berhenti dulu, ya, terus ganti seluruh ungkapannya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Nggak ada “to can”; ucapin “to be able to”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai “be able to” di posisi yang minta bentuk kemampuan tanpa tense. Misalnya sesudah “to” yang lain.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nganggep “can” kayak kata kerja biasa. Kamu nulis gabungan yang nggak mungkin kayak “to can”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temukan “to” yang mendahuluinya → sadar “can” nggak punya bentuk “to” → ganti sama “be able to”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner constructs a mixed conditional where a present unreal state explains a past unreal result.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners force both clauses of a mixed conditional into the same tense, missing that present cause and past result require different forms.
templates.reasoningOperation: Identify that the condition describes a permanent present trait while the result describes a specific past event, requiring mixed tenses.
templates.stem: In formal written English, which completion presents his fear as an ongoing trait he still has, rather than only a past state? If he ____ so afraid of flying, he would have joined us on the trip to Japan last year.

distractors.misconception: Forces the third conditional past perfect form into the condition clause, matching the past result tense.
distractors.whyFails: This is correct English, but it frames the fear as a past state only; the question asks for the form that keeps the fear ongoing today.
distractors.whyFailsId: bahasanya bener, tapi rasa takutnya jadi keadaan lampau saja, nggak kebawa sampai sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk past perfect milik third conditional dipaksa ke anak kalimat syarat biar cocok sama tense hasilnya.

distractors.misconception: Uses ordinary past simple negative instead of the subjunctive 'weren't' required in hypothetical conditionals.
distractors.whyFails: Formal hypothetical conditionals conventionally use 'were' (not 'was') for all subjects in the if-clause, especially in this fixed unreal-present pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: pengandaian formal biasanya pakai “were” di anak kalimat if, bukan “was”.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple negatif biasa dipakai gantiin bentuk “were” yang baku di pengandaian.

distractors.misconception: Uses present tense, missing that the condition is hypothetical/unreal, not a real current fact.
distractors.whyFails: Present simple would state a real fact, but the sentence expresses an unreal present condition explaining a past hypothetical result.
distractors.whyFailsId: present simple bakal nyatain fakta nyata, padahal syaratnya cuma dibayangin.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk present dipakai jadi syaratnya kayak kenyataan, bukan pengandaian.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Weren't' (second-conditional form) expresses the ongoing unreal present trait (his fear) that explains why the past result didn't happen.
explanation.rule: Mixed conditional (present cause, past result): If + past simple/subjunctive were, ... would have + past participle.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Hadn't been' wrongly matches the past-perfect result tense; 'wasn't' skips the subjunctive; 'isn't' treats the condition as real, not hypothetical.
explanation.howToAvoid: Separate the two clauses: is the cause a lasting present trait, or a specific past event? Match each clause's tense independently.
explanation.memoryCue: Present cause + past result = If + were..., would have + participle.
explanation.ruleId: Mixed conditional sebab masa kini dan hasil masa lalu: If + past simple atau bentuk were, terus would have + past participle.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Weren’t” berbentuk second conditional dan nyatain sifat sekarang yang nggak nyata, yaitu rasa takutnya. Itu yang nerangin kenapa hasil lampaunya nggak kejadian.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Hadn’t been” nyamain diri sama tense hasil yang past perfect. “Wasn’t” ngelewatin bentuk “were” yang baku, dan “isn’t” bikin syaratnya kayak kenyataan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Pisahin dua anak kalimatnya: sebabnya sifat menetap sekarang, atau kejadian lampau tertentu? Tentuin tense-nya masing-masing.
explanation.memoryCueId: Sebab masa kini dan hasil masa lalu: If + were ..., would have + past participle.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun mixed conditional dengan keadaan sekarang yang nggak nyata sebagai sebab dari hasil lampau yang nggak kejadian.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu maksa kedua anak kalimatnya pakai tense yang sama, padahal sebab masa kini dan hasil masa lalu minta bentuk beda.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali syaratnya sifat menetap di masa kini dan hasilnya kejadian lampau tertentu → pakai tense yang beda di tiap anak kalimat

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects 'provided that' (a positive condition of agreement) over 'unless' (a negative exception) based on the sentence's logical meaning.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners treat all conditional connectors (unless, provided that, as long as) as interchangeable regardless of positive/negative logic.
templates.reasoningOperation: Determine whether the sentence states a required positive condition (provided that/as long as) or a negative exception (unless), then select accordingly.
templates.stem: You can borrow my car ____ you bring it back before six o'clock.

distractors.misconception: Uses the negative-exception connector where a positive required condition is meant.
distractors.whyFails: 'Unless' means 'except if', which would reverse the meaning to 'you can't borrow it if you bring it back', the opposite of the intended condition.
distractors.whyFailsId: “unless” berarti kecuali kalau, jadi maknanya kebalik dari syarat yang dimaksud.
distractors.misconceptionId: penghubung kekecualian negatif dipakai padahal yang dimaksud syarat positif.

distractors.misconception: Uses a concessive connector implying the condition doesn't matter to the outcome.
distractors.whyFails: 'Even if' suggests the outcome happens regardless of the condition, but here returning the car by six is a genuine requirement, not an irrelevant detail.
distractors.whyFailsId: “even if” bilang hasilnya tetap kejadian apa pun syaratnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: penghubung pertentangan dipakai jadi syaratnya seolah nggak ngaruh.

distractors.misconception: Uses 'in case' (precaution for a possible future event) instead of a condition of permission.
distractors.whyFails: 'In case' expresses a precaution against something that might happen, not a required condition attached to granting permission.
distractors.whyFailsId: “in case” nyatain persiapan buat sesuatu yang mungkin kejadian.
distractors.misconceptionId: “in case” yang nyatain kesiapsiagaan dipakai ganti syarat pemberian izin.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Provided that' states the positive condition that must be met for the permission (borrowing the car) to hold.
explanation.rule: Provided that / as long as = positive required condition; unless = negative exception ('except if').
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Unless' reverses the logic; 'even if' implies irrelevance; 'in case' expresses precaution, not a required condition.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check the logic: is this a required condition (provided that) or an exception that blocks the result (unless)?
explanation.memoryCue: Provided that = 'only if'; unless = 'except if'.
explanation.ruleId: Provided that dan as long as nyatain syarat positif yang wajib dipenuhi. Unless nyatain kekecualian negatif yang berarti kecuali kalau.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Provided that” nyatain syarat positif yang harus dipenuhi biar izin minjem mobilnya tetap berlaku.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Unless” mbalik alur maknanya, “even if” bilang syaratnya nggak ngaruh, dan “in case” nyatain kesiapsiagaan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek alurnya: ini syarat yang wajib dipenuhi, atau kekecualian yang mbatalin hasilnya?
explanation.memoryCueId: “Provided that” berarti cuma kalau; “unless” berarti kecuali kalau.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pilih “provided that” sebagai syarat positif yang wajib dipenuhi, bukan “unless” yang berupa kekecualian negatif.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nganggep unless, provided that, dan as long as bisa gantian. Kamu nggak lihat kutub positif atau negatifnya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin kalimatnya nyebut syarat positif yang wajib dipenuhi atau kekecualian negatif → pilih penghubungnya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner forms the passive of a ditransitive verb by correctly choosing which object becomes the passive subject (typically the indirect object in natural usage).
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners keep both objects in the passive sentence or choose the less natural direct-object-as-subject pattern by default.
templates.reasoningOperation: Identify the indirect object (recipient) as the more natural passive subject choice for verbs like give/send/offer.
templates.stem: The company sent all employees a bonus. → All employees ____ a bonus.

distractors.misconception: Adds an unnecessary preposition after the passive verb when the recipient is already the subject.
distractors.whyFails: Once 'all employees' is the subject, 'to' becomes redundant; the correct passive is simply 'were sent a bonus', with the remaining object following directly.
distractors.whyFailsId: begitu “all employees” jadi subjek, “to” jadi mubazir.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan ditambahin sesudah kata kerja pasif padahal penerimanya udah jadi subjek.

distractors.misconception: Reverses the auxiliary and main verb order.
distractors.whyFails: Passive voice requires be + past participle in that fixed order; 'sent were' is not a valid English word order.
distractors.whyFailsId: “sent were” bukan urutan kata yang sah buat kalimat pasif.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan kata bantu dan kata kerja utamanya dibalik.

distractors.misconception: Fails subject-verb agreement, treating the plural subject 'all employees' as singular.
distractors.whyFails: 'All employees' is plural, so it requires the plural auxiliary 'were', not the singular 'was'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “all employees” bentuknya jamak, jadi kata bantunya nggak boleh tunggal.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesesuaian subjeknya gagal karena subjek jamak diperlakuin sebagai tunggal.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Were sent a bonus' correctly passivizes the indirect object (employees) as subject, keeping the direct object (a bonus) after the verb.
explanation.rule: With ditransitive verbs, the indirect object (recipient) usually becomes the passive subject, followed by the direct object.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Adding 'to' is redundant, reversing auxiliary/verb order is ungrammatical, and 'was' breaks subject-verb agreement.
explanation.howToAvoid: Passivize the recipient as subject, then keep the thing given directly after the verb, no extra preposition.
explanation.memoryCue: Recipient becomes subject: 'Employees were sent a bonus' (no 'to').
explanation.ruleId: Di kata kerja berobjek dua, objek penerimanya biasanya jadi subjek pasif, terus disusul objek langsungnya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Were sent a bonus” bikin penerimanya, yaitu para karyawan, jadi subjek pasifnya. Objek langsungnya tetap berdiri sesudah kata kerjanya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Nambahin “to” itu mubazir, dan mbalik urutan kata bantu dan kata kerjanya nggak sah. Bentuk tunggal juga ngerusak kesesuaian sama subjek jamaknya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Jadiin penerimanya subjek, terus taruh benda yang dikasih langsung sesudah kata kerjanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Penerimanya jadi subjek: “Employees were sent a bonus”, tanpa “to”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun kalimat passive (fokus ke yang kena tindakan) dari kata kerja berobjek dua. Yang biasanya jadi subjeknya adalah penerimanya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nahan dua objeknya di kalimat pasif. Atau kamu bikin objek langsungnya jadi subjek walau kedengeran kurang wajar.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali objek penerimanya sebagai pilihan subjek pasif yang lebih wajar buat kata kerja kayak give, send, dan offer

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects the passive gerund form ('being + past participle') after a verb/preposition that requires a gerund complement.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners use the passive infinitive ('to be + past participle') after verbs that specifically require a gerund complement.
templates.reasoningOperation: Identify the verb's required complement type (gerund vs infinitive) first, then apply the matching passive form.
templates.stem: She resents ____ like a child in front of her colleagues.

distractors.misconception: Applies the passive infinitive pattern to a verb ('resent') that specifically requires a gerund complement.
distractors.whyFails: 'Resent' is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive; the passive form must therefore be 'being treated', not 'to be treated'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “resent” diikuti bentuk -ing, bukan bentuk to, jadi pola pasifnya ikut salah.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola bentuk to pasif dipakai di “resent” yang khusus minta pelengkap bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: Uses the bare passive infinitive without 'to' or the required gerund '-ing' form.
distractors.whyFails: This form fits after modals or causative make/let, not after 'resent', which needs a gerund complement.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini cocok sesudah modal atau sesudah make dan let, bukan sesudah “resent”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk pasif dasar dipakai tanpa “to” maupun akhiran -ing yang diwajibin.

distractors.misconception: Drops the auxiliary needed to mark the passive voice, leaving only the past participle.
distractors.whyFails: Without 'being', the sentence loses its passive marking entirely and becomes grammatically incomplete after 'resents'.
distractors.whyFailsId: tanda pasifnya hilang sama sekali, jadi kalimatnya nggak utuh sesudah “resents”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu pasifnya hilang jadi tersisa past participle saja.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Being treated' is the passive gerund, correctly complementing 'resent', a verb that requires a gerund object.
explanation.rule: Passive gerund (being + past participle) follows verbs/prepositions that require gerund complements, like resent, avoid, admit.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'To be treated' wrongly uses the infinitive pattern; 'be treated' and 'treated' both lack the required gerund marker 'being'.
explanation.howToAvoid: First check if the verb takes a gerund complement; if so, its passive form must be 'being + past participle'.
explanation.memoryCue: Resent/avoid/admit + being + past participle (never 'to be').
explanation.ruleId: Bentuk -ing pasif being + past participle nyusul kata kerja atau kata depan yang minta pelengkap -ing. Contohnya resent, avoid, dan admit.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Being treated” itu bentuk -ing pasif yang pas jadi pelengkap “resent”, kata kerja yang minta objek bentuk -ing.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “To be treated” keliru pakai pola bentuk to. “Be treated” dan “treated” sama-sama kehilangan “being” yang diwajibin.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dulu kata kerjanya minta pelengkap -ing atau nggak. Kalau iya, bentuk pasifnya wajib being + past participle.
explanation.memoryCueId: Resent, avoid, dan admit diikuti being + past participle, nggak pernah “to be”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu milih bentuk pasif being + past participle sesudah kata kerja atau kata depan yang minta pelengkap -ing.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai bentuk to pasif sesudah kata kerja yang justru minta pelengkap bentuk -ing.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali jenis pelengkap yang dituntut kata kerjanya, bentuk -ing atau bentuk to → terapkan bentuk pasif yang cocok

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner shifts first/second-person pronouns and possessives to third person when reporting speech from a different speaker's perspective.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners backshift the verb tense correctly but leave the original speaker's pronouns unchanged, producing a perspective mismatch.
templates.reasoningOperation: Identify who is speaking (the reporter) versus who originally spoke, then shift pronouns/possessives to match the reporter's perspective, independent of tense backshift.
templates.stem: Direct speech (Tom to Anna): "I've lost my keys." Anna reporting to someone else: Tom said ____ had lost ____ keys.

distractors.misconception: Keeps the original speaker's first-person pronoun and possessive unchanged in the reported version.
distractors.whyFails: This keeps the original speaker's viewpoint: 'I' and 'my' still point to Tom as if Tom himself were talking, even though Anna is now passing his words on to someone else.
distractors.whyFailsId: sudut pandang penutur aslinya dibiarin utuh.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti dan kata kepemilikan penutur aslinya dibiarin utuh.

distractors.misconception: Shifts the subject pronoun but forgets to shift the corresponding possessive.
distractors.whyFails: Pronoun and possessive must shift together for the same referent; leaving 'my' unshifted while changing 'I' to 'he' creates an inconsistent reference within one sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata kepemilikannya belum digeser, rujukannya jadi campur.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti subjeknya udah digeser tapi kata kepemilikannya kelupaan.

distractors.misconception: Shifts the possessive but forgets to shift the subject pronoun.
distractors.whyFails: This is the reverse inconsistency: the subject pronoun stays as 'I' (the original speaker's perspective) while the possessive incorrectly shifts, breaking agreement within the sentence.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata gantinya belum digeser, pasangannya jadi nggak selaras.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kepemilikannya udah digeser tapi kata ganti subjeknya kelupaan.

explanation.whyCorrect: Both 'I' and 'my' shift to 'he' and 'his' because Anna is reporting Tom's words about himself from a third-person perspective.
explanation.rule: In reported speech, first/second-person pronouns and possessives shift to match the relationship between reporter and original speaker/listener.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Leaving either the pronoun or possessive unshifted (or leaving both) creates an inconsistent perspective within the same reported sentence.
explanation.howToAvoid: Before reporting, identify who originally spoke and who is reporting now, then shift every pronoun/possessive referring to the original speaker consistently.
explanation.memoryCue: Pronoun shift is separate from tense shift — check both 'I'→'he' AND 'my'→'his' together.
explanation.ruleId: Di kalimat pelaporan, kata ganti dan kata kepemilikan bergeser ngikutin sudut pandang pelapornya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Anna ngelaporin ucapan Tom soal dirinya sendiri. Jadi “I” jadi “he” dan “my” jadi “his”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Kalau kata gantinya atau kata kepemilikannya nggak digeser, sudut pandangnya jadi campur aduk.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tentuin dulu siapa yang semula ngomong dan siapa yang ngelapor sekarang.
explanation.memoryCueId: Geser kata ganti itu urusan sendiri, beda dari geser waktu. Cek dua-duanya sekaligus.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Geser kata ganti dan kata kepemilikan jadi orang ketiga waktu ngelaporin ucapan orang.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu udah bener geser waktunya, tapi kata ganti penutur aslinya dibiarin.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali siapa yang ngelapor dan siapa yang semula ngomong → geser kata gantinya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects the correct complementation pattern for reporting verbs that require a gerund or preposition + gerund (deny + gerund; apologize for + gerund).
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners apply the generic 'reporting verb + that-clause' pattern to verbs that actually require gerund complementation.
templates.reasoningOperation: Recognize the specific complementation pattern fixed to each reporting verb (deny + gerund; apologize for + gerund) rather than defaulting to 'that'.
templates.stem: He apologized ____ late to the meeting.

distractors.misconception: Applies the generic reporting pattern (verb + that-clause) to a verb requiring preposition + gerund.
distractors.whyFails: 'Apologize' is not typically followed directly by a 'that'-clause in this structure; it requires 'apologize for + gerund' to introduce the reason.
distractors.whyFailsId: “apologize” biasanya nggak langsung diikuti anak kalimat “that” di susunan ini.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola pelaporan umum kata kerja + anak kalimat that dipakai di kata kerja yang minta kata depan + bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: Uses an infinitive complement instead of the required preposition + gerund pattern.
distractors.whyFails: 'Apologize to be late' is not a standard pattern; 'apologize' needs 'for' plus a gerund to introduce the action being apologized for.
distractors.whyFailsId: “apologize to be late” bukan pola yang baku dalam Bahasa Inggris.
distractors.misconceptionId: pelengkap bentuk to dipakai ganti pola kata depan + bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: Uses the bare base form after the preposition 'for' instead of the required gerund.
distractors.whyFails: Prepositions must be followed by a gerund, not a bare verb; 'for be' is not a grammatical sequence in English.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata depan harus diikuti bentuk -ing, bukan kata kerja dasar.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja bentuk dasar dipakai sesudah kata depan “for”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Apologized for being late' correctly uses the fixed pattern apologize + for + gerund to introduce the reason for apologizing.
explanation.rule: Apologize for + gerund (reason); deny + gerund (direct object); both differ from generic 'verb + that-clause' reporting.
explanation.whyOthersFail: A 'that'-clause, bare infinitive, or bare verb after 'for' all violate apologize's fixed preposition + gerund complementation.
explanation.howToAvoid: Memorize fixed complementation patterns per reporting verb rather than assuming all reporting verbs take 'that'.
explanation.memoryCue: Apologize FOR + -ing (the reason); deny + -ing (no preposition).
explanation.ruleId: Apologize for + bentuk -ing buat nyebut alasannya; deny + bentuk -ing sebagai objek langsung. Dua-duanya beda dari pola kata kerja + anak kalimat that.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Apologized for being late” pakai pola tetap apologize + for + bentuk -ing buat nyebut alasan minta maafnya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Anak kalimat “that”, bentuk to, maupun kata kerja dasar sama-sama ngelanggar pola kata depan + bentuk -ing.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hafalin pola pelengkap tiap kata kerja pelapor, jangan nganggep semuanya bisa diikuti “that”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Apologize” FOR + bentuk -ing buat alasannya; “deny” + bentuk -ing tanpa kata depan.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pilih pola pelengkap yang pas buat kata kerja pelapor yang minta gerund (bentuk -ing). Sebagian minta kata depan dulu, baru bentuk -ing.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai pola umum kata kerja pelapor + anak kalimat “that”. Padahal kata kerja ini minta pelengkap bentuk -ing.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali pola pelengkap yang nempel di tiap kata kerja pelapor, kayak apologize for + bentuk -ing → jangan langsung pakai “that”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner recognizes that certain plural-form or river/mountain-range country names conventionally take 'the', unlike most singular country names.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners apply the general 'no article before country names' rule universally, missing fixed exceptions like plural-form country names.
templates.reasoningOperation: Recognize that this country name belongs to the fixed exception category (plural-form names) requiring 'the', rather than the general zero-article rule.
templates.stem: My cousin has lived in ____ Netherlands for almost ten years now.

distractors.misconception: Treats the country name as an ordinary countable noun needing an indefinite article.
distractors.whyFails: Country names are proper nouns and don't take indefinite articles; 'the Netherlands' is a fixed exception requiring the definite article specifically.
distractors.whyFailsId: Nama negara adalah nama diri dan tidak memakai artikel tak tentu; “the Netherlands” adalah kekecualian tetap yang khusus menuntut artikel tertentu.
distractors.misconceptionId: nama negara diperlakukan sebagai kata benda terhitung biasa yang butuh artikel tak tentu.

distractors.misconception: Applies the indefinite article rule based on the following vowel sound, ignoring that country names don't take indefinite articles at all.
distractors.whyFails: Country names do not take the indefinite article 'an'; this fixed name requires the definite article in 'the Netherlands'.
distractors.whyFailsId: Nama negara tidak memakai artikel tak tentu “an”; nama tetap ini menuntut artikel tertentu dalam bentuk “the Netherlands”.
distractors.misconceptionId: aturan artikel tak tentu diterapkan berdasarkan bunyi vokal, tanpa melihat bahwa nama negara memang tidak memakainya.

distractors.misconception: Overgeneralizes the common 'no article before country names' rule to every country name.
distractors.whyFails: 'The Netherlands' is one of a fixed set of plural-form or descriptive country names (the Philippines, the United States) that require 'the' as an exception.
distractors.whyFailsId: nama negara ini masuk kelompok kekecualian yang celahnya nggak boleh kosong.
distractors.misconceptionId: aturan umum tanpa artikel di depan nama negara diberlakukan untuk semua nama negara.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'The Netherlands' belongs to the fixed exception group of plural-form country names that require the definite article.
explanation.rule: Most country names take zero article, but plural-form names (the Netherlands, the Philippines) and names with 'United'/'Republic' take 'the'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Indefinite articles never apply to proper country names, and the zero-article default doesn't apply to this exception category.
explanation.howToAvoid: Memorize the exception list: plural-form countries and official 'United/Republic of' names always take 'the'.
explanation.memoryCue: Plural-sounding countries take 'the': the Netherlands, the Philippines, the United States.
explanation.ruleId: Kebanyakan nama negara tanpa artikel, tetapi nama berbentuk jamak seperti the Netherlands dan the Philippines, serta nama yang memuat United atau Republic, memakai “the”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “The Netherlands” termasuk kelompok kekecualian berupa nama negara berbentuk jamak yang menuntut artikel tertentu.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Artikel tak tentu tidak pernah dipakai untuk nama negara, dan aturan bawaan tanpa artikel tidak berlaku untuk kelompok kekecualian ini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hafalin daftar kekecualiannya: nama negara berbentuk jamak dan nama resmi ber-United atau ber-Republic.
explanation.memoryCueId: Nama negara yang kedengeran jamak pakai “the”: “the Netherlands”, “the Philippines”, “the United States”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu ngenalin sebagian nama negara berbentuk jamak atau bernama gugusan biasanya pakai “the”. Itu beda dari kebanyakan nama negara yang tunggal.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu menerapkan aturan umum “nama negara tanpa artikel” untuk semua kasus, sehingga melewatkan kekecualian seperti nama negara berbentuk jamak
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali bahwa nama negara ini termasuk kelompok kekecualian berbentuk jamak yang menuntut “the”, bukan aturan umum tanpa artikel

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use 'of' between a quantifier and an object pronoun, producing 'both of them' rather than the ungrammatical 'both them'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner drops 'of' before an object pronoun because 'both' can appear directly before some noun phrases.
templates.reasoningOperation: notice the object pronoun 'them' -> insert of after the quantifier -> select both of
templates.stem: I have exactly two close friends. ____ them live in different countries now, so we rarely meet in person.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' before the object pronoun
distractors.whyFails: 'Both them' is not standard English; an object pronoun requires 'both of them'.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk ini ngilangin “of” yang diwajibin di depan “them”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dihilangin di depan kata ganti objek.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' and ignores the explicitly two-person set
distractors.whyFails: 'All them' is ungrammatical, and 'all' does not match the explicitly two-person contrast targeted here.
distractors.whyFailsId: “all them” nggak sah dalam Bahasa Inggris baku.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dihilangin sekaligus ngabaikan bahwa kelompoknya jelas dua orang.

distractors.misconception: drops 'of' and reverses the affirmative meaning
distractors.whyFails: 'Neither them' is ungrammatical and would also negate the statement instead of referring to both friends.
distractors.whyFailsId: “neither” juga ngebalik makna kalimatnya jadi negatif.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dihilangin sekaligus ngebalik makna kalimatnya jadi negatif.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Both of them' correctly combines a two-person quantifier with an object pronoun.
explanation.rule: Use quantifier + of before an object pronoun: both of them, all of us, neither of you.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Each alternative either omits the required 'of' before 'them' or changes the intended quantity and polarity.
explanation.howToAvoid: If the quantifier is followed by us, you, them, or another object pronoun, place 'of' between them.
explanation.memoryCue: Pronoun ahead? Use of: both of them.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai kata jumlah + “of” sebelum kata ganti objek. Contohnya “both of them”, “all of us”, dan “neither of you”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Them” itu kata ganti objek. Jadi kata jumlahnya butuh “of” di depannya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Tiap pilihan lain ngilangin “of” yang diwajibin sebelum “them”. Dua di antaranya juga ngubah jumlah dan kutub maknanya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau kata jumlahnya diikutin “us”, “you”, atau “them”, sisipin “of” di antaranya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ada kata ganti objek di depan? Pakai “of”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai “of” di antara kata jumlah dan kata ganti objek, jadinya “both of them”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngilangin “of” di depan kata ganti objek. Alasannya “both” bisa langsung nempel di sebagian frasa benda.
templates.reasoningOperationId: perhatiin kata ganti objek “them” → sisipin “of” sesudah kata jumlahnya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects 'by' for method/means of transport or communication, distinguishing it from 'with' (instrument/tool) and 'on' (surface/device).
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners use 'with' for methods of transport or communication, transferring the instrument preposition to a means-of-doing-something context.
templates.reasoningOperation: Determine whether the sentence describes a method/means (by) or a physical tool/instrument (with) to select the correct preposition.
templates.stem: It's much cheaper to travel ____ bus than ____ taxi in this city.

distractors.misconception: Treats modes of transport as tools/instruments requiring 'with'.
distractors.whyFails: 'With' is used for instruments you hold or use directly (write with a pen), not for methods of transportation, which take 'by'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “with” dipakai buat alat yang dipegang kayak “write with a pen”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kendaraan diperlakuin sebagai alat yang minta “with”.

distractors.misconception: Confuses the fixed 'by + transport' collocation with literal physical position prepositions (on a bus vs in a taxi).
distractors.whyFails: 'On the bus' and 'in the taxi' describe physical location inside the vehicle, not the general method of travel, which uses 'by bus'/'by taxi' without an article.
distractors.whyFailsId: “On the bus” dan “in the taxi” menggambarkan posisi di dalam kendaraannya, bukan cara bepergian secara umum yang memakai “by bus” dan “by taxi” tanpa artikel.
distractors.misconceptionId: pasangan tetap buat cara bepergian ketuker sama kata depan posisi fisik.

distractors.misconception: Applies the correct preposition to only one of the two parallel transport methods.
distractors.whyFails: Both 'bus' and 'taxi' are equally methods of transport and should both take 'by', not a mix of 'by' and 'with'.
distractors.whyFailsId: dua cara bepergian yang sejajar dikasih kata depan beda.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan yang lazim cuma diterapin ke salah satu dari dua cara sejajar.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'By bus' and 'by taxi' are the fixed collocations expressing method of transport, without an article after 'by'.
explanation.rule: Use 'by' + transport noun (no article) for method of travel: by bus, by car, by plane.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'With' suits handheld instruments, not transport methods; 'on/in' describe physical position rather than general method.
explanation.howToAvoid: For general method of transport (not physical position), always use by + bare noun.
explanation.memoryCue: By bus/by car/by plane = method (no article); on the bus/in the car = physical position.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai “by” + kata benda kendaraan tanpa artikel untuk cara bepergian: by bus, by car, by plane.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “By bus” dan “by taxi” adalah pasangan kata tetap untuk menyatakan cara bepergian, tanpa artikel setelah “by”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “With” cocok buat alat yang dipegang. “On” dan “in” nggambarin posisi fisik di dalam kendaraannya, bukan caranya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Buat cara bepergian secara umum, pakai “by” + kata benda telanjang.
explanation.memoryCueId: By bus, by car, by plane untuk caranya tanpa artikel; on the bus dan in the car untuk posisi fisiknya.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pilih “by” buat cara atau sarana bepergian dan berkomunikasi. “With” buat alat, “on” buat permukaan.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “with” buat cara bepergian. Kata depan buat alat kebawa ke konteks cara ngelakuin sesuatu.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kalimatnya nyebut cara atau sarana → pilih kata depan yang lazim buat cara itu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects the correct dependent preposition following an abstract noun (solution to, not solution for/of).
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners assume the noun's dependent preposition matches the related verb's or adjective's preposition (e.g. 'solve for' influencing 'solution for').
templates.reasoningOperation: Recall the noun's own fixed dependent preposition independently of related word forms.
templates.stem: Scientists are still searching for a viable solution ____ the problem of plastic pollution.

distractors.misconception: Transfers the preposition pattern from a related phrase like 'search for' onto 'solution'.
distractors.whyFails: Although 'search for' takes 'for', the noun 'solution' has its own fixed dependent preposition 'to', unrelated to the surrounding verb's preposition.
distractors.whyFailsId: “search for” memang pakai “for”, tapi kata benda “solution” punya pasangan tetapnya sendiri.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola kata depan dari ungkapan berkaitan kayak “search for” dibawa ke “solution”.

distractors.misconception: Assumes 'of' universally links a noun to what it relates to.
distractors.whyFails: 'Solution of' is not the conventional collocation for addressing a problem; 'solution to' is the fixed pairing in this meaning.
distractors.whyFailsId: “solution of” bukan pasangan kata yang biasa buat ngejawab sebuah masalah.
distractors.misconceptionId: “of” dikira selalu bisa nyambungin kata benda sama hal yang berkaitan.

distractors.misconception: Borrows a preposition associated with 'deal with' or 'cope with' a problem.
distractors.whyFails: 'Solution with' is not a standard collocation; the noun 'solution' specifically pairs with 'to', not 'with'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “solution with” bukan pasangan kata yang baku dalam Bahasa Inggris.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan yang lekat di “deal with” dipinjem buat “solution”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Solution to' is the fixed dependent preposition pattern when a solution addresses a specific problem.
explanation.rule: Certain abstract nouns have fixed dependent prepositions that must be memorized individually (solution to, reason for, answer to).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'For', 'of', and 'with' are borrowed from other related collocations but don't match the fixed noun + preposition pairing for 'solution'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Learn noun + preposition collocations as fixed pairs, not derived from related verbs or adjectives.
explanation.memoryCue: Solution TO a problem; reason FOR a decision; answer TO a question.
explanation.ruleId: Sebagian kata benda abstrak punya kata depan tetap yang harus dihafal satu-satu. Contohnya solution to, reason for, dan answer to.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Solution to” itu pola kata depan tetap pas sebuah jalan keluar ngejawab satu masalah tertentu.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “For”, “of”, dan “with” dipinjem dari pasangan kata lain. Ketiganya nggak cocok sama pasangan tetap punya “solution”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Hafalin pasangan kata benda dan kata depannya sebagai satu kesatuan, bukan nurunin dari kata kerjanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Solution TO a problem; reason FOR a decision; answer TO a question.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pilih preposition (kata depan) tetap yang bener sesudah kata benda abstrak, yaitu solution to. Bukan solution for atau solution of.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira kata depan tetap sebuah kata benda ngikutin kata depan kata kerja yang berkaitan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: inget kembali kata depan tetap punya kata bendanya sendiri → lepas dari bentuk kata lain yang berkaitan

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner recognizes that 'regret + to-infinitive' (formal announcement of bad news) differs in meaning from 'regret + gerund' (feeling sorry about a past action).
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners assume 'regret' always takes the same complement form regardless of the intended meaning (announcing vs feeling sorry).
templates.reasoningOperation: Determine whether the sentence is a formal announcement of unwelcome news (to-infinitive) or an expression of sorrow about a past action (gerund).
templates.stem: We regret ___ you that your application has been unsuccessful.

distractors.misconception: Uses the gerund pattern (regretting a past action) where the formal-announcement meaning is intended.
distractors.whyFails: 'Regret informing' would mean feeling sorry about having already informed someone, but this sentence is a formal announcement being made right now, requiring the to-infinitive.
distractors.whyFailsId: “regret informing” berarti nyesal karena udah terlanjur ngasih tahu, padahal kabarnya baru disampein sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: pola bentuk -ing yang nyesalin tindakan lampau dipakai padahal maksudnya pemberitahuan resmi.

distractors.misconception: Uses a perfect gerund implying the informing already happened before the regret.
distractors.whyFails: 'Having informed' presents the news as already delivered before the regret arose, but this sentence is itself the act of delivering that news right now.
distractors.whyFailsId: “having informed” naruh kabarnya seolah udah selesai disampein sebelum penyesalannya muncul.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing perfect “having informed” dipakai jadi pemberitahuannya seolah udah terjadi sebelum penyesalannya.

distractors.misconception: Drops the infinitive marker 'to' entirely.
distractors.whyFails: 'Regret' requires 'to' before the base verb in this formal-announcement meaning; the bare infinitive alone is not the correct complement here.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar tanpa “to” bukan pelengkap yang pas buat “regret” di makna resmi ini.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar tanpa “to” dipakai sebagai pelengkap “regret”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Regret to inform' is the fixed formal pattern for announcing unwelcome news at the moment of speaking/writing.
explanation.rule: Regret + to-infinitive = formal announcement of bad news; regret + gerund = feeling sorry about a past action.
explanation.whyOthersFail: The gerund forms shift the meaning to sorrow about something already done, which doesn't match this live announcement context.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check whether 'regret' introduces news being delivered now (to-infinitive) or sorrow about the past (gerund).
explanation.memoryCue: Regret TO INFORM you now; regret DOING something in the past.
explanation.ruleId: Regret + bentuk to berarti nyampein kabar buruk secara resmi. Regret + bentuk -ing berarti nyesalin tindakan yang udah lewat. “Mean” dan “go on” ikut keluarga pola yang sama, tapi kartu di lesson ini cuma nguji “regret”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kalimat ini baru nyampein kabar penolakannya sekarang, jadi “regret” minta bentuk to: “to inform”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Bentuk -ing nggeser maknanya jadi penyesalan atas sesuatu yang udah terlanjur. Itu nggak cocok sama pemberitahuan yang sedang jalan ini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek “regret” di kalimatnya mbuka kabar yang baru disampein sekarang, atau penyesalan atas masa lalu.
explanation.memoryCueId: Regret TO INFORM you sekarang; regret DOING sesuatu di masa lalu.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu ngenalin “regret” + bentuk to buat nyampein kabar buruk secara resmi, beda dari “regret” + bentuk -ing yang nyesalin tindakan lampau.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngira “regret” selalu diikuti pelengkap yang sama, tanpa ngeliat maksudnya nyampein kabar atau nyesalin.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin kalimatnya nyampein kabar buruk resmi atau nyesalin tindakan lampau → pilih bentuk to atau bentuk -ing

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner uses the perfect gerund ('having + past participle') to emphasize that the gerund's action happened before the main verb's time.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners use the simple gerund even when the sentence needs to clearly mark that one action preceded another.
templates.reasoningOperation: Determine whether the timing relationship between the gerund action and the main verb needs to be explicitly marked as earlier, requiring the perfect gerund.
templates.stem: Which completion most explicitly marks the breaking as earlier than the later admission? He admitted ____ the vase.

distractors.misconception: Uses the simple gerund, which leaves the earlier timing to context instead of encoding it explicitly.
distractors.whyFails: 'Breaking' is a valid complement of 'admit', but it does not explicitly mark anteriority; the question specifically asks for the form that does.
distractors.whyFailsId: “breaking” memang sah buat “admit”, tapi urutan waktunya nggak ditegesin.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing sederhana dipakai jadi urutan waktunya diserahin ke konteks.

distractors.misconception: Uses an infinitive complement after 'admit', a verb that takes a gerund, not an infinitive.
distractors.whyFails: 'Admit' is not followed by a to-infinitive in standard English; it requires a gerund complement.
distractors.whyFailsId: “admit” nggak diikuti bentuk to di Bahasa Inggris baku, kata ini minta pelengkap -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: pelengkap bentuk to dipakai sesudah “admit” yang justru minta bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: Uses the bare base form with no verb marking at all.
distractors.whyFails: 'Admit break' has no valid grammatical function; 'admit' requires a gerund (simple or perfect), never a bare verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “admit break” nggak punya fungsi tata bahasa yang sah, dan kata kerja dasar nggak pernah diterima.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar telanjang dipakai tanpa tanda apa pun.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Having broken' explicitly encodes that the breaking preceded the admission.
explanation.rule: Perfect gerund (having + past participle) explicitly marks the gerund action as anterior to the main verb; a simple gerund may leave that timing implicit.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Breaking' leaves the sequence implicit rather than explicitly marking it; 'to break' and 'break' are invalid complements of 'admit'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Read the task constraint carefully: if it asks you to mark anteriority explicitly, choose having + past participle rather than relying on context alone.
explanation.memoryCue: Having + past participle = explicitly earlier.
explanation.ruleId: Bentuk -ing perfect having + past participle negesin tindakannya mendahului kata kerja utama. Bentuk -ing sederhana ninggalin urutannya tersirat.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Having broken” negesin bahwa pecahnya vas terjadi sebelum pengakuannya.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Breaking” ninggalin urutannya tersirat tanpa negesin. “To break” dan “break” bukan pelengkap yang sah buat “admit”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Baca syarat soalnya teliti. Kalau diminta negesin mana yang lebih dulu, pilih having + past participle.
explanation.memoryCueId: Having + past participle berarti tegas lebih dulu.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai bentuk -ing perfect having + past participle buat nekanin tindakannya terjadi lebih dulu dari kata kerja utamanya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai bentuk -ing sederhana padahal kalimatnya perlu nekanin satu tindakan mendahului tindakan lain.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek hubungan waktunya perlu ditegesin sebagai lebih dulu atau nggak → pilih bentuk -ing perfect kalau perlu

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner constructs a non-defining relative clause using a quantifier + of + relative pronoun (many of whom) to refer back to a group noun.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners use a plain relative pronoun with a separate quantifier sentence instead of the combined quantifier + of + whom/which structure.
templates.reasoningOperation: Recognize that referring to a portion of a previously mentioned plural group requires the fixed quantifier + of + relative pronoun pattern.
templates.stem: The charity has over two hundred volunteers, ____ are retired teachers.

distractors.misconception: Reverses the order of quantifier and relative pronoun.
distractors.whyFails: 'Which many' puts the relative pronoun before the quantifier, reversing the fixed pattern that places the quantifier first, before 'of' and the relative pronoun — and 'which' cannot refer to people anyway.
distractors.whyFailsId: “which many” naruh kata penghubung sebelum kata jumlah, dan “which” juga nggak bisa buat orang.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata penghubung “which” ditaruh sebelum kata jumlah, sekaligus salah pilih kata penghubung buat orang.

distractors.misconception: Scrambles the word order of the fixed quantifier + of + whom structure.
distractors.whyFails: This ordering is not a recognized English pattern; the correct sequence is quantifier + of + whom (many of whom), not whom + many of.
distractors.whyFailsId: urutan ini bukan pola yang dikenal, rangkaiannya wajib kata jumlah dulu, baru “of”.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan pola tetap kata jumlah + of + whom diacak.

distractors.misconception: Uses a personal pronoun 'them' instead of a relative pronoun, which cannot join two clauses.
distractors.whyFails: 'Them' is not a relative pronoun and cannot link the second clause grammatically to the first as a single sentence; it would create a comma splice.
distractors.whyFailsId: “them” bukan kata penghubung, jadi dua anak kalimatnya cuma nyambung koma.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti biasa “them” dipakai gantiin kata penghubung, padahal nggak bisa nyambung dua anak kalimat.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Many of whom' correctly combines the quantifier with the relative pronoun 'whom' to refer back to 'volunteers' in a non-defining clause.
explanation.rule: Quantifier + of + whom/which links a relative clause back to a portion of a previously mentioned group (many of whom, some of which).
explanation.whyOthersFail: Reordering the words breaks the fixed pattern, and 'them' is a personal pronoun that can't function as a clause-linking relative pronoun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Keep the fixed order: quantifier + of + whom (people) / which (things).
explanation.memoryCue: Many of whom / some of which — quantifier first, then 'of', then the relative pronoun.
explanation.ruleId: Kata jumlah + of + whom atau which nyambungin anak kalimat penjelas ke sebagian kelompok yang udah disebut. Contohnya many of whom dan some of which.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Many of whom” madukan kata jumlah sama kata penghubung “whom” buat nunjuk balik ke “volunteers”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Ngacak urutan katanya ngerusak pola tetapnya. “Them” itu kata ganti biasa yang nggak bisa nyambungin antar anak kalimat.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Jaga urutannya tetap: kata jumlah, terus of, terus whom buat orang atau which buat benda.
explanation.memoryCueId: Many of whom dan some of which — kata jumlah dulu, terus “of”, terus kata penghubungnya.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun anak kalimat penjelas tambahan pakai pola kata jumlah + of + kata penghubung buat nunjuk balik ke satu kelompok.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai kata penghubung biasa terus nambah kalimat berisi kata jumlah terpisah, bukan pola gabungannya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali kalimatnya nunjuk sebagian dari kelompok jamak yang udah disebut → pakai pola tetap kata jumlah + of + kata penghubung

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner combines a superlative with present perfect + 'ever' to express a life-experience superlative claim.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners use past simple after a superlative + ever construction, missing that this fixed pattern requires present perfect.
templates.reasoningOperation: Recognize the fixed superlative + ever pattern requires present perfect to express 'in my whole life up to now'.
templates.stem: This is honestly the most delicious meal I ___ ever ___.

distractors.misconception: Uses past simple twice instead of the fixed present perfect + ever pattern.
distractors.whyFails: 'Had; had' seals the experience inside a finished past, cutting the 'ever' life-claim off from the present moment.
distractors.whyFailsId: di kalimat ini bingkainya sekarang, jadi “had; had” motong klaim “ever”-nya.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lampau dipakai dua-duanya, jadi klaim sepanjang hidupnya lepas dari sekarang.

distractors.misconception: Repeats the auxiliary 'have' without the required past participle 'had' for the main verb 'eat/have (a meal)'.
distractors.whyFails: The second slot needs the past participle form of the main verb (had), not a repeated auxiliary without its main verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: bagian keduanya minta past participle kata kerja utamanya, bukan ulangan kata bantu.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu “have” diulang tanpa past participle yang dibutuhin kata kerja utamanya.

distractors.misconception: Mixes past simple auxiliary 'did' with present perfect 'have', producing an inconsistent structure.
distractors.whyFails: The fixed pattern uses a single consistent present perfect auxiliary 'have' throughout, not a mix of 'did' and 'have'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “did; have” nyampur kata bantu lampau sama perfect, jadi susunannya bentrok sendiri.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu past simple “did” dicampur sama present perfect jadi susunannya nggak selaras.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Have ever had' correctly uses present perfect throughout, matching the fixed superlative + ever life-experience pattern.
explanation.rule: Superlative + [noun] + I have ever + past participle expresses a claim that still holds now; inside a past frame the pattern shifts to 'I had ever + past participle'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Had; had' would fit a past frame ('That was the best meal I had ever had'), but this sentence starts from 'This is'; the other combinations mix auxiliary and verb inconsistently.
explanation.howToAvoid: If the claim still holds now, use present perfect; if the story is already framed in the past, use past perfect.
explanation.memoryCue: Best/worst... I have ever + past participle (not 'did ever').
explanation.ruleId: Superlative + kata benda + I have ever + past participle nyatain klaim terbaik atau terburuk sepanjang hidup yang masih berlaku. Kalau ceritanya dibingkai lampau, bentuknya jadi I had ever + past participle.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “This is” naruh klaimnya di waktu sekarang, jadi “have ever had” nyambungin pengalamannya sampai sekarang.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Di kalimat ini bingkainya sekarang, jadi bentuk lampau motong klaim yang masih berlaku. Gabungan lain nggak selaras antara kata bantu dan kata kerjanya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau klaimnya masih berlaku sampai sekarang, pakai present perfect. Kalau ceritanya udah dibingkai lampau, past perfect yang pas.
explanation.memoryCueId: Best atau worst ... I have ever + past participle. Kalau bingkainya lampau, jadi I had ever + past participle.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu maduin superlative (bentuk paling) sama present perfect dan “ever” buat nyatain pengalaman sepanjang hidup.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai bentuk lampau sesudah susunan superlative + ever. Kamu nggak lihat susunan ini minta present perfect kalau klaimnya masih berlaku sekarang.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali susunan superlative + ever → cek klaimnya masih berlaku atau udah dibingkai lampau → pilih present perfect atau past perfect

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner forms a subject question (who/what as the subject) without adding the auxiliary 'do/does', distinct from object questions.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners add 'do/does' to subject questions by over-applying the standard object-question formation rule.
templates.reasoningOperation: Determine whether the question word represents the subject (no auxiliary needed) or the object (auxiliary required) of the sentence.
templates.stem: ____ the window during the storm last night?

distractors.misconception: Adds the auxiliary 'did' as if this were an object question, following the standard question-formation rule mechanically.
