distractors.whyFails: Adding 'did' treats 'who' as if it asked about the object of the action, but here 'who' is itself the doer, so the auxiliary is slotted in mechanically where the pattern does not call for it.
distractors.whyFailsId: “did” disisipin kayak ini pertanyaan tentang objek.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu “did” ditambah kayak ini pertanyaan tentang objek.

distractors.misconception: Adds 'did' and keeps the past-tense main verb form together.
distractors.whyFails: 'Did' and 'broke' each carry their own past-tense marking, so this version stamps past time twice inside a single verb phrase.
distractors.whyFailsId: “did” dan “broke” bawa bentuk lampau dua kali.
distractors.misconceptionId: “did” ditambah tapi bentuk lampau kata kerja utamanya dipertahankan.

distractors.misconception: Uses present-tense auxiliary 'does' for a clearly past-time event ('last night').
distractors.whyFails: The present auxiliary 'does' collides with 'last night', which anchors the event firmly in the past, so the tense of this version contradicts its own time marker.
distractors.whyFailsId: “does” itu bentuk present, bentrok sama “last night”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu bentuk present dipakai buat kejadian yang jelas lampau.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Who broke the window' keeps the statement word order because 'who' is the subject performing the action, requiring no auxiliary.
explanation.rule: Subject questions (who/what as subject) use statement word order with no do/does/did auxiliary.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Adding 'did'/'does' wrongly applies the object-question rule; combining 'did' with 'broke' double-marks the past tense.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check if the question word is asking about the subject or object; subject questions skip the auxiliary entirely.
explanation.memoryCue: Subject questions: Who + verb (no do/did) — 'Who broke it?' not 'Who did break it?'
explanation.ruleId: Pertanyaan tentang subjek pakai urutan kata pernyataan, tanpa kata bantu do, does, atau did.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Who” di sini pelaku yang mecahin jendelanya. Jadi urutannya tetap kayak pernyataan, tanpa kata bantu.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Nambah did atau does berarti nerapin aturan pertanyaan tentang objek. Gabungan “did” dan “broke” nandain lampau dua kali.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dulu, ya: kata tanyanya nanya pelakunya, atau nanya yang kena?
explanation.memoryCueId: Pertanyaan tentang subjek: Who + kata kerja, tanpa do atau did.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Susun pertanyaan tentang subjek pakai who tanpa nambah do atau does.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nambah do atau does di pertanyaan tentang subjek.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kata tanyanya berkedudukan subjek atau objek → tentuin butuh kata bantu atau nggak

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner identifies and corrects a parallel structure error in a list joined by 'and', ensuring all items share the same grammatical form.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners overlook grammatical form mismatches in a list as long as each individual item sounds acceptable on its own.
templates.reasoningOperation: Check that every item in the coordinated list shares the same grammatical form (all gerunds, all infinitives, etc.).
templates.stem: Which sentence has correct parallel structure? "Her hobbies include painting, to hike, and reading."
options: Her hobbies include painting, hiking, and reading.
Her hobbies include painting, to hike, and to read.
Her hobbies include to paint, hiking, and reading.
Her hobbies include painting, to hike, and reading.

distractors.option: Her hobbies include painting, to hike, and to read.
distractors.misconception: Fixes only two of the three items, still leaving the list form inconsistent overall reasoning.
distractors.whyFails: Although two items now match (to hike, to read), 'painting' remains a gerund while the others are infinitives, so the list still isn't parallel.
distractors.whyFailsId: “painting” masih bentuk -ing sementara dua bagian lain bentuk to.
distractors.misconceptionId: cuma dua dari tiga bagiannya yang dibetulin, jadi bentuknya tetap nggak selaras.

distractors.option: Her hobbies include to paint, hiking, and reading.
distractors.misconception: Converts the first item to infinitive while leaving the other two as gerunds.
distractors.whyFails: This creates the same mismatch problem in reverse: one infinitive item among two gerund items still breaks parallel structure.
distractors.whyFailsId: satu bagian bentuk to di antara dua bagian bentuk -ing tetap ngerusak kesejajaran.
distractors.misconceptionId: bagian pertamanya diubah jadi bentuk to sementara dua lainnya dibiarin bentuk -ing.

distractors.option: Her hobbies include painting, to hike, and reading.
distractors.misconception: This is the original unedited sentence, left unchanged.
distractors.whyFails: It still mixes a gerund (painting), an infinitive (to hike), and another gerund (reading), which is the exact error being tested.
distractors.whyFailsId: kalimat ini masih nyampur bentuk -ing sama bentuk to di satu rangkaian.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimat aslinya dibiarin apa adanya tanpa perbaikan.

explanation.whyCorrect: All three items are gerunds (painting, hiking, reading), giving the list consistent grammatical form.
explanation.rule: Items joined by 'and'/'or' in a list must share the same grammatical form (parallel structure).
explanation.whyOthersFail: The other options still mix gerunds and infinitives within the same list, breaking parallelism.
explanation.howToAvoid: After writing a list, check that every item has the identical grammatical form as the first item.
explanation.memoryCue: One list, one form: all -ing, or all to + verb — never mixed.
explanation.ruleId: Bagian-bagian yang disambung “and” atau “or” di dalam satu rangkaian harus berbentuk sama.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ketiga bagiannya sama-sama bentuk -ing, yaitu “painting”, “hiking”, dan “reading”, jadi rangkaiannya sejajar.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Pilihan lain masih nyampur bentuk -ing dan bentuk to di dalam satu rangkaian. Kesejajarannya jadi tetap rusak.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sesudah nulis satu rangkaian, cek tiap bagiannya berbentuk persis sama kayak bagian pertama.
explanation.memoryCueId: Satu rangkaian, satu bentuk: semuanya -ing, atau semuanya to + kata kerja.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu ngenalin dan mbetulin kesalahan kesejajaran bentuk di rangkaian yang disambung “and”. Semua bagiannya harus berbentuk sama.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngelewatin ketidaksamaan bentuk di dalam satu rangkaian, selama tiap bagiannya kedengeran wajar kalau berdiri sendiri.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek tiap bagian di rangkaian itu berbentuk sama atau nggak → semuanya bentuk -ing, atau semuanya bentuk to

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects 'so that' (+ clause with a modal) over 'in order to' (+ bare infinitive) when the following structure is a full clause with a different subject.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners use 'in order to' before a full clause with its own subject and modal verb, a pattern reserved for 'so that'.
templates.reasoningOperation: Check whether the purpose clause has its own subject (requiring so that) or shares the main subject (allowing in order to + infinitive).
templates.stem: She whispered the instructions ____ the other students wouldn't hear.

distractors.misconception: Uses the infinitive-purpose connector before a full clause with a different subject.
distractors.whyFails: 'In order to' must be followed by a bare infinitive with the same subject as the main clause, but here the purpose clause has its own subject ('the other students').
distractors.whyFailsId: “in order to” minta subjek yang sama kayak induk kalimatnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: penghubung tujuan bentuk “to” dipakai di depan anak kalimat bersubjek beda.

distractors.misconception: Uses another infinitive-purpose connector requiring the same subject, mismatching the different-subject clause.
distractors.whyFails: Like 'in order to', 'so as to' needs a bare infinitive with the same subject as the main clause, not a full clause with a new subject.
distractors.whyFailsId: “so as to” minta kata kerja dasar tanpa subjek baru.
distractors.misconceptionId: penghubung tujuan bentuk “to” lainnya dipakai padahal subjeknya beda.

distractors.misconception: Uses a preposition that cannot introduce a full purpose clause.
distractors.whyFails: 'For' would need to be followed by a noun phrase, not a full clause with subject and modal verb like 'the other students wouldn't hear'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “for” cuma bisa diikutin frasa benda.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan dipakai padahal kata itu nggak bisa buka anak kalimat tujuan utuh.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'So that' correctly introduces a purpose clause with its own subject ('the other students') and modal verb ('wouldn't').
explanation.rule: So that + full clause (different subject possible); in order to/so as to + bare infinitive (same subject only).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'In order to' and 'so as to' require the same subject and a bare infinitive, not a separate subject and modal; 'for' can't introduce a full clause.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check if the purpose clause has a different subject from the main clause — if so, use 'so that', not 'in order to'.
explanation.memoryCue: Different subject in the purpose clause = so that; same subject = in order to + infinitive.
explanation.ruleId: “So that” diikutin anak kalimat utuh dan subjeknya boleh beda. “In order to” dan “so as to” diikutin kata kerja dasar dengan subjek yang sama.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Anak kalimat tujuannya punya subjek sendiri, yaitu “the other students”. “So that” yang bisa nampung itu.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “In order to” dan “so as to” minta subjek yang sama plus kata kerja dasar. “For” nggak bisa buka anak kalimat utuh.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dulu, ya: subjek anak kalimat tujuannya beda dari induk kalimatnya?
explanation.memoryCueId: Subjek beda pakai “so that”; subjek sama pakai “in order to”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pilih “so that” yang diikutin anak kalimat bermodal ketika subjeknya beda dari induk kalimat.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai “in order to” di depan anak kalimat utuh yang punya subjek dan modal sendiri.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek anak kalimat tujuannya punya subjek sendiri atau berbagi subjek → pilih penghubung tujuan yang cocok

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner selects a formal addition connector ('furthermore') appropriate for academic/written register, distinguishing it from informal equivalents.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners use informal addition connectors like 'also' or 'plus' in a clearly formal academic context.
templates.reasoningOperation: Match the connector's formality level to the register signaled by the surrounding academic context.
templates.stem: Which formal conjunctive adverb best completes this academic passage? The study's sample size was too small to generalize the findings. ____, the participants were not randomly selected, further weakening the results.

distractors.misconception: Selects a conversational addition phrase instead of a formal conjunctive adverb.
distractors.whyFails: 'What's more' adds information, but its conversational tone does not meet the explicitly academic register required by the prompt.
distractors.whyFailsId: “what’s more” memang nambah keterangan, tapi nadanya percakapan dan soalnya minta ragam akademik.
distractors.misconceptionId: ungkapan penambahan percakapan dipilih gantiin conjunctive adverb yang resmi.

distractors.misconception: Uses a casual spoken connector in a formal academic passage.
distractors.whyFails: 'Plus' is informal and is not the formal conjunctive adverb requested by the question.
distractors.whyFailsId: “plus” bernada santai, bukan conjunctive adverb resmi yang diminta soalnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: penghubung lisan yang santai dipakai di bacaan akademik yang resmi.

distractors.misconception: Uses a coordinating conjunction instead of the requested conjunctive adverb.
distractors.whyFails: 'And' is a conjunction, not a conjunctive adverb, and therefore fails the explicit grammatical category in the prompt.
distractors.whyFailsId: “and” itu conjunction, bukan conjunctive adverb yang secara tegas diminta soalnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: conjunction setara dipakai gantiin conjunctive adverb yang diminta.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Furthermore' is a formal conjunctive adverb used to add a related supporting point in academic prose.
explanation.rule: Formal conjunctive adverbs of addition include furthermore and moreover; conversational alternatives include plus and what is more.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'What's more' and 'Plus' do not match the requested academic register, while 'And' is not a conjunctive adverb.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check both dimensions named in the prompt: grammatical category and register. A connector can express addition yet still fail one of those constraints.
explanation.memoryCue: Academic addition adverb: furthermore or moreover.
explanation.ruleId: Conjunctive adverb penambahan yang resmi antara lain furthermore dan moreover. Padanan percakapannya antara lain plus dan what is more.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Furthermore” itu conjunctive adverb resmi buat nambah satu butir pendukung di tulisan akademik.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “What’s more” dan “Plus” nggak cocok sama ragam akademik yang diminta. “And” bukan conjunctive adverb.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dua hal yang disebut soalnya: jenis katanya dan ragam bahasanya. Penghubung bisa bermakna nambah tapi tetap gagal di salah satunya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Penambahan buat ragam akademik: furthermore atau moreover.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu milih conjunctive adverb penambahan yang resmi buat ragam tulisan akademik, beda dari padanan santainya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu pakai penghubung penambahan yang santai kayak also atau plus di konteks akademik yang jelas resmi.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cocokin tingkat keresmian penghubungnya sama ragam yang ditandai konteks akademiknya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner applies subject-auxiliary inversion after a fronted negative adverbial ('Never', 'Rarely', 'Not only') for emphatic formal style.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners front the negative adverbial for emphasis but keep normal statement word order instead of inverting subject and auxiliary.
templates.reasoningOperation: Recognize that fronting a negative/restrictive adverbial for emphasis triggers obligatory subject-auxiliary inversion.
templates.stem: ____ such a disorganized meeting before — nothing was decided at all.

distractors.misconception: Fronts the negative adverbial without applying the required subject-auxiliary inversion.
distractors.whyFails: In this version the auxiliary 'have' is already there but stays behind the subject; fronted 'Never' obligatorily moves that auxiliary in front of the subject.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata bantu “have” udah ada tapi tetap di belakang subjek, padahal “Never” di depan mewajibinnya maju.
distractors.misconceptionId: keterangan negatifnya dimajuin, tapi kata bantu “have” yang udah ada dibiarin di belakang subjek.

distractors.misconception: Fronts 'Never' with no auxiliary at all, ignoring both the inversion rule and the need for 'have' with 'before'.
distractors.whyFails: Besides missing the inversion, present perfect ('have attended') is needed for 'never...before' experience statements, and the auxiliary is absent entirely.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata bantunya nggak ada sama sekali, padahal makna “never before” minta bentuk present perfect.
distractors.misconceptionId: “Never” dimajuin tanpa kata bantu sama sekali, aturan pembalikan dan kebutuhan “have” sama-sama diabaikan.

distractors.misconception: Places 'never' after the auxiliary instead of at the very front of the sentence.
distractors.whyFails: For this emphatic pattern, 'Never' must be the fronted first word, with the auxiliary and subject inverted after it, not 'have' first.
distractors.whyFailsId: di pola penekanan ini “Never” wajib jadi kata pertama, bukan kata bantunya.
distractors.misconceptionId: “never” ditaruh sesudah kata bantunya, bukan di posisi paling depan kalimat.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Never have I attended' correctly fronts 'Never' and inverts the auxiliary 'have' before the subject 'I', the required emphatic pattern.
explanation.rule: Fronting negative/restrictive adverbials (never, rarely, not only, seldom) for emphasis requires subject-auxiliary inversion.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Skipping inversion, omitting the auxiliary, or misordering 'never' and 'have' all violate the fixed emphatic inversion pattern.
explanation.howToAvoid: Whenever a negative adverbial is fronted for emphasis, immediately invert with an auxiliary before the subject.
explanation.memoryCue: Never + auxiliary + subject: 'Never have I...', 'Rarely does she...'.
explanation.ruleId: Majuin keterangan negatif atau pembatas kayak never, rarely, not only, dan seldom demi penekanan mewajibin pembalikan subjek dan kata bantunya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Never have I attended” majuin “Never” terus mbalik kata bantu “have” ke depan subjek “I”. Itu pola penekanan yang diwajibin.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Ngelewatin pembalikannya, ngilangin kata bantunya, atau salah nyusun letak “never” dan “have” sama-sama ngelanggar pola bakunya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tiap keterangan negatif dimajuin demi penekanan, langsung balik kata bantunya ke depan subjek.
explanation.memoryCueId: Never + kata bantu + subjek: “Never have I ...”, “Rarely does she ...”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nerapin pembalikan subjek dan kata bantu sesudah keterangan negatif dimajuin, kayak Never, Rarely, dan Not only.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu majuin keterangan negatifnya demi penekanan tapi tetap pakai urutan pernyataan biasa, tanpa mbalik subjek dan kata bantunya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali keterangan negatif atau pembatas yang dimajuin → wajib balik kata bantu ke depan subjek

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Learner constructs the 'Such + be + subject + that' fronted-emphasis pattern for dramatic literary/formal effect.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learners keep 'such' in its normal pre-noun position instead of fronting the whole predicate for emphatic inversion.
templates.reasoningOperation: Recognize the fixed fronted pattern 'Such + was/were + subject + that + result clause' as an alternative to the standard 'The impact was such that...'.
templates.stem: ____ of the earthquake that entire buildings collapsed within seconds.

distractors.misconception: Fronts 'such' but fails to invert the verb 'was' before the subject.
distractors.whyFails: This emphatic pattern requires full inversion of verb and subject after fronted 'such' (Such was the impact), not just fronting 'such' alone.
distractors.whyFailsId: pola ini minta pembalikan penuh kata kerja dan subjek sesudah “such” dimajuin.
distractors.misconceptionId: “such” udah dimajuin tapi kata kerja “was” nggak dibalik ke depan subjeknya.

distractors.misconception: Keeps normal subject-first order and misplaces 'such' mid-sentence.
distractors.whyFails: This word order doesn't match any grammatical English pattern; the fixed emphatic structure requires 'Such' to start the sentence, followed immediately by the verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: “The impact such was” mempertahankan subjek di depan dan menyelipkan “such” di tengah, sehingga tidak ada pemajuan maupun pembalikan sama sekali.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan biasa dengan subjek di depan dipertahanin dan “such” ditaruh di tengah.

distractors.misconception: Treats the sentence as a yes/no question by fronting only the verb.
distractors.whyFails: This produces question word order, but the sentence is a dramatic statement, not a question; 'such' must be the very first fronted word.
distractors.whyFailsId: susunan ini keluar sebagai urutan pertanyaan, padahal kalimatnya pernyataan dramatis.
distractors.misconceptionId: kalimatnya diperlakukan sebagai kalimat tanya dengan majuin kata kerjanya saja.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Such was the impact' correctly fronts 'such' with full subject-verb inversion, the fixed literary emphatic pattern.
explanation.rule: Such + was/were + subject + that + result clause is a fixed formal/literary inversion pattern for dramatic emphasis.
explanation.whyOthersFail: Partial fronting, misplaced 'such', or question-style inversion all fail to reproduce this exact fixed emphatic structure.
explanation.howToAvoid: Treat 'Such was/were + subject' as a memorized fixed opening chunk, not something to build word-by-word.
explanation.memoryCue: Such was the impact that... — 'such' leads, verb follows immediately.
explanation.ruleId: Such + was atau were + subjek + that + anak kalimat akibat itu pola pembalikan tetap di ragam resmi atau sastra.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Such was the impact” majuin “such” dengan pembalikan penuh antara kata kerja dan subjeknya. Itu pola penekanan sastra yang udah tetap.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Pemajuan setengah jalan, letak “such” yang keliru, atau pembalikan bergaya pertanyaan sama-sama gagal ngasilin susunan tetap ini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Perlakukan “Such was” atau “Such were” + subjek sebagai satu bukaan tetap yang dihafal, bukan susunan yang dirakit kata per kata.
explanation.memoryCueId: Such was the impact that ... — “such” memimpin, kata kerjanya langsung nyusul.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun pola penekanan Such + be + subjek + that buat kesan dramatis di ragam sastra atau resmi.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nahan “such” di posisi biasanya sebelum kata benda, bukan majuin seluruh predikatnya buat pembalikan yang nekanin.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali pola tetap Such + was atau were + subjek + that + anak kalimat akibat → pakai sebagai bentuk lain dari “The impact was such that ...”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: A habitual action with a third-person singular subject uses present simple -s.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner keeps the bare form 'drink' for a third-person singular subject, or slips into the -ing form or the past form even though the sentence describes a present habit.
templates.reasoningOperation: find the routine marker 'every morning' -> identify the third-person singular subject -> add -s to the present-simple verb
templates.stem: These days my brother ___ coffee every morning.

distractors.misconception: base-form overuse
distractors.whyFails: The subject is third-person singular.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar, padahal subjeknya orang ketiga tunggal.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar dipakai berlebihan.

distractors.misconception: progressive confusion
distractors.whyFails: No auxiliary is present and the sentence describes a habit.
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak ada kata bantu, dan kalimatnya soal kebiasaan.
distractors.misconceptionId: tertukar sama bentuk yang sedang berlangsung.

distractors.misconception: past-tense confusion
distractors.whyFails: 'These days' fixes the sentence in the present, so the past form does not fit here.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk lampau, padahal “these days” nunjuk sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: tertukar sama bentuk lampau.

explanation.whyCorrect: A habitual action with a third-person singular subject uses present simple -s.
explanation.rule: Present simple affirmative: he/she/it + base verb + -s/-es.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Drink' misses third-person -s; 'drinking' needs an auxiliary and describes a different aspect; 'drank' moves the routine into the past.
explanation.howToAvoid: Underline the subject and the routine marker before choosing. With he, she, or it in a present routine, check the verb for -s/-es.
explanation.memoryCue: He, she, it: the present-simple verb gets -s.
explanation.ruleId: Present simple positif buat he, she, dan it. Kata kerjanya dapat akhiran -s atau -es.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “My brother” sama kayak he. Kebiasaan tiap pagi, jadi kata kerjanya “drinks”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Drink” nggak ada -s. “Drinking” butuh kata bantu. “Drank” malah mundur ke masa lalu.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tandai subjek dan kata waktunya dulu. Kalau he, she, atau it, cek akhiran -s.
explanation.memoryCueId: He, she, it: kata kerjanya dapat -s.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kebiasaan dengan subjek he, she, atau it pakai kata kerja plus -s
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang lupa akhiran -s buat he, she, atau it. Kadang malah kepakai bentuk -ing atau bentuk lampau.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari kata petunjuk kebiasaan “every morning” → lihat subjeknya → tambahin -s

templates.pedagogicalObjective: The pronoun they takes the plural form are.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner pairs 'they' with a be-form that belongs to another subject, such as 'am' or 'is', or leaves 'be' in its bare form.
templates.reasoningOperation: match the subject pronoun 'they' to the present-tense forms of be -> select are
templates.stem: They ___ at home today.

distractors.misconception: first-person be
distractors.whyFails: am is used with I, not they.
distractors.whyFailsId: dipakai bareng I, bukan bareng they.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk be buat orang pertama.

distractors.misconception: singular be
distractors.whyFails: is is not used with they.
distractors.whyFailsId: buat satu orang, sedangkan they itu jamak.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk be buat subjek tunggal.

distractors.misconception: base form
distractors.whyFails: be is not the finite form needed here.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar, nggak bisa jadi kata kerja utama.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar.

explanation.whyCorrect: The pronoun they takes the plural form are.
explanation.rule: Present tense of be: I am; he/she/it is; you/we/they are.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Am' belongs with I; 'is' belongs with a singular third-person subject; bare 'be' cannot act as the finite present verb here.
explanation.howToAvoid: Say the short pair aloud before completing the sentence: I am, he/she/it is, you/we/they are.
explanation.memoryCue: They always pairs with are in the present.
explanation.ruleId: Bentuk be sekarang: I am. He, she, it is. You, we, they are.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “They” itu jamak. Bentuk be buat jamak ya “are”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Am” punyanya I. “Is” buat satu orang. “Be” bentuk dasar, nggak bisa jalan sendiri.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sebut pasangannya dulu: “I am”, “she is”, “they are”.
explanation.memoryCueId: “They” selalu sama “are”: “they are at home”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kata ganti they pakai bentuk jamak are
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang masangin they sama am atau is. Kadang be dibiarin bentuk dasar.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cocokin they sama bentuk be sekarang → pilih are

templates.pedagogicalObjective: A plural noun phrase, two books, requires are.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner keeps singular 'is' after 'there' even though the real subject 'two books' is plural, or reaches for the bare form 'be' or the past form 'was'.
templates.reasoningOperation: look past 'there' to the noun phrase that follows -> identify 'two books' as plural -> select are
templates.stem: There ___ two books on the table.

distractors.misconception: singular agreement
distractors.whyFails: Two books is plural.
distractors.whyFailsId: buat satu benda, sedangkan “two books” lebih dari satu.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk tunggal dipakai buat benda jamak.

distractors.misconception: base form
distractors.whyFails: be cannot serve as the finite verb here.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar, nggak bisa jadi kata kerja utama.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar.

distractors.misconception: past tense
distractors.whyFails: The sentence describes the present situation.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk lampau, padahal kalimatnya soal keadaan sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lampau.

explanation.whyCorrect: A plural noun phrase, two books, requires are.
explanation.rule: There are + plural noun; there is + singular noun.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Is' and 'was' use singular agreement, while bare 'be' is not a finite present verb. The plural phrase 'two books' requires 'are'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Do not make the verb agree with 'there'. Look at the first noun after the verb and decide whether it is singular or plural.
explanation.memoryCue: There are + plural; there is + singular.
explanation.ruleId: There are plus kata benda jamak. There is plus kata benda tunggal.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Bendanya “two books”, jumlahnya lebih dari satu. Jadi pakai “are”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Is” dan “was” buat satu benda. “Be” nggak bisa berdiri sendiri di sini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Jangan cocokin kata kerjanya sama “there”. Lihat benda pertama sesudahnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Banyak: “there are”. Satu: “there is”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Frasa benda jamak kayak two books pakai are
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang pakai is sesudah there, padahal bendanya lebih dari satu. Kadang malah kepakai be atau was.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lewati kata “there” → lihat benda sesudahnya → tentuin tunggal atau jamak

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Her modifies the noun brother to show possession.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner puts a subject, object, or stand-alone possessive pronoun in front of the noun, a position that only a possessive adjective like 'her' can fill.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify Anna as the female owner -> notice that 'brother' follows the blank -> select the possessive adjective her
templates.stem: Anna is my friend. ___ brother is a doctor.

distractors.misconception: subject pronoun
distractors.whyFails: She cannot directly modify brother.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk subjek, nggak bisa langsung nerangin “brother”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti subjek.

distractors.misconception: possessive pronoun
distractors.whyFails: Hers stands alone and is not followed by a noun.
distractors.whyFailsId: berdiri sendiri, nggak pernah diikuti kata benda.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti kepemilikan mandiri.

distractors.misconception: object pronoun
distractors.whyFails: Him is an object pronoun.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk objek, bukan kata kepemilikan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti objek.

explanation.whyCorrect: Her modifies the noun brother to show possession.
explanation.rule: Possessive adjective before a noun: my, your, his, her, its, our, their.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'She' is a subject, 'hers' replaces a noun, and 'him' is an object; only 'her' can directly modify 'brother'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check whether a noun comes immediately after the blank. If it does, use a possessive adjective such as my, his, her, or their.
explanation.memoryCue: Her + noun; hers stands alone.
explanation.ruleId: Sebelum kata benda pakai kata kepemilikan. Contohnya my, your, his, her, its, our, their.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Sesudah bagian kosong ada kata benda “brother”. “Her” bikin jelas brother-nya punya Anna.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “She” itu subjek. “Hers” berdiri sendiri. “Him” itu objek.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau sesudahnya masih ada kata benda, jangan pakai “hers”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Her plus kata benda; hers jalan sendiri.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai kata kepemilikan her buat nunjukin brother-nya punya Anna
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang naruh she, hers, atau him di depan kata benda. Padahal posisi itu buat kata kepemilikan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali Anna sebagai pemiliknya → lihat “brother” sesudah bagian kosongnya → pilih kata kepemilikan

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Can expresses present ability.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner fills the ability slot with 'be', 'do', or 'have' instead of the modal 'can', the only one of the four that pairs directly with a bare verb to express ability.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the meaning as present ability -> choose the modal can -> keep the following verb swim in base form
templates.stem: My sister ___ swim, but she cannot drive.

distractors.misconception: be verb
distractors.whyFails: Am does not express ability with the base verb swim.
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak nyatain kemampuan bareng bentuk dasar “swim”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja be.

distractors.misconception: do auxiliary
distractors.whyFails: Do does not form an ability statement here.
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak bikin kalimat kemampuan di sini.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu do.

distractors.misconception: possession
distractors.whyFails: Have expresses possession or other meanings, not ability.
distractors.whyFailsId: artinya punya atau ngalamin, bukan mampu.
distractors.misconceptionId: tertukar sama makna punya.

explanation.whyCorrect: Can expresses present ability.
explanation.rule: Modal can + base verb expresses ability.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Am' cannot directly precede base 'swim'; 'do' does not express ability; 'have' changes the meaning to possession or experience.
explanation.howToAvoid: When the sentence means 'is able to', use can followed immediately by the base verb, with no 'to' and no -s.
explanation.memoryCue: Can + base verb: can swim, can drive.
explanation.ruleId: Can plus kata kerja dasar buat nyatain kemampuan. Tanpa to, tanpa -s.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Kalimat ini soal bisa atau nggak bisa. “Can swim” artinya mampu berenang.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Am” nggak bisa langsung ketemu “swim”. “Do” nggak nyatain kemampuan. “Have” artinya punya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau maknanya mampu, pakai can lalu kata kerja dasarnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Can plus kata kerja dasar: can swim, can drive.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kata can nyatain kemampuan yang berlaku sekarang
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang ngisi bagian kemampuan pakai be, do, atau have.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali maknanya sebagai kemampuan → pilih can → biarin kata kerjanya bentuk dasar

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Construct a mixed conditional in which an unreal past decision controls a hypothetical future event.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner forces both clauses into the same time frame and loses the past-to-future relationship.
templates.reasoningOperation: date the unreal condition in the past -> date the consequence in the future -> combine past perfect with would be + -ing
templates.stem: Which completion presents the start as something that would still be under way on that future day? If the board had approved the budget last month, construction ___ next Monday.

distractors.misconception: moves the result into the unreal past
distractors.whyFails: This is correct English — 'would have' can point to a future date that is now impossible — but it presents the start as a single completed event rather than something under way on that day.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would have” di sini sah, tapi dimulainya jadi satu kejadian tuntas, bukan yang sedang jalan.
distractors.misconceptionId: akibatnya dipindahin ke masa lalu yang nggak nyata.

distractors.misconception: treats the future result as real despite the unreal past condition
distractors.whyFails: The budget was not approved, so the future start is hypothetical and needs 'would', not 'will'.
distractors.whyFailsId: anggarannya nggak disetujui, jadi mulainya cuma dibayangin dan minta “would”.
distractors.misconceptionId: akibat masa depannya diperlakukan nyata walaupun syarat lampaunya nggak nyata.

distractors.misconception: uses simple past for an explicitly future consequence
distractors.whyFails: Simple past conflicts with 'next Monday' and fails to mark the hypothetical result.
distractors.whyFailsId: past simple bentrok sama “next Monday” dan nggak nandain akibatnya cuma dibayangin.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple dipakai buat akibat yang jelas ada di masa depan.

explanation.whyCorrect: The unreal approval belongs to last month, while the hypothetical start belongs to next Monday; 'would be starting' preserves that cross-time relationship.
explanation.rule: A mixed conditional may combine if + past perfect for an unreal past cause with would + infinitive/continuous for a present or future result.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Would have started' puts the result in the past; 'will start' makes it real; 'started' conflicts with the future time marker.
explanation.howToAvoid: Draw two points on a timeline—one for the condition and one for the result—before choosing the verb forms.
explanation.memoryCue: Past cause, future result: if had done, would be doing.
explanation.ruleId: Mixed conditional bisa madukan if + past perfect buat sebab lampau yang nggak nyata. Akibat masa kini atau masa depannya pakai would + kata kerja dasar atau bentuk berkelanjutan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Persetujuan yang nggak nyata itu ada di bulan lalu, sedangkan pembangunan yang dibayangin ada di Senin depan. “Would be starting” jagain hubungan lintas waktu itu.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Would have started” mindahin akibatnya ke masa lalu, “will start” bikin akibatnya nyata, dan “started” bentrok sama waktu masa depannya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Gambar dua titik di garis waktu, satu buat syaratnya dan satu buat akibatnya, sebelum milih bentuk kata kerjanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Sebab lampau dan akibat masa depan: if had done, would be doing.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun mixed conditional yang keputusan lampaunya nggak nyata dan ngendaliin kejadian masa depan yang dibayangin.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu maksa kedua anak kalimatnya di kerangka waktu yang sama, jadi hubungan lampau ke masa depannya hilang.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tandai syarat nggak nyatanya di masa lalu → tandai akibatnya di masa depan → gabungin past perfect sama would be + bentuk -ing

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use a modal perfect progressive to deduce that an activity was in progress at a specific past moment.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner notices past evidence but ignores the ongoing-at-that-moment meaning and chooses a completed-action form.
templates.reasoningOperation: evaluate the evidence strength -> locate the past reference point -> mark the deduced activity as ongoing with must have been + -ing
templates.stem: At 9 p.m. the office lights were on and keyboards could be heard, so the team ___ late at that moment.

distractors.misconception: uses a completed-event deduction instead of an ongoing past activity
distractors.whyFails: The phrase 'at that moment' and the audible activity frame the work as in progress, which requires the progressive form.
distractors.whyFailsId: “at that moment” dan suara kegiatannya mbingkai pekerjaannya sedang jalan, jadi butuh bentuk berkelanjutan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesimpulan soal kejadian tuntas dipakai gantiin kegiatan lampau yang sedang jalan.

distractors.misconception: changes evidence-based deduction into present advice or expectation
distractors.whyFails: 'Should work' neither refers to the observed past moment nor expresses a confident deduction from evidence.
distractors.whyFailsId: “should work” nggak nunjuk saat lampau yang diamati dan nggak nyatain kesimpulan dari bukti.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesimpulan berdasarkan bukti diubah jadi nasihat atau harapan masa kini.

distractors.misconception: reverses the polarity of the evidence
distractors.whyFails: The lights and keyboard sounds support, rather than rule out, the conclusion that the team was working.
distractors.whyFailsId: lampu nyala dan suara papan ketik justru ndukung kesimpulan bahwa timnya kerja.
distractors.misconceptionId: arah kesimpulan dari buktinya dibalik.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Must have been working' combines strong deduction, past reference, and an activity in progress at 9 p.m.
explanation.rule: For a strong deduction about an activity in progress at a past time, use must have been + verb-ing.
explanation.whyOthersFail: The simple perfect loses the ongoing viewpoint; 'should' changes the function; 'cannot' contradicts the evidence.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check three layers separately: certainty, time, and whether the activity is complete or in progress.
explanation.memoryCue: Strong evidence + ongoing past = must have been working.
explanation.ruleId: Buat kesimpulan kuat soal kegiatan yang sedang jalan di satu saat lampau, pakai must have been + kata kerja -ing.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Must have been working” madukan kesimpulan kuat, acuan waktu lampau, dan kegiatan yang sedang jalan jam sembilan malam.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Bentuk perfect sederhana kehilangan sudut pandang sedang jalan, “should” ngubah fungsinya, dan “cannot” bertentangan sama buktinya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek tiga lapis terpisah: tingkat keyakinannya, waktunya, dan kegiatannya udah tuntas atau masih jalan.
explanation.memoryCueId: Bukti kuat plus kegiatan lampau yang sedang jalan: must have been working.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai modal perfect bentuk berkelanjutan buat nyimpulin satu kegiatan sedang jalan di satu saat lampau.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu liat buktinya di masa lalu tapi ngabaikan makna sedang jalan saat itu, terus milih bentuk yang nandain tindakan tuntas.
templates.reasoningOperationId: nilai kekuatan buktinya → temukan titik acuan lampaunya → tandai kegiatannya sebagai sedang jalan pakai must have been + bentuk -ing

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Apply subject-auxiliary inversion when a restrictive 'only' phrase is fronted for formal emphasis.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner fronts 'only after/by/when' but keeps ordinary subject-verb order.
templates.reasoningOperation: detect the fronted restrictive 'only' phrase -> identify the tense -> supply an auxiliary before the subject
templates.stem: Only after the second audit ___ the scale of the error.

distractors.misconception: keeps ordinary statement order after a fronted restrictive phrase
distractors.whyFails: 'The board understood' keeps plain statement order with no auxiliary at all, so the signal carried by the fronted 'Only after...' phrase is never acted on.
distractors.whyFailsId: urutan pernyataan biasa dipertahanin tanpa kata bantu, jadi isyarat “Only after” di depan nggak ditindaklanjuti.
distractors.misconceptionId: urutan pernyataan biasa dipertahanin sesudah frasa pembatas dimajuin.

distractors.misconception: inverts the lexical verb directly
distractors.whyFails: English requires do-support here; the lexical verb stays in base form after the auxiliary.
distractors.whyFailsId: “understood the board” mbalik kata kerja utamanya, bukan kata bantunya, jadi susunannya rusak.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja utamanya langsung dibalik.

distractors.misconception: adds emphatic do but does not invert it with the subject
distractors.whyFails: The auxiliary is present but remains after the subject, so the required inversion has not occurred.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata bantunya ada tapi tetap berdiri sesudah subjek, jadi pembalikannya belum terjadi.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu penegas ditambahin tapi nggak dibalik sama subjeknya.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Only after the second audit did the board understand...' correctly places the past auxiliary before the subject and leaves 'understand' in base form.
explanation.rule: When a restrictive phrase beginning with only is fronted, invert auxiliary and subject in the main clause: Only after X did + subject + base verb.
explanation.whyOthersFail: The alternatives either keep normal order, invert the lexical verb, or fail to move the auxiliary before the subject.
explanation.howToAvoid: Treat fronted 'Only after/by/when...' like a signal to build question-style auxiliary-subject order in the following main clause.
explanation.memoryCue: Only after... did the subject + base verb.
explanation.ruleId: Waktu frasa pembatas yang dibuka “only” dimajuin, balik kata bantu dan subjek di induk kalimatnya. Polanya: Only after X did + subjek + kata kerja dasar.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Only after” di depan maksa “did” naik ke depan “the board”, dan “understand” tetap bentuk dasar.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Pilihan lain tetap pakai urutan biasa, mbalik kata kerja utamanya, atau nggak mindahin kata bantunya ke depan subjek.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Perlakukan “Only after”, “Only by”, dan “Only when” yang dimajuin sebagai isyarat. Susun urutan kata bantu dan subjek kayak di kalimat tanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Only after ... did + subjek + kata kerja dasar.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nerapin pembalikan subjek dan kata bantu waktu frasa pembatas berawalan “only” dimajuin demi penekanan resmi.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu majuin “only after”, “only by”, atau “only when” tapi tetap pakai urutan subjek dan kata kerja biasa.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali frasa pembatas berawalan “only” yang dimajuin → tentuin tense-nya → hadirin kata bantu sebelum subjeknya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Construct a pseudo-cleft with a fused 'what' clause as subject and a focused complement after 'be'.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner blends an it-cleft with a what-cleft or makes the verb agree with a nearby plural noun rather than the whole what-clause.
templates.reasoningOperation: recognize the initial what-clause as one subject unit -> choose singular agreement -> place the focused complement after be
templates.stem: What the team needed most ___ a clear decision.

distractors.misconception: makes the verb agree with the nearby plural noun team
distractors.whyFails: The subject is the entire singular idea 'What the team needed most', so singular 'was' is required.
distractors.whyFailsId: Pilihan “were” menyesuaikan kata kerjanya dengan “team”, padahal subjeknya seluruh anak kalimat “What the team needed most”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya dicocokin sama kata benda jamak terdekat, yaitu team.

distractors.misconception: inserts an it-cleft linker into a pseudo-cleft
distractors.whyFails: A pseudo-cleft links the what-clause directly to its focus with 'be'; it does not add 'that'.
distractors.whyFailsId: pola ini nyambungin anak kalimat what langsung ke bagian yang ditonjolin, tanpa nambah “that”.
distractors.misconceptionId: penghubung milik it-cleft disisipin ke pola anak kalimat what.

distractors.misconception: adds a dummy cleft subject and creates two competing subjects
distractors.whyFails: The what-clause already functions as the subject, so adding 'it' makes the structure ungrammatical.
distractors.whyFailsId: anak kalimat what udah jadi subjek, jadi nambah “it” bikin susunannya nggak sah.
distractors.misconceptionId: subjek boneka ditambahin jadi muncul dua subjek yang saling berebut.

explanation.whyCorrect: The whole what-clause is a singular subject, and 'was' links it directly to the focused complement 'a clear decision'.
explanation.rule: Pseudo-cleft: What + clause + be + focused element. Treat the fused what-clause as a single subject unit.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Were' follows the wrong noun; 'that was' and 'it was' incorrectly import pieces of an it-cleft.
explanation.howToAvoid: Bracket the whole 'What ...' clause before checking agreement; do not let a noun inside that bracket control the verb.
explanation.memoryCue: What we needed was X—one what-clause, one singular idea.
explanation.ruleId: Pola penekanan pakai what: What + anak kalimat + be + bagian yang ditonjolin. Anak kalimat what itu satu kesatuan subjek.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Seluruh anak kalimat what jadi satu subjek tunggal, dan “was” nyambungin langsung ke “a clear decision”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Were” ngikutin kata benda yang keliru. “That was” dan “it was” nyelipin potongan pola it-cleft yang nggak pada tempatnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kurung dulu seluruh anak kalimat “What ...” sebelum ngecek kesesuaiannya. Jangan biarin kata benda di dalamnya ngatur kata kerjanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: What we needed was X — satu anak kalimat what, satu gagasan tunggal.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun kalimat penekanan dengan anak kalimat what sebagai subjek dan bagian yang ditonjolin sesudah bentuk be.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nyampur pola it-cleft sama pola anak kalimat what, atau nyocokin kata kerjanya sama kata benda jamak terdekat.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali anak kalimat what di awal sebagai satu kesatuan subjek → pilih bentuk tunggal → taruh bagian yang ditonjolin sesudah be

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Having reviewed shows that the review happened before the reopening.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner marks the earlier completed action with a broken form — a lone past participle, a bare verb after 'having', or a to + -ing hybrid — instead of the full 'having + past participle' pattern.
templates.reasoningOperation: confirm that the committee performed both actions -> place the review before the reopening -> encode the earlier active action with having + past participle
templates.stem: ___ the evidence twice, the committee reopened the investigation.

distractors.misconception: past participle alone
distractors.whyFails: Reviewed does not clearly mark the active prior action here.
distractors.whyFailsId: “reviewed” nggak nandain dengan jelas tindakan aktif yang lebih dulu di sini.
distractors.misconceptionId: past participle sendirian dipakai buat nandain tindakan yang lebih dulu.

distractors.misconception: bare verb
distractors.whyFails: 'Having review' pairs 'having' with a bare verb, so the perfect participle chain never gets completed.
distractors.whyFailsId: “having” digandeng kata kerja bentuk dasar, jadi rangkaian participle perfect-nya nggak pernah kebentuk.
distractors.misconceptionId: “having” digandeng kata kerja dasar jadi rangkaian participle-nya nggak kelar.

distractors.misconception: gerund mismatch
distractors.whyFails: To reviewing is not the required participle-clause form.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to reviewing” bukan bentuk anak kalimat participle yang dibutuhin di sini.
distractors.misconceptionId: campuran to + bentuk -ing dipakai di posisi anak kalimat participle.

explanation.whyCorrect: Having reviewed shows that the review happened before the reopening.
explanation.rule: Perfect participle clause: having + past participle indicates an earlier completed action.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Reviewed' suggests a passive relationship; 'having review' lacks the past participle; 'to reviewing' combines incompatible infinitive and gerund forms.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check both subject control and timeline: the understood subject of the participle clause must perform its action, and an earlier completed action takes having + past participle.
explanation.memoryCue: Earlier active action: having reviewed; earlier passive action: having been reviewed.
explanation.ruleId: Anak kalimat participle bentuk perfect: having + past participle nandain tindakan yang lebih dulu dan udah selesai.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Having reviewed” naruh peninjauannya sebelum “the committee reopened”, jadi urutan waktunya jelas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Reviewed” ngasih kesan hubungan pasif, dan “having review” kehilangan bentuk past participle-nya. “To reviewing” nyatuin bentuk to sama bentuk -ing yang nggak bisa disatuin.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dua hal: pelakunya dan urutan waktunya. Subjek tersirat di anak kalimat participle wajib ngelakuin tindakannya, dan tindakan yang lebih dulu selesai pakai having + past participle.
explanation.memoryCueId: Tindakan aktif yang lebih dulu: “having reviewed”. Tindakan pasif yang lebih dulu: “having been reviewed”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu pakai bentuk having + past participle buat nandain tindakan yang lebih dulu sebelum kalimat utamanya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nandain tindakan yang selesai lebih dulu pakai bentuk yang patah. Bisa past participle sendirian, kata kerja dasar sesudah “having”, atau campuran to + bentuk -ing. Pola having + past participle yang utuh malah nggak kerangkai.
templates.reasoningOperationId: pastiin komitenya ngelakuin kedua tindakan itu → taruh peninjauannya sebelum pembukaan kembali → tandai tindakan aktif yang lebih dulu pakai having + past participle

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Much as + clause expresses concession and takes a finite verb.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner completes the concessive clause after 'Much as' with a form that breaks it — a present-tense verb that clashes with the past frame, a dangling participle with no finite verb, or present 'has appeal', which clashes in both tense and collocation — instead of the finite past verb the clause needs.
templates.reasoningOperation: recognize 'much as' as a concessive linker -> require a finite clause after it -> align the verb with the completed past board decision
templates.stem: Much as the proposal ___ to several members at last month's meeting, the board rejected it on practical grounds.

distractors.misconception: present mismatch
distractors.whyFails: The marker 'at last month's meeting' fixes the evaluation in finished past time, so the present-tense 'appeals' clashes with it.
distractors.whyFailsId: frasa “at last month's meeting” maku penilaiannya di masa lampau, jadi bentuk present bentrok.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk present dipakai padahal frasa “at last month's meeting” maku penilaiannya di masa lampau.

distractors.misconception: participle fragment
distractors.whyFails: Appealing does not provide the finite clause required after much as.
distractors.whyFailsId: “appealing” nggak ngasih anak kalimat bertense yang diwajibin sesudah much as.
distractors.misconceptionId: penggalan participle dipakai di posisi yang minta kata kerja bertense.

distractors.misconception: present-tense clash plus unnatural collocation
distractors.whyFails: 'The proposal has appeal' is in fact a full clause, but its present-tense 'has' clashes with the past frame of 'at last month's meeting', and 'has appeal to several members' is not a natural collocation.
distractors.whyFailsId: “has appeal” memang klausa utuh, tapi present-nya bentrok bingkai lampau dan pasangan katanya nggak wajar.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk present yang bentrok sama bingkai lampau sekaligus pasangan katanya nggak wajar.

explanation.whyCorrect: Much as + clause expresses concession and takes a finite verb.
explanation.rule: Much as + subject + verb means although, despite the fact that.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Appeals' clashes with the past frame fixed by 'at last month's meeting'; 'appealing' leaves the concessive clause without a finite verb; 'has appeal' keeps a present verb against that same past frame and is not a natural collocation here.
explanation.howToAvoid: After 'much as', verify that you have a full subject-plus-finite-verb clause, then align its tense with the surrounding narrative.
explanation.memoryCue: Much as + subject + finite verb = although.
explanation.ruleId: Much as + subjek + kata kerja artinya walaupun, meskipun kenyataannya begitu.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Frasa “at last month's meeting” maku ceritanya di masa lampau, jadi “appealed” yang pas sesudah much as.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Appeals” bentrok sama bingkai lampau yang dipaku frasa “at last month's meeting”. “Appealing” ninggalin anak kalimatnya tanpa kata kerja bertense. “Has appeal” tetap present di bingkai lampau itu, dan bukan pasangan kata yang wajar di posisi ini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sesudah much as, pastiin ada anak kalimat utuh berisi subjek dan kata kerja bertense. Terus selarasin tense-nya sama alur cerita sekitarnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Much as + subjek + kata kerja bertense berarti walaupun.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kamu nyusun anak kalimat pertentangan pakai much as + subjek + kata kerja bertense.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngelengkapin anak kalimat pertentangan sesudah “Much as” pakai bentuk yang ngerusaknya. Bisa kata kerja present yang bentrok sama bingkai lampau, atau participle nggantung tanpa kata kerja bertense. Bisa juga “has appeal” yang bentrok tense sekaligus bukan pasangan kata yang wajar. Padahal anak kalimat itu butuh kata kerja lampau bertense.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali much as sebagai penghubung pertentangan → tuntut anak kalimat bertense sesudahnya → selarasin kata kerjanya sama keputusan dewan yang udah selesai

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Choose a, an, or the from the first sound and whether the listener already knows the noun.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner chooses an from spelling alone or uses the for a first, non-specific mention.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the noun sound and reference status -> select the article
templates.stem: This is Nadia. She is ___ engineer.

distractors.misconception: consonant-letter shortcut
distractors.whyFails: 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so 'a' is not the correct indefinite article.
distractors.whyFailsId: kata sesudahnya mulai dengan bunyi vokal.
distractors.misconceptionId: milih dari huruf, bukan dari bunyi.

distractors.misconception: specific-article overuse
distractors.whyFails: Nothing says the listener already knows which engineer; this is a first, non-specific mention.
distractors.whyFailsId: bikin kesan bendanya udah tertentu, padahal baru disebut.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata the dipakai buat penyebutan pertama.

distractors.misconception: plural-or-uncountable quantifier
distractors.whyFails: 'Engineer' is a singular countable noun, so 'some' cannot introduce it here.
distractors.whyFailsId: nggak dipakai buat satu benda tunggal.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata jumlah buat banyak benda dipakai ke benda tunggal.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'An' comes before the vowel sound in 'engineer'.
explanation.rule: Use a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound, and the when the noun is specific or already known.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'A' does not match the initial vowel sound; 'the' adds an unsupported specific reference; 'some' does not introduce one singular countable noun.
explanation.howToAvoid: Say the first sound aloud, then ask whether you mean one of many or a particular known item.
explanation.memoryCue: Listen to the sound: an engineer.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai a sebelum bunyi konsonan. Pakai an sebelum bunyi vokal. Pakai the kalau bendanya udah jelas yang mana.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Engineer” dibaca mulai bunyi vokal. Jadi pasangannya “an”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “A” nggak cocok sama bunyi vokal. “The” bikin kesannya udah tertentu. “Some” nggak buat satu benda.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Ucapin bunyi awalnya dulu. Baru tanya: bendanya udah jelas yang mana?
explanation.memoryCueId: Dengerin bunyinya: an engineer.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Milih a, an, atau the dari bunyi awal katanya. Cek juga bendanya udah tertentu atau belum.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang milih an dari huruf vokal (a, i, u, e, o). Padahal yang nentuin bunyi awalnya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: dengerin bunyi awal katanya → tentuin udah tertentu atau belum

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use have got or has got with the correct subject and form a basic possession question.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses have with a singular third-person subject or combines do with have got.
templates.reasoningOperation: match subject number to have or has -> keep got after the auxiliary
templates.stem: She ___ got a new phone.

distractors.misconception: plural-form transfer
distractors.whyFails: A singular third-person subject such as 'she' takes 'has got', not 'have got'.
distractors.whyFailsId: buat I, you, we, dan they, bukan “she”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk buat subjek jamak dipakai ke subjek tunggal.

distractors.misconception: be-verb substitution
distractors.whyFails: 'Is got' is not the possession structure tested here; the correct form is 'has got'.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk be, jadi is got nggak nyatain punya.
distractors.misconceptionId: be dipakai buat pola punya.

distractors.misconception: double-auxiliary construction
distractors.whyFails: 'Does got' is not grammatical; 'have got' forms its own possession pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: does got nggak pernah bener di bahasa Inggris.
distractors.misconceptionId: dua kata bantu ditumpuk.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'She' is singular third person, so the phrase is 'has got'.
explanation.rule: Use have got with I, you, we, and they; use has got with he, she, and it.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Have' does not agree with 'she'; 'is' and 'does' do not form the have-got possession structure.
explanation.howToAvoid: Choose have or has from the subject first, then keep got after it.
explanation.memoryCue: He, she, it has got; I, you, we, they have got.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai “have got” buat “I”, “you”, “we”, dan “they”. Pakai “has got” buat “he”, “she”, dan “it”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “She” sekelompok sama he dan it. Kelompok itu pakai “has got”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Have” nggak cocok sama “she”. “Is” dan “does” nggak bikin pola punya ini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tentuin have atau has dari subjeknya dulu. Baru taruh got.
explanation.memoryCueId: “He”, “she”, “it”: has got. “I”, “you”, “we”, “they”: have got.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Masangin have got dan has got sama subjeknya buat nunjukin punya
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang pakai satu bentuk buat semua subjek. Kadang have ketuker sama is atau does.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat subjeknya → pilih have atau has → got tetap di belakangnya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Form and use the past simple of regular verbs in affirmative and negative sentences.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner adds -ed after did or changes a consonant-plus-y verb to the wrong spelling.
templates.reasoningOperation: locate the past marker -> decide whether did already carries tense -> choose the base or -ed form
templates.stem: They ___ football yesterday.

distractors.misconception: missing-past-marking
distractors.whyFails: 'Play' is the bare present form and ignores the finished-time marker 'yesterday' entirely.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar sekarang, padahal “yesterday” nunjuk masa lalu.
distractors.misconceptionId: waktu lampau nggak ditandai.

distractors.misconception: third-person-present form
distractors.whyFails: 'Plays' is present simple for he, she, or it; 'they' and 'yesterday' require past simple.
distractors.whyFailsId: buat he, she, atau it di masa sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sekarang orang ketiga dipakai buat masa lalu.

distractors.misconception: progressive-form substitution
distractors.whyFails: 'Playing' needs an auxiliary such as 'were' and does not by itself mark a completed past event.
distractors.whyFailsId: butuh kata bantu kayak “were”, nggak bisa sendiri.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai tanpa kata bantu.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Yesterday' is a finished past-time marker, so the regular verb is 'played'.
explanation.rule: Regular past simple usually adds -ed; after did or did not, the main verb returns to its base form.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Play' omits the past marker; 'plays' is present third person; 'playing' is a participle without an auxiliary.
explanation.howToAvoid: Find the time word first. If did already appears, use the base form after did.
explanation.memoryCue: Yesterday: play becomes played; did + play, never did + played.
explanation.ruleId: Bentuk lampau beraturan biasanya nambah -ed. Sesudah did atau did not, kata kerjanya bentuk dasar.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Yesterday” bilang kejadiannya udah selesai. Kata kerjanya jadi “played”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Play” nggak nandain lampau. “Plays” buat he, she, it sekarang. “Playing” butuh kata bantu.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cari kata waktunya dulu. Kalau ada did, kata kerjanya balik ke bentuk dasar.
explanation.memoryCueId: Yesterday: play jadi played. Ingat did plus play.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bikin bentuk lampau beraturan pakai akhiran -ed. Sesudah did, kata kerjanya balik ke bentuk dasar.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang nandain lampau dua kali. Udah ada did, kata kerjanya masih dapat -ed.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari kata waktu lampaunya → cek ada did atau nggak

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Match was or were to the subject in a basic past-tense be sentence.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses was with a plural subject or adds did before was or were in a question.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify subject number -> match it to was or were -> place be before the subject in a question
templates.stem: They ___ at school yesterday.

distractors.misconception: singular-past transfer
distractors.whyFails: 'They' is plural, so the past form must be 'were', not 'was'.
distractors.whyFailsId: buat subjek tunggal, sedangkan “they” itu jamak.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lampau tunggal dipakai buat subjek jamak.

distractors.misconception: present-tense substitution
distractors.whyFails: 'Yesterday' requires a past form, while 'are' is present tense.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk sekarang, padahal “yesterday” nunjuk masa lalu.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sekarang dipakai buat masa lalu.

distractors.misconception: bare-infinitive substitution
distractors.whyFails: The finite past verb cannot be the bare form 'be'; choose 'were' for 'they'.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar, nggak bisa jadi kata kerja utama.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk dasar dipakai di posisi kata kerja utama.

explanation.whyCorrect: The plural subject 'they' takes 'were' in the past.
explanation.rule: Use was with I, he, she, and it; use were with you, we, and they.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Was' is singular, 'are' is present, and bare 'be' is not a finite past form.
explanation.howToAvoid: Say the subject-and-be pair aloud: I was, she was, you were, they were.
explanation.memoryCue: They were yesterday; she was yesterday.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai “was” buat “I”, “he”, “she”, dan “it”. Pakai “were” buat “you”, “we”, dan “they”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “They” itu jamak. Bentuk lampaunya “were”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Was” buat subjek tunggal. “Are” bentuk sekarang. “Be” bentuk dasar, nggak bisa sendiri.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sebut pasangannya dengan suara: I was, she was, they were.
explanation.memoryCueId: “They” pakai “were”. “She” pakai “was”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Milih was atau were sesuai subjeknya di kalimat lampau
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang pakai was buat semua subjek. Kadang malah kepakai bentuk sekarang are.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat subjeknya tunggal atau jamak → pilih was atau were

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Form common plural nouns with -s, -es, -ies, and irregular changes.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner applies one plural spelling rule to every noun.
templates.reasoningOperation: inspect the word ending -> apply the matching plural pattern -> check irregular forms
templates.stem: What is the plural of city?

distractors.misconception: simple-s-overgeneralization
distractors.whyFails: 'Citys' keeps the y unchanged after a consonant, a combination English spelling does not allow.
distractors.whyFailsId: huruf y dibiarin utuh sesudah konsonan.
distractors.misconceptionId: akhiran -s dipakai buat semua kata.

distractors.misconception: add-es-without-spelling-change
distractors.whyFails: The spelling must change from consonant + y to -ies, not 'cityes'.
distractors.whyFailsId: y sesudah konsonan harus berubah dulu.
distractors.misconceptionId: akhiran -es ditambah tanpa ngubah ejaan.

distractors.misconception: singular-retention
distractors.whyFails: The question asks for more than one city, so the singular form is incomplete.
distractors.whyFailsId: masih bentuk tunggal, padahal yang diminta lebih dari satu.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk tunggal dibiarin.

explanation.whyCorrect: Because 'city' ends in a consonant plus y, its plural is 'cities'.
explanation.rule: Many nouns take -s; nouns ending in s, x, ch, or sh often take -es; consonant + y changes to -ies.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Citys' and 'cityes' do not follow the consonant-plus-y spelling rule, while 'city' remains singular.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look at the final letters before adding a plural ending, then check common irregular nouns separately.
explanation.memoryCue: Consonant + y: change y to i, then add es.
explanation.ruleId: Banyak kata benda cukup nambah -s. Kata yang berakhiran s, x, ch, atau sh biasanya nambah -es. Konsonan plus y berubah jadi -ies.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “City” berakhiran konsonan lalu y. Bentuk jamaknya “cities”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Citys” dan “cityes” nggak ngikutin aturan konsonan plus y. “City” masih tunggal.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat huruf terakhirnya dulu. Kata yang nggak beraturan dihafal terpisah.
explanation.memoryCueId: Konsonan plus y: ganti y jadi i, baru tambah es.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bikin bentuk jamak kata benda, termasuk perubahan ejaan konsonan plus y
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang nambahin -s ke semua kata tanpa lihat huruf akhirnya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat huruf akhir katanya → pilih pola jamaknya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Choose in, on, or at for a container, surface, or specific place point.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner chooses a preposition from the object word without identifying the spatial relationship.
templates.reasoningOperation: classify the location as inside, on a surface, or at a point -> select the place preposition
templates.stem: The book is ___ the table.

distractors.misconception: container-reading
distractors.whyFails: The book rests on the table's surface; it is not inside the table.
distractors.whyFailsId: artinya di dalam meja, bukan nempel di permukaannya.
distractors.misconceptionId: letak di permukaan dibaca sebagai di dalam.

distractors.misconception: point-location-overuse
distractors.whyFails: 'At' marks a general point or meeting place, not the surface relationship shown here.
distractors.whyFailsId: nunjuk titik atau tempat ketemuan secara umum.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata at dipakai buat semua letak.

distractors.misconception: movement-preposition-substitution
distractors.whyFails: 'To' expresses movement toward a destination, but the sentence describes a stationary location.
distractors.whyFailsId: nunjuk gerakan ke tujuan, padahal bukunya diam.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata depan gerakan dipakai buat letak yang diam.

explanation.whyCorrect: Use 'on' when an object rests on a surface such as a table.
explanation.rule: Use in for an enclosed space, on for a surface, and at for a specific point or place.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'In' changes the relation to inside; 'at' is a point marker; 'to' signals movement rather than location.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask one question: is the object inside, touching a surface, or located at a point?
explanation.memoryCue: In a bag, on a table, at a bus stop.
explanation.ruleId: Pakai in buat di dalam ruang tertutup. Pakai on buat di atas permukaan. Pakai at buat satu titik tempat.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Bukunya nempel di permukaan meja. Buat permukaan pakai “on”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “In” bikin artinya di dalam meja. “At” nunjuk satu titik. “To” nunjuk gerakan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya satu hal: bendanya di dalam, di permukaan, atau di satu titik?
explanation.memoryCueId: In a bag, on a table, at a bus stop.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Milih in, on, atau at buat nunjukin letak benda
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang nerjemahin langsung dari kata “di”. Bahasa Indonesia cuma punya satu kata buat tiga-tiganya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: bayangin posisi bendanya → pilih kata depannya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Build present continuous with the correct form of be plus a verb ending in -ing.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner drops be, drops -ing, or uses present simple for an action happening now.
templates.reasoningOperation: detect the now-time cue -> choose the subject form of be -> add verb-ing
templates.stem: She ___ dinner right now.

distractors.misconception: bare-verb-without-auxiliary
distractors.whyFails: Present continuous needs a form of 'be' before the -ing verb; 'cook' alone is incomplete.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk dasar sendirian, kurang kata bantunya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja dasar dipakai tanpa kata bantu.

distractors.misconception: present-simple-habit
distractors.whyFails: 'Cooks' states a routine, but 'right now' points at this very moment, not a habit.
distractors.whyFailsId: nyatain kebiasaan, padahal “right now” nunjuk saat ini.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk kebiasaan dipakai buat kejadian saat ini.

distractors.misconception: missing-be-auxiliary
distractors.whyFails: The -ing form must be paired with 'is' for the subject 'she'.
distractors.whyFailsId: kurang kata bantu di depannya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata bantu be nggak dipasang.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Right now' points at this very moment, so the action in progress needs 'is cooking'.
explanation.rule: Present continuous = am/is/are + verb-ing for an action happening around the time of speaking.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Cook' and 'cooking' omit the required auxiliary; 'cooks' is present simple for a habit.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check both pieces: the correct be form for the subject and the -ing form of the main verb.
explanation.memoryCue: Now = be + -ing: she is cooking.
explanation.ruleId: Present continuous: am, is, atau are plus kata kerja -ing. Dipakai buat kejadian yang lagi berlangsung.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Right now” nunjuk saat ini juga. Jadi bentuknya “is cooking”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Cook” dan “cooking” kurang kata bantunya. “Cooks” buat kebiasaan, bukan saat ini.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dua bagian: bentuk be buat subjeknya, dan akhiran -ing.
explanation.memoryCueId: Lagi berlangsung: be plus -ing, kayak she is cooking.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bikin present continuous utuh: bentuk be yang cocok plus kata kerja -ing
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang nulis kata kerja -ing tanpa am, is, atau are. Bahasa Indonesia nggak butuh kata bantu itu.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temukan kata petunjuk “right now” → pasang dua bagiannya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Match common question words with the information requested: person, place, time, reason, or thing.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner chooses a question word from sentence position rather than the information needed.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the information type requested -> select the matching question word
templates.stem: ___ do you live?

distractors.misconception: thing-question substitution
distractors.whyFails: 'What' asks about a thing or activity, not the place where someone lives.
distractors.whyFailsId: nanya benda atau kegiatan, bukan tempat tinggal.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata tanya benda dipakai buat nanya tempat.

distractors.misconception: time-question substitution
distractors.whyFails: 'When' asks about time, while this question asks for a location.
distractors.whyFailsId: nanya waktu, bukan lokasi tinggalnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata tanya waktu dipakai buat nanya tempat.

distractors.misconception: reason-question substitution
distractors.whyFails: 'Why' asks for a reason, but the blank needs a place question word.
distractors.whyFailsId: nanya alasan, bukan lokasi tinggalnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata tanya alasan dipakai buat nanya tempat.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Where' asks for a place, so it completes 'Where do you live?'.
explanation.rule: Who asks about people, what about things, where about places, when about time, and why about reasons.
explanation.whyOthersFail: The other words request a thing, time, or reason rather than a place.
explanation.howToAvoid: Decide what information the answer should contain before choosing the question word.
explanation.memoryCue: Where = place; when = time; who = person.
explanation.ruleId: Who buat orang. What buat benda. Where buat tempat. When buat waktu. Why buat alasan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Jawaban buat kalimat ini nama tempat. Jadi kata tanyanya “Where”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: Kata tanya lain minta benda, waktu, atau alasan. Bukan tempat.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tentuin dulu isi jawabannya. Baru pilih kata tanyanya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Where buat tempat, when buat waktu, who buat orang.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Milih kata tanya sesuai jenis informasi yang dicari
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang milih kata tanya dari kebiasaan, bukan dari isi jawabannya.
templates.reasoningOperationId: bayangin jawabannya → pilih kata tanyanya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use some and any with basic countable and uncountable nouns in statements, questions, and negatives.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses some in a negative sentence or adds a plural ending to an uncountable noun.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify polarity and noun countability -> choose the quantifier and noun form
templates.stem: I don't have ___ money.

distractors.misconception: positive-quantifier-in-negative
distractors.whyFails: 'Some' asserts that an amount exists, which clashes with the negation in 'don't have'.
distractors.whyFailsId: bilang jumlahnya ada, padahal kalimatnya nyangkal.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata jumlah versi positif dipakai di kalimat negatif.

distractors.misconception: singular-article-with-uncountable
distractors.whyFails: 'Money' is uncountable here, so it does not take the singular article 'a'.
distractors.whyFailsId: cuma buat benda satuan, dan “money” bukan begitu.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata a dipasang ke benda yang nggak bisa dihitung.

distractors.misconception: countable-quantity-substitution
distractors.whyFails: 'Many' modifies plural countable nouns, while 'money' is uncountable.
distractors.whyFailsId: buat benda banyak yang bisa dihitung satu-satu.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata jumlah buat benda yang bisa dihitung dipakai ke yang nggak bisa.

explanation.whyCorrect: Negative sentences commonly use 'any' with an uncountable noun such as 'money'.
explanation.rule: Use some mainly in positive statements and any in negatives or questions; use many with plural countable nouns and much with uncountable nouns.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Some' is not the expected basic negative quantifier; 'a' and 'many' do not match uncountable 'money'.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check polarity first, then decide whether the noun can be counted one by one.
explanation.memoryCue: Negative + uncountable: I do not have any money.
explanation.ruleId: Some biasanya buat kalimat positif. Any buat kalimat negatif dan kalimat tanya. Many buat benda yang bisa dihitung, much buat yang nggak bisa.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Ada “don’t”, jadi kalimatnya negatif. “Money” juga nggak bisa dihitung satu-satu. Pasangan buat dua-duanya “any”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Some” maunya kalimat positif. “A” dan “many” cuma buat benda yang bisa dihitung.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek dua hal: kalimatnya nyangkal atau nggak? Bendanya bisa dihitung atau nggak?
explanation.memoryCueId: Negatif plus nggak bisa dihitung: I do not have any money.
