templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Milih some, any, many, atau much sesuai bentuk kalimat dan jenis bendanya
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang pakai some di kalimat negatif. Kadang many kepakai buat benda yang nggak bisa dihitung.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek kalimatnya positif atau negatif → cek bendanya bisa dihitung atau nggak

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Distinguish subject pronouns, object pronouns, possessive adjectives, and possessive pronouns in basic sentences.
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner uses me as a subject or confuses my with mine before or after a noun.
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the grammatical role and whether a noun follows -> select the matching pronoun form
templates.stem: ___ name is Sari.

distractors.misconception: subject-pronoun-before-noun
distractors.whyFails: 'She' is a subject pronoun; before the noun 'name', the possessive adjective 'her' is required.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk subjek, nggak bisa berdiri sebelum kata benda.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti subjek ditaruh sebelum kata benda.

distractors.misconception: stand-alone-possessive-before-noun
distractors.whyFails: 'Hers' stands alone and cannot directly modify the following noun 'name'.
distractors.whyFailsId: berdiri sendiri, nggak bisa nerangin kata benda sesudahnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: kepemilikan mandiri ditaruh sebelum kata benda.

distractors.misconception: object-pronoun-substitution
distractors.whyFails: 'Me' is an object pronoun and cannot show possession before 'name'.
distractors.whyFailsId: bentuk objek, nggak nyatain kepemilikan.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti objek dipakai buat kepemilikan.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Her' is a possessive adjective that comes before the noun 'name'.
explanation.rule: Use subject pronouns as subjects, object pronouns after verbs or prepositions, possessive adjectives before nouns, and possessive pronouns alone.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'She' is a subject, 'hers' is a stand-alone possessive, and 'me' is an object form.
explanation.howToAvoid: Look at the word after the blank. If a noun follows, choose a possessive adjective such as my, his, her, or their.
explanation.memoryCue: Her name, but the name is hers.
explanation.ruleId: Kata ganti subjek jadi subjek. Kata ganti objek berdiri sesudah kata kerja. Kata kepemilikan kayak her berdiri sebelum kata benda. Hers berdiri sendiri.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Sesudah bagian kosong ada kata benda “name”. Jadi pakai “Her”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “She” bentuk subjek. “Hers” berdiri sendiri. “Me” bentuk objek.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Cek posisinya: subjek, sesudah kata kerja, atau sebelum kata benda.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Her name”, tapi “the name is hers”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Bedain kata ganti subjek, kata ganti objek, dan dua bentuk kepemilikan
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu gampang ketuker antara her, hers, dan she. Bahasa Indonesia cuma punya satu kata “dia”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: lihat kata sesudah bagian kosongnya → tentuin bentuk kata gantinya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Give direct commands and instructions using the bare base form of the verb
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner dresses a command up like a statement, adding -s, -ing, or 'to' because Indonesian verbs never change shape and extra marking feels safer
templates.reasoningOperation: detect a sentence that tells the listener directly to act -> select the bare base form with no subject
templates.stem: The teacher walks in and says: “___ your books to page 40, everyone.”

distractors.misconception: adding -s as if the command needed subject-verb agreement with a singular subject
distractors.whyFails: An imperative speaks directly to 'you', so the verb never takes third-person -s; 'Opens your books' has no subject to agree with.
distractors.whyFailsId: perintah ngomong langsung ke “you”, jadi nggak ada subjek yang butuh akhiran -s.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambah -s seolah perintahnya harus nyocokin subjek tunggal.

distractors.misconception: using the -ing form on its own, which describes an activity instead of telling someone to act
distractors.whyFails: 'Opening your books' merely names an activity; nobody has actually been told to do anything yet.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Opening your books” cuma ngasih nama kegiatan, belum ada yang disuruh apa-apa.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk -ing dipakai sendirian, jadinya cuma nyebut kegiatan.

distractors.misconception: using a to-infinitive where a direct command is required
distractors.whyFails: 'To open your books' announces a purpose; it does not instruct the class to act right now.
distractors.whyFailsId: “To open” kesannya nyatain tujuan, bukan nyuruh kelas bertindak sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: pakai “to” + kata kerja buat perintah langsung.

explanation.whyCorrect: The teacher is telling the whole class to act right now, so the command starts with the bare verb: 'Open your books.'
explanation.rule: Imperatives use the base form of the verb alone: no subject, no -s, no -ing, and no 'to' in front.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Opens' adds third-person -s although a command has no stated subject; 'Opening' only names an activity without telling anyone to act; 'To open' expresses a purpose rather than an instruction.
explanation.howToAvoid: When a sentence tells someone directly to do something, start it with the bare verb and nothing else.
explanation.memoryCue: Commands come bare: 'Open', 'Sit', 'Listen'.
explanation.ruleId: Kalimat perintah pakai kata kerja bentuk dasar aja: tanpa subjek, tanpa -s, tanpa -ing, dan tanpa “to” di depan.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Gurunya lagi nyuruh seisi kelas buat buka buku sekarang, jadi perintahnya mulai dari bentuk dasar: “Open your books.”
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Opens” nambah -s padahal perintah nggak punya subjek; “Opening” cuma nyebut kegiatan tanpa nyuruh siapa-siapa; “To open” malah nyatain tujuan, bukan instruksi.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau kalimatnya nyuruh orang ngelakuin sesuatu, mulai dari kata kerja polos tanpa embel-embel.
explanation.memoryCueId: Perintah itu polosan: “Open”, “Sit”, “Listen”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Kasih perintah atau instruksi langsung pakai kata kerja bentuk dasar.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngedandanin kalimat perintah kayak kalimat berita: ditambah -s, -ing, atau “to”, padahal perintah mulai dari bentuk dasar polos.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali kalimat yang nyuruh langsung → pilih kata kerja bentuk dasar tanpa subjek

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Place adverbs of frequency in mid position before the main verb while keeping subject-verb agreement intact
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner drops the adverb after the verb or between verb and object, mirroring the Indonesian order 'minum selalu', or loses the third-person -s while juggling the adverb
templates.reasoningOperation: locate the frequency adverb and the main verb -> place the adverb before the verb that agrees with the subject
templates.stem: My sister ___ tea after dinner; she never skips it.

distractors.misconception: moves the adverb between the verb and its object, copying Indonesian word order
distractors.whyFails: English rejects an adverb of frequency between the verb and its object; 'drinks always tea' mirrors 'minum selalu teh', not English order.
distractors.whyFailsId: “drinks always tea” niru pola “minum selalu teh”, bukan urutan bahasa Inggris.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata frekuensinya diselipin antara kata kerja dan objek, niru urutan bahasa Indonesia.

distractors.misconception: leaving the bare verb with no third-person marking after a singular subject
distractors.whyFails: The subject 'my sister' is third-person singular, so the verb must be 'drinks'; the bare form drops obligatory agreement.
distractors.whyFailsId: subjeknya “my sister”, jadi kata kerjanya wajib “drinks” pakai -s.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja dasar dibiarin polos padahal subjeknya orang ketiga tunggal.

distractors.misconception: inserting 'is' before a main verb, blending the 'be' pattern with the present simple
distractors.whyFails: 'Is' cannot sit directly before the bare main verb 'drink'; the sentence needs one pattern, not a mix of two.
distractors.whyFailsId: “is” nggak bisa duduk langsung di depan kata kerja dasar “drink”; polanya jadi campur aduk.
distractors.misconceptionId: nyelipin “is” di depan kata kerja utama.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Always' sits in mid position before the main verb, and 'drinks' keeps the third-person -s: 'My sister always drinks tea.'
explanation.rule: Adverbs of frequency (always, usually, often, never) go before the main verb, and the verb still agrees with the subject.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Drinks always' pushes the adverb between verb and object, an order English rejects; 'always drink' loses the third-person -s; 'is always drink' mixes 'be' with a bare main verb.
explanation.howToAvoid: Slot the frequency word just before the main verb, then check the verb ending against the subject.
explanation.memoryCue: Frequency first, verb second: 'She always drinks'.
explanation.ruleId: Kata frekuensi (“always”, “usually”, “often”, “never”) duduk sebelum kata kerja utama, dan kata kerjanya tetap nyocokin subjek.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Always” duduk sebelum kata kerja utama, dan “drinks” tetap pakai -s buat orang ketiga tunggal: “My sister always drinks tea.”
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Drinks always” nyelipin kata frekuensi di antara kata kerja dan objek, urutan yang ditolak bahasa Inggris; “always drink” kehilangan -s; “is always drink” nyampur “be” sama kata kerja utama.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Selipkan kata frekuensi pas sebelum kata kerja utama, terus cek akhiran kata kerjanya ke subjek.
explanation.memoryCueId: Frekuensi dulu, kata kerja belakangan: “She always drinks”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Naruh kata keterangan frekuensi kayak “always” di posisi tengah, sebelum kata kerja utama.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh “always” sesudah kata kerja kayak urutan “minum selalu”, atau akhiran -s kata kerjanya malah hilang.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cari kata frekuensi dan kata kerja utamanya → taruh kata frekuensi sebelum kata kerja yang udah cocok sama subjek

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Mark ownership with apostrophe + s attached to the owner's name
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner shows possession by putting two nouns side by side as in 'tas Sinta', or writes a plural-looking -s without the apostrophe
templates.reasoningOperation: identify the owner and the thing owned -> attach 's to the owner's name and place it before the noun
templates.stem: Is this ___ bag? She was sitting here a minute ago.

distractors.misconception: drops the marker of ownership entirely, lining up two nouns as Indonesian does
distractors.whyFails: 'Sinta bag' lines up a name and a noun with nothing to signal ownership; English needs 's on the owner.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Sinta bag” nggak punya tanda kepemilikan apa pun; bahasa Inggris butuh apostrof + s.
distractors.misconceptionId: dua kata benda ditempel langsung kayak bahasa Indonesia.

distractors.misconception: writes a plain -s ending that superficially resembles the possessive but loses the apostrophe
distractors.whyFails: Without the apostrophe, 'Sintas' reads as a plural of Sinta rather than something that belongs to her.
distractors.whyFailsId: tanpa apostrof, “Sintas” kebaca kayak bentuk jamak, bukan punya Sinta.
distractors.misconceptionId: nulis -s polos tanpa apostrof.

distractors.misconception: inserting a duplicate owner pronoun after the name, marking possession twice
distractors.whyFails: 'Sinta her bag' stacks a name and a possessive word for the same owner; English marks possession only once.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Sinta her bag” nandain pemilik dua kali buat orang yang sama.
distractors.misconceptionId: nambahin kata ganti milik sesudah nama.

explanation.whyCorrect: Ownership is marked on the owner's name with apostrophe + s: 'Sinta's bag' means the bag belongs to Sinta.
explanation.rule: To say something belongs to a person, add 's to their name and put it before the thing: 'Sinta's bag'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Sinta bag' lines up two nouns with no ownership marker; 'Sintas' looks like a plural because the apostrophe is missing; 'Sinta her bag' marks possession twice.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask who owns it, add 's to that name, and drop any extra pronoun.
explanation.memoryCue: Owner + 's + thing: 'Sinta's bag'.
explanation.ruleId: Buat bilang sesuatu punya seseorang, tambahin apostrof + s ke namanya dan taruh sebelum barangnya: “Sinta's bag”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Tanda kepemilikan nempel di nama pemiliknya: “Sinta's bag” artinya tas itu punya Sinta.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Sinta bag” cuma nempelin dua kata benda tanpa tanda kepemilikan; “Sintas” kebaca jamak karena apostrofnya hilang; “Sinta her bag” nandain kepemilikan dua kali.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya siapa pemiliknya, tambahin apostrof + s ke nama itu, dan buang kata ganti tambahan.
explanation.memoryCueId: Pemilik + apostrof s + barang: “Sinta's bag”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Nandain kepemilikan pakai apostrof + s yang nempel di nama pemiliknya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nempelin dua kata benda langsung kayak “tas Sinta”, atau nulis -s tanpa apostrof.
templates.reasoningOperationId: tentuin siapa pemilik dan apa barangnya → tempelin apostrof + s ke nama pemilik, taruh sebelum barangnya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Make polite requests and orders with 'would like' plus a noun
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner answers a request situation with plain 'like' or squeezes the desire verb into -ing, because Indonesian 'mau' never changes shape
templates.reasoningOperation: detect a polite here-and-now request -> select 'would like' with a bare verb after 'would'
templates.stem: At the café counter, the barista asks what you want. You say: “I ___ a glass of orange juice, please.”

distractors.misconception: stating a general preference in casual flat form instead of the polite request formula
distractors.whyFails: 'I like a glass of orange juice' only reports a general taste; ordering something now takes 'would like'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “I like a glass of orange juice” cuma cerita selera; buat mesen sekarang butuh “would like”.
distractors.misconceptionId: selera umum ketuker sama permintaan sopan.

distractors.misconception: forcing a stative desire verb into the progressive to sound ongoing
distractors.whyFails: 'Want' is a stative verb that resists -ing in its ordinary sense, so 'am wanting' does not work for a simple order.
distractors.whyFailsId: “want” itu kata kerja statif yang nolak -ing di makna biasanya, jadi nggak cocok buat mesen.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja keinginan dipaksa jadi bentuk -ing.

distractors.misconception: gluing an -ing onto the verb after 'would', a blend of two separate patterns
distractors.whyFails: After 'would', the verb must stay in its base form; 'would liking' fits no English pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah “would” kata kerjanya wajib bentuk dasar; “would liking” nggak ada polanya.
distractors.misconceptionId: nempelin -ing sesudah “would”.

explanation.whyCorrect: Ordering politely uses 'would like': 'I would like a glass of orange juice, please.'
explanation.rule: 'Would like' + noun makes a polite request for something you want now; 'like' alone only states a general preference.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Like' states a general preference rather than ordering; 'am wanting' forces a stative verb into -ing; 'would liking' breaks the rule that 'would' takes the base form.
explanation.howToAvoid: When asking for something politely, reach for 'would like' and keep the verb after 'would' bare.
explanation.memoryCue: Polite orders: 'I would like ..., please.'
explanation.ruleId: “Would like” + kata benda dipakai buat minta sesuatu dengan sopan saat ini; “like” polos cuma nyatain selera umum.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Mesen dengan sopan pakai “would like”: “I would like a glass of orange juice, please.”
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Like” cuma cerita selera umum, bukan mesen; “am wanting” maksa kata kerja statif jadi -ing; “would liking” ngelanggar aturan bentuk dasar sesudah “would”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau minta sesuatu dengan sopan, pakai “would like” dan biarin kata kerja sesudah “would” tetap dasar.
explanation.memoryCueId: Pesenan sopan: “I would like ..., please.”

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Minta sesuatu dengan sopan pakai “would like” + kata benda.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu jawab situasi pesen-memesan pakai “like” polos atau maksa -ing, karena “mau” di bahasa Indonesia nggak pernah berubah bentuk.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali permintaan sopan di situasi sekarang → pilih “would like” dengan kata kerja dasar sesudah “would”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the -ing form after the preference verbs like, love, and hate
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner chains a bare verb straight after like/love/hate or glues 'to' and -ing together, copying Indonesian verb strings like 'benci bangun'
templates.reasoningOperation: spot a preference verb such as like, love, or hate -> select the -ing form for the activity that follows
templates.stem: My brother ___ up early on Sundays, so he never sets an alarm before the weekend.

distractors.misconception: following the feeling verb with a bare infinitive, chaining verbs directly as Indonesian does
distractors.whyFails: 'Hates get' chains two verbs with no connector, mirroring 'benci bangun'; after 'hates' the activity needs -ing.
distractors.whyFailsId: “hates get” niru pola “benci bangun”; sesudah “hates” kegiatannya butuh -ing.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja perasaan disambung kata kerja dasar langsung.

distractors.misconception: mixes the to-infinitive and the -ing ending into one broken shape
distractors.whyFails: 'To getting' welds two different patterns together and belongs to neither; pick 'to get' or 'getting', never both.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to getting” ngelas dua pola beda; pilih “to get” atau “getting”, jangan dua-duanya.
distractors.misconceptionId: “to” dan -ing dicampur jadi satu bentuk.

distractors.misconception: inserting 'is' before the feeling verb, a hybrid of the adjective pattern and a normal verb
distractors.whyFails: 'Hate' is a full main verb, so it takes no 'is' in front; 'is hate' crosses the adjective pattern with the verb pattern.
distractors.whyFailsId: “hate” itu kata kerja utama penuh, jadi nggak butuh “is” di depannya.
distractors.misconceptionId: nyelipin “is” di depan kata kerja perasaan.

explanation.whyCorrect: After preference verbs like 'hate', the following activity takes -ing: 'hates getting up early'.
explanation.rule: Like, love, hate, and enjoy are followed by verb + -ing when talking about activities in general.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Hates get' chains a bare verb straight after 'hates'; 'hates to getting' welds 'to' onto an -ing form; 'is hate getting' plants 'is' before a normal main verb.
explanation.howToAvoid: After like, love, or hate, turn the next activity into its -ing form.
explanation.memoryCue: Feelings feed on -ing: 'love swimming', 'hate waiting'.
explanation.ruleId: “Like”, “love”, “hate”, dan “enjoy” diikuti kata kerja + -ing kalau ngomongin kegiatan secara umum.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Sesudah kata kerja perasaan kayak “hates”, kegiatannya pakai -ing: “hates getting up early”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Hates get” nyambung kata kerja dasar langsung; “hates to getting” ngelas “to” ke bentuk -ing; “is hate getting” naruh “is” di depan kata kerja utama.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sesudah “like”, “love”, atau “hate”, ubah kegiatan berikutnya jadi bentuk -ing.
explanation.memoryCueId: Perasaan doyan -ing: “love swimming”, “hate waiting”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai bentuk -ing sesudah kata kerja perasaan “like”, “love”, dan “hate”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nyambung kata kerja dasar langsung sesudah “hate” kayak “benci bangun”, atau nempelin “to” dan -ing barengan.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin kata kerja perasaan → ubah kegiatan sesudahnya jadi bentuk -ing

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Ask and answer about life experience with the present perfect and ever/never
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner slots a finished-past or bare form after 'have', flattening the experience question into an ordinary past story
templates.reasoningOperation: spot the experience frame 'Have you ever' -> select the past participle after 'have'
templates.stem: “Have you ever ___ to Japan?” “No, never, but I really want to go.”

distractors.misconception: using the past-simple form inside a present perfect question frame
distractors.whyFails: 'Have you ever went' pairs 'have' with a finished-past form; the frame requires the participle 'been'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Have you ever went” masangin “have” sama bentuk lampau selesai; kerangkanya minta “been”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk past simple dimasukin ke kerangka present perfect.

distractors.misconception: leaving the bare verb although 'have' needs the past participle after it
distractors.whyFails: 'Have you ever be' leaves the verb unchanged; after 'have' the verb must appear as 'been'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Have you ever be” ninggalin kata kerjanya polos; sesudah “have” harus “been”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerja dibiarin dasar sesudah “have”.

distractors.misconception: mixes 'have' with a finite past form of 'be' instead of the participle
distractors.whyFails: 'Have you ever was' doubles up two finite forms; 'have' can only be followed by the participle 'been'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Have you ever was” numpuk dua bentuk berubah; “have” cuma bisa diikuti participle “been”.
distractors.misconceptionId: “have” dicampur sama bentuk lampau “was”.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Have you ever' asks about life experience, and after 'have' the verb must be the past participle: 'been'.
explanation.rule: The present perfect with 'ever' and 'never' talks about experience up to now: have/has + past participle.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Went' is a finished-past form that cannot follow 'have'; 'be' stays bare where a participle is needed; 'was' mixes a second finite past form into the perfect frame.
explanation.howToAvoid: After 'have' or 'has', always reach for the third form of the verb, never the past simple.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Ever' rides with 'have been', 'have seen', 'have done'.
explanation.ruleId: Present perfect dengan “ever” dan “never” ngomongin pengalaman sampai sekarang: “have/has” + past participle.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Have you ever” nanyain pengalaman hidup, dan sesudah “have” kata kerjanya wajib past participle: “been”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Went” itu bentuk lampau selesai yang nggak bisa ngikutin “have”; “be” masih polos padahal butuh participle; “was” nyelipin bentuk lampau kedua ke kerangka perfect.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sesudah “have” atau “has”, selalu ambil bentuk ketiga kata kerjanya, jangan past simple.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Ever” jalannya bareng “have been”, “have seen”, “have done”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Nanya dan jawab soal pengalaman hidup pakai present perfect plus “ever” atau “never”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu naruh bentuk lampau selesai atau bentuk dasar sesudah “have”, jadi pertanyaan pengalamannya berubah kayak cerita lampau biasa.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali kerangka “Have you ever” → pilih past participle sesudah “have”

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Describe unfinished states with the present perfect plus for and since
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reads a since-phrase as a plain present habit or as a closed past chapter, missing that the state runs from a past start point up to now
templates.reasoningOperation: find a since/for duration that is still true now -> select have/has + past participle
templates.stem: We ___ in this flat since 2019, and we still love it here.

distractors.misconception: using the plain present as a habit statement, ignoring the stretch of time that began in the past
distractors.whyFails: 'We live in this flat since 2019' treats the sentence as a bare habit; 'since 2019' demands a form that links past to present.
distractors.whyFailsId: “We live in this flat since 2019” anggep kalimatnya kebiasaan doang; “since 2019” minta bentuk penyambung masa lalu ke sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: present polos dipakai kayak kebiasaan, durasi dari dulunya keabaikan.

distractors.misconception: choosing the present progressive for right now, though the span from 2019 needs a past-to-present link
distractors.whyFails: 'Are living' only covers the current moment and cannot pair with 'since 2019', which reaches back into the past.
distractors.whyFailsId: “are living” cuma nutup momen sekarang dan nggak bisa gandeng “since 2019” yang nunjuk ke belakang.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lagi-berlangsung dipilih buat rentang yang narik dari 2019.

distractors.misconception: sealing the period off as a completed event, though the family still lives there
distractors.whyFails: 'Lived' closes the stay as finished, but 'we still love it here' says the family has not moved out.
distractors.whyFailsId: “lived” bikin tinggalnya kesan udahan, padahal “we still love it here” bilang mereka belum pindah.
distractors.misconceptionId: periodenya ditutup seolah udah kelar.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'Since 2019' plus 'we still love it' means the stay started in the past and continues, so 'have lived' fits.
explanation.rule: For a state that began in the past and is still true, use the present perfect with 'for' (length of time) or 'since' (starting point).
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Live' reports a bare habit and ignores the running duration; 'are living' cannot pair with 'since 2019'; 'lived' closes the stay as finished although the family is still there.
explanation.howToAvoid: See 'since' or 'for' with something still true? Link past to present with have/has + participle.
explanation.memoryCue: 'Since 2019' pulls the verb into 'have lived'.
explanation.ruleId: Buat keadaan yang mulai di masa lalu dan masih bener, pakai present perfect dengan “for” (lama waktu) atau “since” (titik mulai).
explanation.whyCorrectId: “Since 2019” plus “we still love it” artinya tinggalnya mulai dulu dan masih lanjut, jadi “have lived” yang pas.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Live” cuma laporan kebiasaan dan ngabaikan durasi yang lagi jalan; “are living” nggak bisa gandeng “since 2019”; “lived” nutup masa tinggalnya padahal keluarganya masih di situ.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Lihat “since” atau “for” dengan sesuatu yang masih bener? Sambungin masa lalu ke sekarang pakai “have/has” + participle.
explanation.memoryCueId: “Since 2019” narik kata kerjanya jadi “have lived”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Ceritain keadaan yang belum kelar pakai present perfect plus “for” dan “since”.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu baca frasa “since” kayak kebiasaan sekarang atau bab masa lalu yang udah ketutup, padahal keadaannya jalan dari dulu sampai sekarang.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin durasi “since/for” yang masih bener sekarang → pilih “have/has” + past participle

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Express wishes about the unreal present with wish + past simple
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner keeps the real-present tense after 'wish' or borrows 'would' and the past perfect from other unreal patterns
templates.reasoningOperation: identify a wish about the present situation -> shift the verb one step back to the past simple
templates.stem: I wish I ___ closer to the office; the commute eats two hours of my day.

distractors.misconception: keeping the present tense after 'wish', reading the situation as a real current fact
distractors.whyFails: 'I wish I live closer' keeps the verb in the real present, so the sentence loses its unreal, wishful meaning.
distractors.whyFailsId: “I wish I live closer” tetep di bentuk nyata, makna pengandaiannya hilang.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk sekarang dipertahanin sesudah “wish”.

distractors.misconception: inserting 'would' for the speaker's own situation, as if the sentence were a result clause
distractors.whyFails: 'Would' after 'wish' is reserved for other people's irritating behaviour or for result clauses; for your own state, use the past simple.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would” sesudah “wish” jatahnya keluhan soal orang lain atau klausa hasil; buat keadaan sendiri pakai past simple.
distractors.misconceptionId: “would” diselipin buat keadaan diri sendiri.

distractors.misconception: reaching two steps back with the past perfect, aiming the wish at a finished past moment
distractors.whyFails: 'Had lived' points the regret at a past that is over, but this wish is about the speaker's present commute.
distractors.whyFailsId: “had lived” ngarahin penyesalan ke masa lalu, padahal keluhannya soal perjalanan tiap hari yang sekarang.
distractors.misconceptionId: past perfect dipakai padahal harapannya soal sekarang.

explanation.whyCorrect: A wish about the present uses the past simple to mark unreality: 'I wish I lived closer.'
explanation.rule: Wish/if only + past simple expresses a present situation you would like to be different.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Live' keeps the real present and kills the unreal meaning; 'would live' belongs in result clauses or complaints about others; 'had lived' pushes the regret into the finished past.
explanation.howToAvoid: Wishing about now? Move the verb one step back, so the present becomes past simple.
explanation.memoryCue: Wish about now = one step back: 'wish I lived'.
explanation.ruleId: “Wish/if only” + past simple nyatain keadaan sekarang yang pengin kamu ubah.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Harapan soal sekarang pakai past simple buat nandain ketidaknyataan: “I wish I lived closer.”
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Live” ngejaga bentuk sekarang dan ngilangin makna pengandaian; “would live” jatahnya klausa hasil atau keluhan soal orang lain; “had lived” ndorong penyesalannya ke masa lalu yang udah kelar.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Berharap soal sekarang? Mundurin kata kerjanya satu langkah: bentuk sekarang jadi past simple.
explanation.memoryCueId: Harapan soal sekarang = mundur satu langkah: “wish I lived”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Nyatain harapan soal keadaan sekarang yang nggak nyata pakai “wish” + past simple.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngejaga bentuk sekarang sesudah “wish”, atau minjem “would” dan past perfect dari pola pengandaian lain.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali harapan soal situasi sekarang → mundurin kata kerjanya satu langkah ke past simple

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Voice regret about the finished past with if only + past perfect
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner stops at the past simple or drags 'would have' into the wish clause when regretting a completed past action
templates.reasoningOperation: identify regret about a completed past event -> select the past perfect inside the wish clause
templates.stem: If only I ___ the contract more carefully before signing it last year.

distractors.misconception: staying with the past simple, which cannot mark the unreal past that regret needs
distractors.whyFails: With 'last year' anchoring the event, plain 'read' reports rather than regrets; the unreal past needs 'had read'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “last year” udah ngunci kejadiannya; “read” polos jadi laporan, bukan penyesalan.
distractors.misconceptionId: past simple dipertahanin buat penyesalan lampau.

distractors.misconception: moving the 'would have' shape of the result clause into the wish clause itself
distractors.whyFails: 'Would have read' expresses an imagined result; inside the 'if only' clause itself the verb must be 'had read'.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would have read” nyatain hasil khayalan; di dalam klausa “if only” kata kerjanya harus “had read”.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk klausa hasil dipindah ke klausa harapan.

distractors.misconception: choosing the present perfect, which ties the missed reading to the present moment
distractors.whyFails: 'Have read' connects the action to now, but the signing closed that chapter last year; the regret looks further back.
distractors.whyFailsId: “have read” nyambungin kejadiannya ke sekarang, padahal babnya ketutup tahun lalu.
distractors.misconceptionId: present perfect dipilih buat kejadian yang udah ketutup.

explanation.whyCorrect: Regret about a finished past action takes the past perfect: 'If only I had read the contract.'
explanation.rule: Wish/if only + past perfect looks back at a past event you cannot change anymore.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Read' stays one step short and reads like a plain past report; 'would have read' belongs in the result clause of a third conditional; 'have read' ties the action to the present.
explanation.howToAvoid: Regretting something already over? Go two steps back: past perfect after 'if only'.
explanation.memoryCue: Past regret = 'if only I had ...'.
explanation.ruleId: “Wish/if only” + past perfect nengok ke kejadian lampau yang udah nggak bisa diubah.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Penyesalan soal kejadian lampau yang selesai pakai past perfect: “If only I had read the contract.”
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Read” kurang satu langkah dan kebaca kayak laporan lampau biasa; “would have read” jatahnya klausa hasil di pengandaian tipe tiga; “have read” ngiket kejadiannya ke sekarang.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Nyeselin sesuatu yang udah lewat? Mundur dua langkah: past perfect sesudah “if only”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Penyesalan lampau = “if only I had ...”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Nyatain penyesalan soal masa lalu yang udah kelar pakai “if only” + past perfect.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu berhenti di past simple atau narik “would have” ke dalam klausa harapan pas nyeselin kejadian lampau.
templates.reasoningOperationId: kenali penyesalan soal kejadian lampau yang selesai → pilih past perfect di dalam klausa harapannya

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use the future perfect epistemically for confident assumptions about what has already happened
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner treats 'will' as pure futurity, so an assumption about an already-completed event gets recast as a prediction still to come
templates.reasoningOperation: detect 'by now' anchoring an assumed completed event -> select will have + past participle for the epistemic reading
templates.stem: You ___ the news by now — the memo about the merger went to every department on Monday morning.

distractors.misconception: reading 'by now' as a point still ahead and choosing a plain prediction about the future
distractors.whyFails: The memo circulated days ago, so 'by now' demands an inference about a done deal, not a forecast of a coming event.
distractors.whyFailsId: memonya udah nyebar dari Senin; “by now” minta simpulan soal hal yang udah beres, bukan ramalan.
distractors.misconceptionId: “by now” dibaca kayak titik yang masih di depan.

distractors.misconception: forcing the verb into the present progressive although 'by now' asks for an accumulated result
distractors.whyFails: 'Are hearing the news by now' paints an unfolding scene, but the anchor 'by now' measures what has already accumulated.
distractors.whyFailsId: “are hearing the news by now” ngelukisin adegan berjalan, padahal “by now” ngukur hasil yang udah kekumpul.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk lagi-berlangsung dipaksa buat hasil yang udah numpuk.

distractors.misconception: picking the future continuous for an event the timeline treats as already delivered
distractors.whyFails: 'Will be hearing' projects the event forward as an activity, clashing with a timeline on which the news already landed.
distractors.whyFailsId: “will be hearing” ndorong kejadiannya jadi aktivitas ke depan, tabrakan sama garis waktu yang udah nganter kabarnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: future continuous dipilih buat kejadian yang udah lewat.

explanation.whyCorrect: 'By now' anchors the assumption to the present: 'will have heard' confidently asserts that the hearing has already taken place.
explanation.rule: Will have + past participle can express a confident assumption that something is already complete, especially with anchors like 'by now'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Will hear' points at a future event although the memo already circulated; 'are hearing' casts it as an ongoing scene; 'will be hearing' stretches it into future activity, clashing with 'by now'.
explanation.howToAvoid: When 'will' meets an anchor like 'by now', test whether the sentence is inferring a completed fact rather than forecasting one.
explanation.memoryCue: 'You'll have heard by now' = I'm sure it already reached you.
explanation.ruleId: “Will have” + past participle bisa nyatain dugaan yakin kalau sesuatu udah selesai, apalagi ada penanda kayak “by now”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: “By now” ngiket dugaannya ke saat ini: “will have heard” yakin banget kabar itu udah sampai.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Will hear” nunjuk kejadian masa depan padahal memonya udah nyebar; “are hearing” bikin adegannya kayak lagi berlangsung; “will be hearing” malah manjangin kejadiannya ke depan, tabrakan sama “by now”.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Pas “will” ketemu penanda kayak “by now”, cek dulu: ini nebak fakta yang udah selesai, atau ngeramal?
explanation.memoryCueId: “You'll have heard by now” = aku yakin kabarnya udah sampai.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai future perfect buat dugaan yakin soal sesuatu yang mestinya udah kejadian.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu anggep “will” murni soal masa depan, jadi dugaan soal kejadian yang udah selesai malah kebaca kayak ramalan yang belum terjadi.
templates.reasoningOperationId: deteksi “by now” yang nunjuk kejadian yang diduga udah selesai → pilih “will have” + past participle

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Mark anteriority in passive reporting structures with the perfect passive infinitive
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reports an earlier event with a present or active infinitive, losing both the time gap and the victim role of the subject
templates.reasoningOperation: check whether the reported event precedes the report and whether the subject receives the action -> select to have been + past participle
templates.stem: The painting is believed ___ from the gallery during the postwar chaos, decades before it resurfaced in Vienna.

distractors.misconception: using the simple passive shape, hiding that the theft was a prior event seen from the report
distractors.whyFails: 'To be stolen' makes the theft simultaneous with today's belief, but the sentence dates it decades earlier.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to be stolen” bikin pencuriannya sezaman sama keyakinan hari ini, padahal kalimatnya naruh kejadiannya puluhan tahun lebih awal.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk pasif sekarang dipakai buat kejadian lampau.

distractors.misconception: choosing the active infinitive, which would make the painting the one who stole
distractors.whyFails: 'To have stolen' casts the painting as the thief; the painting underwent the theft, so the infinitive must be passive.
distractors.whyFailsId: “to have stolen” bikin lukisannya jadi si pencuri; lukisannya kena pencurian, jadi bentuknya harus pasif.
distractors.misconceptionId: bentuk aktif dipilih, subjeknya jadi pelaku.

distractors.misconception: attaching a gerund where the reporting verb 'believe' takes the to-infinitive pattern
distractors.whyFails: 'Is believed having been stolen' breaks the complementation of 'believe', which requires a to-infinitive after the passive report.
distractors.whyFailsId: “is believed having been stolen” ngerusak pola “believe” yang sesudah laporan pasif minta to-infinitive.
distractors.misconceptionId: gerund ditempel padahal polanya minta to-infinitive.

explanation.whyCorrect: The theft happened decades before today's belief, and the painting was its target, so the perfect passive infinitive 'to have been stolen' carries both signals.
explanation.rule: After reporting verbs like 'is believed/said/thought', use 'to have been + past participle' for an earlier event that happened to the subject.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'To be stolen' erases the time gap between theft and report; 'to have stolen' makes the painting the thief; 'having been stolen' swaps in a gerund where 'believe' takes a to-infinitive.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask two questions: did it happen earlier, and did it happen to the subject? Yes and yes means 'to have been done'.
explanation.memoryCue: Earlier + passive = 'to have been stolen'.
explanation.ruleId: Sesudah kata pelaporan kayak “is believed/said/thought”, pakai “to have been” + past participle buat kejadian lebih awal yang menimpa subjeknya.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Pencuriannya kejadian puluhan tahun sebelum keyakinan hari ini, dan lukisannya jadi sasarannya, jadi “to have been stolen” bawa dua sinyal itu sekaligus.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “To be stolen” ngehapus jarak waktu antara pencurian dan laporan; “to have stolen” bikin lukisannya jadi pencurinya; “having been stolen” nuker pola “believe” yang minta to-infinitive.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya dua hal: kejadiannya lebih dulu? subjeknya yang kena? Dua-duanya iya berarti “to have been done”.
explanation.memoryCueId: Lebih dulu + pasif = “to have been stolen”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Nandain kejadian yang lebih dulu di struktur pelaporan pasif pakai perfect passive infinitive.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu laporin kejadian yang lebih dulu pakai bentuk sekarang atau bentuk aktif, jadi jarak waktunya dan peran korbannya sama-sama hilang.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek apakah kejadiannya lebih dulu dari laporannya dan apakah subjeknya kena tindakan → pilih “to have been” + past participle

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Keep the base-form subjunctive in that-clauses after demand, insist, and similar verbs
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner runs normal agreement or backshift inside the that-clause, because Indonesian complement clauses never change the verb's shape
templates.reasoningOperation: spot a demand or insist verb introducing a that-clause -> keep the embedded verb in the bare base form
templates.stem: The board formally demanded that the director ___ before the audit results were made public.

distractors.misconception: applying ordinary subject-verb agreement with a singular subject inside the demand clause
distractors.whyFails: The mandative clause suspends ordinary agreement, so 'the director resigns' is exactly the pattern 'demanded that' blocks.
distractors.whyFailsId: klausa tuntutan nangguhin kesesuaian biasa; “the director resigns” justru pola yang diblokir “demanded that”.
distractors.misconceptionId: kesesuaian subjek biasa dipaksain di klausa tuntutan.

distractors.misconception: backshifting the verb as ordinary reported speech instead of keeping the base subjunctive
distractors.whyFails: Backshift suits neutral reports; a demand freezes its embedded verb in the base form regardless of the past reporting verb.
distractors.whyFailsId: mundurin kata kerja cocoknya buat laporan netral; tuntutan ngunci bentuk dasar walau kata pelaporannya lampau.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata kerjanya dimundurin kayak laporan netral.

distractors.misconception: softening the demand with a conditional 'would', as if the clause reported a hypothetical
distractors.whyFails: 'Would resign' turns the demand into a mused possibility; the board issued an instruction, not a speculation.
distractors.whyFailsId: “would resign” ngubah tuntutannya jadi angan-angan; dewannya ngasih perintah, bukan spekulasi.
distractors.misconceptionId: tuntutan dilembutin pakai “would”.

explanation.whyCorrect: After 'demanded that', the embedded verb stays in the bare subjunctive regardless of subject or time: 'that the director resign'.
explanation.rule: Verbs of demand and proposal (demand, insist, suggest, require) take a that-clause with the base form: 'demand that she resign'.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'Resigns' applies ordinary third-person agreement that the mandative clause suspends; 'resigned' backshifts like neutral reported speech; 'would resign' softens the demand into a hypothetical.
explanation.howToAvoid: After demand/insist/suggest + that, freeze the verb in its dictionary form, whatever the subject and tense around it.
explanation.memoryCue: Demands strip the verb bare: 'demand that he resign'.
explanation.ruleId: Kata kerja tuntutan dan usulan (“demand”, “insist”, “suggest”, “require”) bawa klausa “that” dengan bentuk dasar: “demand that she resign”.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Sesudah “demanded that”, kata kerja di dalamnya tetap subjunctive dasar apa pun subjek dan waktunya: “that the director resign”.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “Resigns” nerapin kesesuaian orang ketiga yang justru ditangguhkan klausa tuntutan; “resigned” mundur kayak laporan netral; “would resign” ngelembutin tuntutannya jadi kemungkinan.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Sesudah “demand/insist/suggest” + “that”, bekuin kata kerjanya di bentuk kamus, apa pun subjek dan waktu di sekitarnya.
explanation.memoryCueId: Tuntutan nelanjangin kata kerja: “demand that he resign”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Ngejaga subjunctive bentuk dasar di klausa “that” sesudah “demand”, “insist”, dan kawan-kawannya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu nerapin kesesuaian subjek biasa atau mundurin kata kerjanya kayak laporan biasa, karena klausa pelengkap di bahasa Indonesia nggak pernah ngubah bentuk kata kerja.
templates.reasoningOperationId: temuin kata tuntutan yang buka klausa “that” → kunci kata kerja di dalamnya di bentuk dasar

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use sentential 'which' after a comma to comment on a whole preceding clause
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner reaches for 'what', 'that', or a fresh pronoun to refer back to a whole clause, mapping Indonesian 'yang' onto the wrong English word
templates.reasoningOperation: check what the relative points back to, a noun or the whole previous clause -> after a comma, select 'which' for a clause antecedent
templates.stem: The shipment arrived nine days late, ___ forced the plant to halt its assembly line.

distractors.misconception: using 'what' as a relative pronoun, though it cannot point back to an antecedent
distractors.whyFails: 'What' packages its own meaning ('the thing that') and cannot look back at the clause before the comma.
distractors.whyFailsId: “what” bawa maknanya sendiri, artinya “the thing that”, dan nggak bisa nengok ke belakang.
distractors.misconceptionId: “what” dipakai buat nunjuk balik ke klausa sebelumnya.

distractors.misconception: using 'that' to add extra detail after a comma, though it only opens essential clauses
distractors.whyFails: After a comma, a commenting clause refuses 'that'; only 'which' can carry a non-restrictive comment.
distractors.whyFailsId: sesudah koma, klausa komentar nolak “that”; cuma “which” yang boleh bawa komentar nonrestriktif.
distractors.misconceptionId: “that” dipakai sesudah koma buat komentar tambahan.

distractors.misconception: starting a fresh pronoun clause and splicing two sentences together in a non-standard join
distractors.whyFails: 'It forced the plant...' begins a second independent sentence, leaving two full clauses fused by a bare comma.
distractors.whyFailsId: “It forced the plant...” mulai kalimat merdeka kedua, jadi dua klausa utuh cuma dilem koma.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata ganti baru dipakai, dua kalimat ketempel koma.

explanation.whyCorrect: The delay itself, the whole first clause, is what forced the halt, and only 'which' can pick up a full clause after a comma.
explanation.rule: Sentential relative clauses use ', which' to comment on the entire preceding statement, not just a noun.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'What' cannot look back at an antecedent; 'that' never follows a comma in a non-restrictive clause; 'it' starts a second independent sentence and leaves a comma splice.
explanation.howToAvoid: If the comment is about the whole previous statement, put a comma and 'which'; nothing else fits that slot.
explanation.memoryCue: Comment on the whole thing? Comma + which.
explanation.ruleId: Klausa relatif sentensial pakai “, which” buat komentarin seluruh pernyataan sebelumnya, bukan cuma satu kata benda.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Yang maksa pabrik berhenti itu keterlambatannya, alias seluruh klausa pertama, dan cuma “which” yang bisa mungut klausa utuh sesudah koma.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “What” nggak bisa nengok ke anteseden; “that” nggak pernah ngikutin koma di klausa komentar; “it” malah buka kalimat kedua dan ninggalin dua kalimat ketempel koma.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Kalau komentarnya soal seluruh pernyataan sebelumnya, taruh koma plus “which”; nggak ada kata lain yang muat di slot itu.
explanation.memoryCueId: Komentarin semuanya? Koma + “which”.

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “which” sesudah koma buat komentarin satu klausa utuh sebelumnya.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu ngambil “what”, “that”, atau kata ganti baru buat nunjuk balik ke klausa utuh, karena semuanya kerasa kayak “yang”.
templates.reasoningOperationId: cek yang ditunjuk balik itu kata benda atau klausa utuh → sesudah koma, pilih “which” buat anteseden klausa

templates.pedagogicalObjective: Use generic 'the' with a singular noun for statements about a species or class as a whole
templates.misconceptionTargeted: Learner picks an article or determiner that quantifies individual animals, although extinction is a property of the class itself
templates.reasoningOperation: test whether the predicate applies to individuals or to the class as one unit -> select generic 'the' for class-level statements
templates.stem: ___ Sumatran tiger is now on the brink of extinction, with fewer than four hundred individuals left in the wild.

distractors.misconception: using the indefinite article for a claim about the whole species, which only fits one-member-at-a-time statements
distractors.whyFails: 'A Sumatran tiger' introduces one unspecified animal, but no single animal can be 'on the brink of extinction'; only the species can.
distractors.whyFailsId: “A Sumatran tiger” ngenalin satu ekor nggak jelas, padahal satu ekor nggak bisa dibilang nyaris punah.
distractors.misconceptionId: artikel tak tentu dipakai buat klaim soal spesies utuh.

distractors.misconception: spreading the claim over each countable member, though dying out can only be true of the class
distractors.whyFails: 'Every Sumatran tiger' distributes the predicate to each animal one by one, yet extinction cannot be true of individuals.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Every Sumatran tiger” bagi-bagi predikatnya per ekor, padahal kepunahan cuma bener buat kelasnya.
distractors.misconceptionId: klaimnya disebar ke tiap ekor satu-satu.

distractors.misconception: picking the free-choice quantifier, which selects random members rather than naming the species
distractors.whyFails: 'Any Sumatran tiger' invites you to pick an arbitrary animal, while the sentence makes a claim about the species as a unit.
distractors.whyFailsId: “Any Sumatran tiger” nyuruh milih ekor sembarang, padahal kalimatnya ngeklaim spesiesnya sebagai unit.
distractors.misconceptionId: kata pemilih bebas dipakai, anggotanya jadi acak.

explanation.whyCorrect: Being on the brink of extinction is true of the species as a single unit, and generic 'the' + singular noun names exactly that class.
explanation.rule: 'The' + singular countable noun can denote a whole species or class, and is required when the predicate (die out, be extinct, evolve) holds only at class level.
explanation.whyOthersFail: 'A' fits one-member-at-a-time properties, not class-level facts; 'Every' distributes the claim over each animal, which extinction cannot do; 'Any' picks random members instead of naming the species.
explanation.howToAvoid: Ask whether one single animal could make the sentence true; if only the whole class can, reach for generic 'the'.
explanation.memoryCue: Species talk wears 'the': 'The tiger is endangered.'
explanation.ruleId: “The” + kata benda tunggal bisa nunjuk satu spesies utuh, dan wajib dipakai kalau predikatnya (punah, berevolusi) cuma bener di level kelas.
explanation.whyCorrectId: Nyaris punah itu bener buat spesiesnya sebagai satu unit, dan “the” generik + kata benda tunggal persis namain kelas itu.
explanation.whyOthersFailId: “A” cocoknya buat sifat satu-ekor-satu-waktu, bukan fakta level kelas; “Every” nyebarin klaim ke tiap ekor, padahal kepunahan nggak bisa gitu; “Any” mungut anggota acak, bukan namain spesiesnya.
explanation.howToAvoidId: Tanya: satu ekor doang bisa bikin kalimatnya bener nggak? Kalau cuma kelas utuh yang bisa, ambil “the” generik.
explanation.memoryCueId: Ngomongin spesies pakai “the”: “The tiger is endangered.”

templates.pedagogicalObjectiveId: Pakai “the” generik dengan kata benda tunggal buat pernyataan soal spesies atau kelas secara utuh.
templates.misconceptionTargetedId: Kamu milih artikel atau penentu yang ngitung ekor per ekor, padahal kepunahan itu sifat kelasnya sendiri.
templates.reasoningOperationId: uji predikatnya berlaku buat individu atau buat kelas sebagai satu unit → pilih “the” generik buat pernyataan level kelas
